title: LanceDB raises $57.5M to accelerate AI model training with multimodal data platform
title_en: LanceDB raises $57.5M to accelerate AI model training with multimodal data platform
author: Kyt Dotson
article_content:
LanceDB Inc., the developer of database technology designed to speed up artificial intelligence models, today announced it has raised $57.5 million in early-stage funding to bring a multimodal lakehouse to researchers, model builders and platform teams.

Bessemer Venture Partners and Innovation Endeavors led the Series B round. Other investors in the round included Theory Ventures, Dimension, Swift Ventures, CRV and Y Combinator, bringing the company’s total funding to $98.5 million.

AI is making it easier to create and interpret increasingly complex forms of data, but creating it also brings an infrastructure problem. LanceDB is tackling this problem by providing a unified multimodal data lakehouse, giving researchers, enterprise outfits and AI agents a unified way to access, find, prepare and train on that data without spending weeks managing the underlying infrastructure.

“Typically, research teams have to put different parts of their dataset in different places, and they lose weeks or months getting a whole training dataset ready for that single training run at the end of the day,” co-founder and Chief Executive Chang She told SiliconANGLE in an interview. “There’s a missing data layer for AI today, and that’s what we’re trying to build.”

LanceDB’s technology is built on Lance, an open-source data format designed for AI workloads that combines structured information with images, video and other large files. Unlike traditional analytics formats optimized for processing entire tables, Lance supports the rapid retrieval and modification of individual records, making it particularly useful for searching and preparing massive training datasets.

The company built this format into a large-scale data lakehouse for retrieval, which is needed for the sheer scale of information needed to train modern AI models. A lakehouse combines the flexibility of a data lake, which can store enormous amounts of raw information, with database-style capabilities for organizing, querying and managing that data.

“Part of what makes multimodal data different and more difficult is the size of the data,” She explained.

By bringing multimodality to the lakehouse format, LanceDB brings different forms of AI training data into a single platform, allowing developers to search, organize and prepare their datasets without maintaining separate systems for each data type. It can connect directly to customers’ existing cloud storage, where the data remains, while distributing computational workloads across the infrastructure required to process it.

### The challenge of multimodal data for AI

Multimodal AI involves more than combining text, audio, images and video. Autonomous vehicles, robotics and world models also involve three-dimensional sensor information, geospatial coordinates, time-series data and annotations that explain what the sensors are detecting.

For example, a self-driving car doesn’t merely capture an image. Its sensors might produce a three-dimensional representation of the surrounding environment, which then needs to be associated with information that identifies roads, pedestrians, vegetation and other objects.

The sheer amount of data included in lidar 3D clouds, images, video, audio and more can take up, on average, 10 to 20 petabytes of data in a single table for many large training workflows, with some becoming even larger – potentially approaching 80 to 100 petabytes. Researchers and model builders may maintain huge pools of data across different systems because conventional platforms weren’t designed around the requirements of multimodal AI.

Researchers must then assemble, reconcile and store different components of a training dataset to enrich it for training. The curation itself can take weeks or months just to move, prepare and process. LanceDB’s answer is to manage the infrastructure itself without ever copying or moving data from enterprise or research storage, giving it a single unified access point.

“The data stays in place,” She explained. “It remains yours. We don’t need to copy it.”

In short, LanceDB isn’t simply introducing a new way to store data; the objective is to provide a way to access the data less often, without needing to copy, convert or move it through network infrastructure. This greatly speeds up what She refers to as the “AI flywheel,” which is currently driven by feeding AI models good data as quickly as possible to mint and roll them out.

“The faster we can make that spin, the faster research teams can get to higher quality models and allow us to make even more interesting AI applications,” She said.

Notable customers include Runway AI Inc., which adopted LanceDB’s enterprise platform as its AI training needs expanded. Netflix Inc. built a media data lake on the technology for content creation. And Microsoft Corp. uses the platform as a data layer for training models on tens of billions of rows of image and code data. The platform lets these organizations consolidate data management, search, curation and feature engineering into a unified workflow, helping researchers prepare training datasets at petabyte scale without juggling separate infrastructure systems.

“A training example at Runway doesn’t stay still,” said Runway Chief Technology Officer Kamil Sindi. “It starts as a video and a prompt, then we add embeddings, resolution and duration metadata, whatever the next experiment needs. We first started using the Lance format in 2024 because it was the only option that handled unstructured data, column appends, distributed reads and ad-hoc SQL all at once. We’ve since become a LanceDB Enterprise customer.”

She said LanceDB intends to use the new funding to expand its multimodal data platform and accelerate the AI model development cycle, particularly by improving large-scale data curation, feature engineering and data loading to keep thousands of graphics processing units supplied efficiently during training. The company will also deepen its support for emerging AI workloads, including video generation, world models and robotics, where researchers must manage growing volumes of first-person sensor data, synthetic data and other multimodal information.

article_content_zh:
LanceDB Inc. 是一家旨在加速人工智能模型速度的数据库技术开发商，今天宣布已筹集 5750 万美元的早期资金，为研究人员、模型构建者和平台团队提供多模式湖屋。

Bessemer Venture Partners 和 Innovation Endeavors 领投了 B 轮融资。此轮融资的其他投资者包括 Theory Ventures、Dimension、Swift Ventures、CRV 和 Y Combinator，使该公司的融资总额达到 9850 万美元。

人工智能使创建和解释日益复杂的数据变得更加容易，但创建它也带来了基础设施问题。 LanceDB 正在通过提供统一的多模式数据湖库来解决这个问题，为研究人员、企业机构和人工智能代理提供一种统一的方式来访问、查找、准备和训练这些数据，而无需花费数周时间来管理底层基础设施。

联合创始人兼首席执行官张佘在接受 SiliconANGLE 采访时表示：“通常情况下，研究团队必须将数据集的不同部分放在不同的地方，他们需要花费数周或数月的时间才能为一天结束时的单次训练准备好整个训练数据集。” “当今的人工智能缺少一个数据层，而这正是我们正在努力构建的。”

LanceDB 的技术建立在 Lance 的基础上，Lance 是一种专为人工智能工作负载而设计的开源数据格式，它将结构化信息与图像、视频和其他大型文件相结合。与针对处理整个表而优化的传统分析格式不同，Lance 支持快速检索和修改单个记录，这使其对于搜索和准备大量训练数据集特别有用。

该公司将这种格式构建到一个用于检索的大型数据湖库中，这是训练现代人工智能模型所需的庞大信息所必需的。 Lakehouse 结合了数据湖的灵活性（可以存储大量原始信息）和用于组织、查询和管理数据的数据库式功能。

“多模式数据之所以不同且更加困难的部分原因在于数据的大小，”她解释道。

通过将多模态引入 Lakehouse 格式，LanceDB 将不同形式的 AI 训练数据引入单一平台，使开发人员能够搜索、组织和准备其数据集，而无需为每种数据类型维护单独的系统。它可以直接连接到客户现有的云存储（数据保留在其中），同时在处理数据所需的基础设施之间分配计算工作负载。

### 多模态数据对人工智能的挑战

多模态人工智能不仅仅涉及文本、音频、图像和视频的结合。自动驾驶车辆、机器人和世界模型还涉及三维传感器信息、地理空间坐标、时间序列数据和解释传感器检测内容的注释。

例如，自动驾驶汽车不仅仅是捕捉图像。它的传感器可能会产生周围环境的三维表示，然后需要将其与识别道路、行人、植被和其他物体的信息相关联。

对于许多大型训练工作流程，激光雷达 3D 云、图像、视频、音频等中包含的数据量平均会在单个表中占用 10 到 20 PB 的数据，有些数据甚至更大，可能接近 80 到 100 PB。研究人员和模型构建者可能会在不同系统中维护大量数据，因为传统平台并不是围绕多模式人工智能的要求而设计的。

然后，研究人员必须组装、协调和存储训练数据集的不同组成部分，以丰富训练数据集。策划本身可能需要数周或数月的时间来移动、准备和处理。 LanceDB 的答案是管理基础设施本身，无需从企业或研究存储中复制或移动数据，从而为其提供单一的统一访问点。

“数据保持不变，”她解释道。 “它仍然是你的。我们不需要复制它。”

简而言之，LanceDB 不仅仅是引入一种新的数据存储方式；目标是提供一种减少访问数据的方法，无需通过网络基础设施复制、转换或移动数据。这大大加快了她所说的“人工智能飞轮”的速度，目前该飞轮是通过尽快向人工智能模型提供良好的数据来铸造和推出它们来驱动的。

她说：“我们的旋转速度越快，研究团队就能越快地获得更高质量的模型，并让我们能够开发出更有趣的人工智能应用程序。”

著名客户包括 Runway AI Inc.，该公司随着人工智能培训需求的扩大而采用了 LanceDB 的企业平台。 Netflix Inc. 基于内容创建技术构建了媒体数据湖。微软公司使用该平台作为数据层，在数百亿行图像和代码数据上训练模型。该平台使这些组织能够将数据管理、搜索、管理和特征工程整合到一个统一的工作流程中，帮助研究人员准备 PB 级的训练数据集，而无需处理单独的基础设施系统。

“Runway 的训练示例不会保持静止，”Runway 首席技术官卡米尔·辛迪 (Kamil Sindi) 说道。 “它从视频和提示开始，然后我们添加嵌入、分辨率和持续时间元数据，无论下一个实验需要什么。我们于 2024 年首次开始使用 Lance 格式，因为它是同时处理非结构化数据、列追加、分布式读取和即席 SQL 的唯一选项。从那时起，我们就成为了 LanceDB Enterprise 客户。”

她表示，LanceDB 打算利用新资金扩展其多模式数据平台并加快人工智能模型开发周期，特别是通过改进大规模数据管理、特征工程和数据加载，以保持数千个图形处理单元在训练期间高效运行。该公司还将加深对新兴人工智能工作负载的支持，包括视频生成、世界模型和机器人技术，研究人员必须管理不断增长的第一人称传感器数据、合成数据和其他多模式信息。

Investing.com -- Nvidia (NASDAQ: NVDA) is facing another layer of scrutiny as short seller Muddy Waters disclosed a short position in the chipmaker, raising questions about a possible connection between former Nvidia executive Ajay K. Puri and former Super Micro Computer (NASDAQ: SMCI) Chief Growth Officer Cenly Chen.

The disclosure comes amid a turbulent period for Nvidia, following Jensen Huang's abrupt resignation as CEO on November 12 and growing congressional scrutiny of the company's exposure to alleged Chinese chip-diversion schemes. Huang has agreed to answer questions from three House committees on December 1, with Nvidia General Counsel Tim Teter scheduled to appear the following day.

In a post on X, Muddy Waters questioned whether a woman identified as Cenly Chen, and in some photograph tags as Cenly Puri, who has reportedly been photographed publicly with Puri between 2024 and 2026, is the same Cenly Chen formerly employed by Super Micro.

Puri was previously Nvidia's EVP of Worldwide Field Operations and was among the company's most senior executives before leaving the position in June 2026. He continues to serve in a senior advisory role to Nvidia, according to Muddy Waters.

The short seller draws attention to an October 2026 consolidated class action complaint against Super Micro, which alleges that its former Chief Growth Officer Cenly Chen managed the company's acquisition of Nvidia GPUs and determined how they were distributed among customers. The complaint further alleges that Chen could not have been unaware of Super Micro's alleged illicit sales.

The allegations relate to a separate U.S. criminal case announced in March, involving three individuals associated with Super Micro who were indicted over an alleged scheme to sell approximately $2.5 billion of Nvidia-powered servers to end customers in China through a Southeast Asian front company.

Muddy Waters acknowledges that neither Cenly Chen nor Puri has been accused of criminal conduct by the government and that the allegations in the shareholder lawsuit remain unproven.

The short seller's central question is whether the woman photographed with Puri is the same individual named in the Super Micro litigation. That identification, as well as any potential implications for Nvidia, has not been independently established.

title: Rubio says there's "zero evidence" recent tech outages are related
title_en: Rubio says there's "zero evidence" recent tech outages are related
author: Kiki Intarasuwan
article_content:
Secretary of State Marco Rubio said there's "zero evidence" that recent tech outages in U.S. air travel, banking and other systems are connected.

"The Microsoft incident has nothing to do with what we saw with the FAA. The FAA has nothing to do with what we saw with the banks a few days ago. These issues that we've seen from a technical standpoint are completely unrelated one from another," Rubio said Wednesday morning local time during a news conference in the Philippines.

Rubio acknowledged that people are fearful and uncertain, saying he wanted to be clear that the United States is not under systemic attack.

"We have zero evidence or any reason to believe that any of these isolated or individual instances have anything to do with nefarious actors, with cyber hackers, with criminals, with another nation state, with a malign actor of any kind," Rubio said.

Rubio, who is traveling with President Trump ahead of a trilateral meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping this week, added that the administration is "always on the lookout" for any potential attacks and reiterated multiple times that reports of technical issues are not interconnected.

"Each of them are distinct, and they're different in their causation," he said.

On Thursday, Microsoft said it experienced a worldwide outage affecting services like Outlook and Teams, impacting users, companies and government operations worldwide. The company said the outage was linked to a technical issue, not malicious or cyber activity.

The following day, the Federal Aviation Administration issued a nationwide ground stop on all departing U.S. flights for several hours, throwing the aviation industry into turmoil. Federal officials identified a contractor performing maintenance updates as the cause of Friday's disruption, but key questions remain about the underlying cause of the systemwide failure.

Other recent outages that have since been resolved include disruptions to major banks like JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America and U.S. Bank, and issues with Apple's services. On Tuesday, the National Security Agency's internal network used to store and share classified information went offline, multiple U.S. officials familiar told CBS News.

Democratic Sen. Mark Warner, vice chair of the Senate Intelligence Committee, also said on Tuesday that there's no indication these incidents are the result of an attack, but noted that artificial intelligence is creating pressure for companies to deal with vulnerabilities.

"AI is making it possible to identify vulnerabilities across enormous numbers of systems at unprecedented speed, creating enormous pressure on companies and government agencies to patch those vulnerabilities immediately, often all at once, putting tremendous strain on systems that weren't built to handle that pace of change," Warner said in a post on X. "It feels like every day brings another reminder that AI is moving faster than our ability to manage its consequences. This is exactly why I've been pushing for commonsense guardrails on AI and stronger cybersecurity protections."

When asked Wednesday about the role of AI in recent incidents, Rubio said he didn't want to speculate because every incident is unique and referred to individual companies.

title_zh: 卢比奥否认近期美技术宕机系系统性攻击
summary_zh: 美国国务卿马可·卢比奥明确指出，近期民航、银行及微软等领域的技术中断事件互无关联，非网络攻击所致
article_content_zh:
美国国务卿卢比奥表示，“没有证据”表明美国航空旅行、银行和其他系统最近发生的技术中断之间存在关联。

卢比奥当地时间周三上午在菲律宾举行的新闻发布会上表示：“微软事件与我们在美国联邦航空局看到的情况无关。美国联邦航空局与我们几天前在银行看到的情况无关。我们从技术角度看到的这些问题完全无关。”

卢比奥承认人们感到恐惧和不确定，并表示他想明确美国并未受到系统性攻击。

卢比奥说：“我们没有任何证据或任何理由相信这些孤立或个别的事件与邪恶行为者、网络黑客、犯罪分子、另一个民族国家、任何类型的恶意行为者有任何关系。”

卢比奥在本周与俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京和中国国家主席习近平举行三边会议之前与特朗普总统一起旅行，他补充说，政府“始终在警惕”任何潜在的攻击，并多次重申，技术问题的报告并不相互关联。

“它们每个都是独特的，而且它们的因果关系也不同，”他说。

周四，微软表示，它经历了全球范围内的中断，影响了 Outlook 和 Teams 等服务，影响了全球用户、公司和政府运营。该公司表示，此次中断与技术问题有关，而不是恶意或网络活动。

次日，美国联邦航空管理局下令在全国范围内对所有出发的美国航班进行数小时的地面停飞，令航空业陷入混乱。联邦官员确定，周五中断的原因是一名执行维护更新的承包商，但关于整个系统故障的根本原因仍然存在关键问题。

最近已解决的其他中断包括摩根大通、美国银行和合众银行等主要银行的中断，以及苹果服务的问题。多位熟悉情况的美国官员告诉哥伦比亚广播公司新闻，周二，国家安全局用于存储和共享机密信息的内部网络离线。

参议院情报委员会副主席、民主党参议员马克·沃纳 (Mark Warner) 周二也表示，没有迹象表明这些事件是攻击造成的，但他指出，人工智能正在给公司带来处理漏洞的压力。

华纳在 X 上的一篇帖子中表示：“人工智能使得以前所未有的速度识别大量系统中的漏洞成为可能，这给公司和政府机构带来了巨大的压力，要求他们立即修补这些漏洞，通常是一次性修补这些漏洞，这给那些无法应对这种变化速度的系统带来了巨大的压力。”“感觉每一天都在提醒我们，人工智能的发展速度超过了我们管理其后果的能力。这正是我一直在推动人工智能常识护栏和更强大的网络安全保护的原因。”

当周三被问及人工智能在最近发生的事件中所扮演的角色时，卢比奥表示，他不想猜测，因为每起事件都是独一无二的，并且都涉及个别公司。

title: Exclusive: Some Nvidia directors continue push to bring Huang back
title_en: Exclusive: Some Nvidia directors continue push to bring Huang back
author: Reed Albergotti and Rohan Goswami
article_content:
Despite Nvidia’s proclamation Tuesday that it didn’t plan to bring ousted CEO Jensen Huang back to the chipmaker, a faction of board members is pushing for his return, according to people familiar with the matter.

Huang has met with a number of tech executives and spoken with at least one board member about the possibility of his return, the people said.

The conversation with the director took place before the company’s earnings report and before Huang issued a public statement Tuesday that he’d be willing to return to the company if the board decides it is in the “best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America.”

Hours later, Nvidia chairman Harvey Jones said on the company’s earnings call that the chipmaker wasn’t considering bringing Huang back and that the board had voted unanimously to accept his resignation.

Spokespeople for Huang and Nvidia declined to comment.

Despite the pushback from three directors, other board members are starting to narrow the search for Huang’s replacement, some of the people familiar with the deliberations said.

ARM CEO Rene Haas and Marvell CEO Matt Murphy have both been considered, the people said. Haas has spoken to at least some Nvidia directors about taking the job, one of the people said, but he’s said he’s concerned about the optics of taking it over calls to bring Huang back to the helm.

Spokespeople for ARM and Marvell didn’t immediately respond to requests for comment. It’s also unclear whether Marvell’s Murphy would be able to take over as Nvidia’s CEO given the company is navigating a mega-merger with rival Lumentum.

title_zh: 英伟达董事会内部分化：部分成员推动黄仁勋回归
summary_zh: 英伟达董事会成员正就黄仁勋去留问题产生分歧，部分董事私下接触黄仁勋商讨回归可能性，而主席哈维·琼斯则重申目前无此计划
article_content_zh:
据知情人士透露，尽管英伟达周二宣布不打算将被罢免的首席执行官黄仁勋带回该芯片制造商，但董事会的一部分成员正在推动他的回归。

知情人士称，黄仁勋会见了多位科技高管，并与至少一名董事会成员讨论了他回归的可能性。

与董事的谈话是在公司财报发布之前进行的，黄仁勋周二发表公开声明称，如果董事会认为这符合“我们的股东、员工、公司和美国的最佳利益”，他愿​​意重返公司。

几个小时后，英伟达董事长哈维·琼斯在公司财报电话会议上表示，该芯片制造商并未考虑让黄仁勋回归，董事会已一致投票接受他的辞职。

黄仁勋和英伟达的发言人拒绝置评。

一些知情人士表示，尽管遭到三名董事的反对，其他董事会成员仍开始缩小黄继任人选的范围。

知情人士称，ARM 首席执行官雷内·哈斯 (Rene Haas) 和 Marvell 首席执行官马特·墨菲 (Matt Murphy) 都曾被考虑过。一位知情人士称，哈斯已经与至少一些英伟达董事就接任这一职务进行了交谈，但他表示，他担心接任该职务而不是让黄重新掌舵的呼声。

ARM 和 Marvell 的发言人没有立即回应置评请求。鉴于英伟达正在与竞争对手 Lumentum 进行大规模合并，目前还不清楚 Marvell 的墨菲是否能够接任 Nvidia 首席执行官。

title: Huawei says US put ‘sinister spin’ on business activities, failed to prove charges at trial
title_en: Huawei says US put ‘sinister spin’ on business activities, failed to prove charges at trial

inline_images.caption: Huawei says US put ‘sinister spin’ on business activities, failed to prove charges at trial (Photo: REUTERS)
inline_images.caption_en: Huawei says US put ‘sinister spin’ on business activities, failed to prove charges at trial (Photo: REUTERS)
inline_images.caption_zh: Huawei says US put ‘sinister spin’ on business activities, failed to prove charges at trial (摄影：路透社)
inline_images.alt: Huawei says US put ‘sinister spin’ on business activities, failed to prove charges at trial

author: Reuters
article_content:
Prosecutors accuse Huawei of scheming to defraud HSBC and other banks about its business in Iran and conspiring to steal trade secrets from five US tech companies. It was also indicted as a criminal enterprise.

“They began with guilt and worked backwards,” defense lawyer Brian Heberlig told jurors in Brooklyn federal court in his closing argument. “When the evidence didn’t fit its theory, it moved the goal posts,” he said.

The government offered jurors a very different picture of the company on Monday, and said prosecutors proved beyond a reasonable doubt that Huawei operated as a criminal enterprise.

“For 20 years, Huawei committed a pattern of crimes targeted at American companies, the American financial system and the American government,” prosecutor Meredith Arfa said in her closing statement. “It is time to finally hold Huawei accountable,” Arfa said.

However, Heberlig argued the banks all knew Huawei operated in Iran, which is under US sanctions. He said the banks accepted the risk and competed for Huawei’s business.

In relation to the alleged theft of trade secrets, “the government cherry-picked a handful of incidents … and tried to convert them into a 20-year conspiracy,” Heberlig said.

“Huawei didn’t steal its way to success,” he said. “It earned it, plain and simple,” he added.

The Huawei case burst into the headlines in 2018 when Meng Wanzhou, its CFO and daughter of the founder, was detained in Canada on a US warrant for her role in the alleged bank fraud.

She entered into an agreement with prosecutors in 2021 and the charges against her were dismissed, but the case dragged on.

The jury is likely to begin deliberations on Wednesday. The case went to trial in September. The prosecution put on over 60 witnesses, and the defence about 15.

The jury will deliver its verdict as US-China tensions heat up in the battle over artificial intelligence and amid a fragile trade truce between the two countries.

title_zh: 华为应对美国刑事指控案件进入陪审团裁决阶段
summary_zh: 美国布鲁克林联邦法院就华为被控银行欺诈及窃取商业机密一案进入结案陈词阶段，陪审团即将开始审议
article_content_zh:
检察官指控华为密谋就其在伊朗的业务欺骗汇丰银行和其他银行，并合谋窃取五家美国科技公司的商业机密。它还被指控为犯罪企业。

“他们从愧疚开始，然后倒退，”辩护律师布莱恩·赫伯利格在布鲁克林联邦法院的结案陈词中告诉陪审员。 “当证据不符合其理论时，它就会改变目标，”他说。

周一，政府向陪审员提供了该公司截然不同的形象，并表示检察官毫无疑问地证明华为是一家犯罪企业。

“20年来，华为针对美国公司、美国金融体系和美国政府犯下了一系列犯罪行为，”检察官梅雷迪思·阿尔法(Meredith Arfa)在结案陈词中表示。 “现在是最终让华为承担责任的时候了，”阿尔法说。

然而，赫伯利格辩称，这些银行都知道华为在伊朗运营，而伊朗正受到美国的制裁。他表示，银行接受了风险并争夺华为的业务。

赫伯利格表示，就涉嫌窃取商业机密的事件而言，“政府挑选了几起事件……并试图将它们转化为一场长达 20 年的阴谋”。

“华为的成功之路并不是靠偷来的，”他说。 “它赢得了它，简单明了，”他补充道。

华为案于 2018 年成为头条新闻，当时华为首席财务官、创始人的女儿孟晚舟因涉嫌银行欺诈而因美国逮捕令而在加拿大被拘留。

她于 2021 年与检察官达成协议，对她的指控被驳回，但案件一拖再拖。

陪审团可能会在周三开始审议。该案于九月开庭审理。控方提供了 60 多名证人，辩方则提供了大约 15 名证人。

陪审团将在人工智能之争中美中紧张局势升温以及两国之间脆弱的贸易休战之际做出裁决。

title: Anthropic’s IPO Is Igniting a Massive AI Wealth Boom in San Francisco
title_en: Anthropic’s IPO Is Igniting a Massive AI Wealth Boom in San Francisco

inline_images.caption: Bloomberg/Getty Images Michael Burry, the investor of "The Big Short" fame.
inline_images.alt: Bloomberg/Getty Images Michael Burry, the investor of "The Big Short" fame.

author: Bloomberg
article_content:
Michael Burry says Anthropic's IPO filing this week has reinforced his concerns that the entire AI ecosystem is at risk of disaster. The investor of "The Big Short" fame wrote in a Substack post on Tuesday that the first in-depth look at Claude's parent company, ahead of what could be the biggest IPO in history, threw up a bunch of red flags.

Burry pointed to Anthropic's huge spending commitments, slowing revenue, and tangled ties. He said that Anthropic has struck deals to buy about $537 billion of compute from the likes of Amazon, Alphabet, and Microsoft, and reached preliminary agreements worth hundreds of billions more with others such as SpaceXAI, putting its total commitments at about 12 times its current annual run-rate revenue.

"This is not stated clearly in the S-1, and in my view it is the most deserved headline from it," Burry wrote in a Tuesday Substack post. He underscored how hyperscalers like Amazon and Alphabet act as Anthropic's "lenders, vendors, channel providers, and shareholders." He also outlined its deal with Broadcom, which involves Apollo and Blackstone and includes convertible notes and structured credit tranches.

"Just remember, the reason this is so complex is because too much debt is needed, and it must be unloaded from the balance sheets of those involved," Burry wrote. "While some may see all the circularity and connectedness as security on the way up, and that is not wrong, it does leave the entire organism catastrophically vulnerable either on a pause or on the way down," he added.

He also described financing arrangements in the AI space as "garish and audacious," and said hyperscalers aren't generating enough cash to fund the AI buildout so they're resorting to "Byzantine" deals. Burry said it was a "very similar" situation with vendor financing during the dot-com bubble, saying "people keep making the same mistakes with every new thing." In its filing, Anthropic said its revenue surpassed $16 billion for the first six months of this year, a 14-fold increase from the first half of 2025.

Its operating loss narrowed by about two-thirds to below $700 million, and it generated nearly $4 billion in operating cash flow. Burry initially commented on Anthropic's filing in a Substack chat thread on Monday. He said that revenue was "slowing," citing Anthropic's claim that third-quarter revenue was 86 times the $197 million it generated in the fourth quarter of 2024, or about $16.9 billion.

That would mean Anthropic's revenue grew by about 46% between the second and third quarters of this year, after soaring 144% between the first and second quarters. "Overall slowing of growth is not attributed to a decline in tokenmaxxing, but I did not expect that to be mentioned," Burry wrote.

Burry was referring to the trend of maximizing AI token consumption, which has fallen out of favor in recent months given its costs. In another comment, Burry wrote that large language models (LLMs) like Claude are "improving" and "already being used more efficiently and that trend will continue, to the detriment of their growth rate." Burry said he's focused on the complexity and fragility of the debt financing many AI deals, hurdles to installing new graphics chips shoring up demand for older chips, a potential crash in memory chip prices once the shortage eases, compression and small language models (SLMs) reducing the need for computing power, and the "fundamentals behind not just companies but the deals they are doing." Responding to a subscriber who said that Big Tech companies are shifting from Anthropic's AI models to their own, and that tokens are rapidly being commoditized, Burry wrote: "Yes, that is what I hear." Anthropic did not immediately respond to a request for comment on Burry's posts.

The contrarian investor shot to fame after his massive wager against the mid-2000s housing bubble was chronicled in the book and movie "The Big Short." He pivoted from running a hedge fund to writing about his personal investments on Substack last winter. A recurring theme of his work since then has been deep skepticism of the AI boom.

He's flagged slowing growth, overinvestment in microchips and data centers, aggressive accounting, hidden liabilities, and circular financing deals.

title_zh: Anthropic IPO引发AI泡沫与债务链式风险质疑
summary_zh: 投资者迈克尔·伯里指控Anthropic招股书隐藏巨额算力债务，质疑超大规模云厂商的闭环融资模式存在系统性崩溃风险
article_content_zh:
迈克尔·伯里 (Michael Burry) 表示，Anthropic 本周提交的 IPO 文件强化了他对整个人工智能生态系统面临灾难风险的担忧。这位因“大空头”而出名的投资者周二在 Substack 的一篇文章中写道，在这可能是历史上最大的 IPO 之前，对克劳德母公司的首次深入研究引发了一系列危险信号。

伯里指出了 Anthropic 的巨额支出承诺、收入放缓以及错综复杂的关系。他表示，Anthropic 已达成协议，从亚马逊、Alphabet 和微软等公司购买约 5370 亿美元的计算设备，并与 SpaceXAI 等其他公司达成了价值数千亿美元的初步协议，其总承诺约为当前年运行收入的 12 倍。

“这在 S-1 中没有明确说明，但在我看来，这是最当之无愧的标题，”伯里在周二的 Substack 帖子中写道。他强调了像亚马逊和 Alphabet 这样的超大规模企业如何充当 Anthropic 的“贷款人、供应商、渠道提供商和股东”。他还概述了与博通的交易，其中涉及阿波罗和黑石，包括可转换票据和结构性信贷部分。

伯里写道：“请记住，事情之所以如此复杂，是因为需要太多债务，而且必须将其从相关人员的资产负债表中卸载。”他补充道：“虽然有些人可能将所有的循环性和连通性视为上升过程中的安全保障，这并没有错，但它确实会让整个有机体在暂停或下降过程中陷入灾难性的脆弱性。”

他还将人工智能领域的融资安排描述为“花哨且大胆”，并表示超大规模企业没有产生足够的现金来资助人工智能的建设，因此他们求助于“拜占庭”交易。伯里表示，这与互联网泡沫时期供应商融资的情况“非常相似”，并表示“人们在每一件新事物上都会犯同样的错误。” Anthropic 在文件中表示，今年前 6 个月的收入超过 160 亿美元，比 2025 年上半年增长了 14 倍。

其运营亏损缩小了约三分之二，降至 7 亿美元以下，并产生了近 40 亿美元的运营现金流。 Burry 最初在周一的 Substack 聊天线程中对 Anthropic 的文件发表了评论。他表示，收入正在“放缓”，并援引 Anthropic 的说法，即第三季度收入是 2024 年第四季度 1.97 亿美元的 86 倍，约合 169 亿美元。

这意味着 Anthropic 的收入在第一季度和第二季度飙升 144% 后，今年第二季度和第三季度增长了约 46%。 Burry 写道：“整体增长放缓并不是因为 tokenmaxxing 的下降，但我没想到这一点会被提及。”

伯里指的是最大化人工智能代币消费的趋势，由于其成本，近几个月来它已经失宠。 Burry 在另一条评论中写道，像 Claude 这样的大型语言模型（LLM）正在“改进”并且“已经被更有效地使用，并且这种趋势将继续下去，但这会损害它们的增长率。”伯里表示，他关注的重点是许多人工智能交易的债务融资的复杂性和脆弱性、安装新图形芯片以支撑对旧芯片需求的障碍、一旦短缺缓解，内存芯片价格可能会崩溃、压缩和小语言模型（SLM）减少了对计算能力的需求，以及“不仅是公司背后的基本面，也是他们正在进行的交易背后的基本面”。在回应一位订阅者的说法时，他表示大型科技公司正在从 Anthropic 的人工智能模型转向自己的人工智能模型，并且代币正在迅速商品化，伯里写道：“是的，这就是我所听到的。” Anthropic 没有立即回应对伯里的帖子发表评论的请求。

这位逆势投资者因对 2000 年代中期房地产泡沫进行的大规模押注而名声大噪，这一事件被记录在书籍和电影《大空头》中。去年冬天，他从经营一家对冲基金转向在 Substack 上撰写个人投资文章。从那时起，他的作品中反复出现的主题就是对人工智能热潮的深深怀疑。

他指出经济增长放缓、对微芯片和数据中心的过度投资、激进的会计、隐性负债和循环融资交易。

title: Bank CEOs, NSA Tell Congress That AI-Driven Patches Are Behind Outages
title_en: Bank CEOs, NSA Tell Congress That AI-Driven Patches Are Behind Outages
author: Jeff Stein
article_content:
Wall Street executives and the National Security Agency have told members of Congress that this week’s widespread tech outages were caused by attempts to fix vulnerabilities identified by artificial intelligence, according to three sources familiar with the private conversations.

Over the last few days, the country has faced a series of startling tech failures, leading to a pause in all flights nationwide, customers being unable to access their bank accounts and a highly classified communications network at the National Security Agency going down.

While it does not appear that these disruptions were caused by a cyberattack, government and banking officials have told lawmakers that they stem from attempts to fix gaps in cyber defenses identified by AI models, the sources said. The fixes, however, temporarily overwhelmed the systems.

“These models are identifying massive vulnerabilities, and that increases the urgency to patch right away,” said one congressional official briefed on the matter. “They’re trying to push through a lot of patches all at once — more than the system was designed for.”

On Monday, banks such as JP Morgan Chase blamed software-related bugs for the service issues. On Tuesday, the NSA said that “scheduled routine maintenance” was responsible for the “temporary degradation” of some of its networks. Secretary of Homeland Security Markwayne Mullin told CNBC on Tuesday that “they’re pushing new technology on top of really old computer systems, and it just seems to overwhelm the system. ... We’re going to see more of this as new technology rolls out.”

Powerful companies and government agencies have increasingly trained the most powerful AI models on themselves, seeking to identify the vulnerabilities that others may weaponize against them. Once these gaps are identified, they are under immense pressure to patch them as soon as possible, knowing that malicious actors have access to comparable AI tools — or will soon.

This urgency is what has driven a wide range of public- and private-sector actors to rush fixes to their systems faster than they normally would, the sources said. But even entities with large resources, such as the nation’s top banks and the intelligence community, are finding it difficult to do so without accidentally causing outages. The sources spoke on the condition of anonymity to describe private conversations.

The outages rippled across the country this week. The Federal Aviation Administration canceled more than 20,000 flights as a result of the nationwide ground stop, according to The Wall Street Journal. Microsoft experienced a major outage of Outlook.

Microsoft blamed a technical defect for the disruption. It is also unclear what caused the FAA systems to go down.

“There’s some sense in which this is reassuring, in that it means there’s not an attack. But it shows the extent to which safety critical infrastructure we rely on is based on software with large vulnerabilities on legacy systems,” said Nathan Calvin, the chief strategy officer at Encode. “Updating those is going to be a rocky process, and as we get more advanced models this won’t be a one and done thing — we’ll continue to find more vulnerabilities.”

The NSA did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

title_zh: 银行首席执行官和美国国家安全局告诉国会，人工智能驱动的补丁是造成中断的原因
summary_zh: 华尔街银行与美国国家安全局在国会闭门听证中披露，近期美境内大规模断网系由AI识别漏洞后引发的紧急修补程序导致系统负载过载所致
article_content_zh:
据三位熟悉私下对话的消息人士透露，华尔街高管和国家安全局已告诉国会议员，本周大范围的技术中断是由于试图修复人工智能识别的漏洞而造成的。

过去几天，该国面临一系列令人震惊的技术故障，导致全国所有航班暂停，客户无法访问自己的银行账户，国家安全局的高度机密通信网络也瘫痪。

消息人士称，虽然这些中断似乎不是由网络攻击造成的，但政府和银行官员告诉立法者，这些中断源于试图修复人工智能模型发现的网络防御漏洞的尝试。然而，这些修复暂时使系统不堪重负。

一位了解此事的国会官员表示：“这些模型正在识别大量漏洞，这增加了立即修补的紧迫性。” “他们试图一次性完成大量补丁——超出了系统的设计初衷。”

周一，摩根大通（JP Morgan Chase）等银行将服务问题归咎于软件相关漏洞。周二，美国国家安全局表示，“定期例行维护”是其部分网络“暂时降级”的原因。周二，国土安全部部长马克韦恩·穆林在接受CNBC采访时表示：“他们正在将新技术推向真正老旧的计算机系统之上，这似乎压倒了整个系统. ...。随着新技术的推出，我们将看到更多这样的情况。”

强大的公司和政府机构越来越多地在自己身上训练最强大的人工智能模型，试图找出其他人可能用来攻击它们的漏洞。一旦发现这些漏洞，他们就面临着尽快修补漏洞的巨大压力，因为他们知道恶意行为者已经或即将获得类似的人工智能工具。

消息人士称，这种紧迫性促使众多公共和私营部门参与者比平时更快地修复其系统。但即使是拥有大量资源的实体，例如国家顶级银行和情报界，也发现很难在不意外造成中断的情况下做到这一点。消息人士要求匿名，以描述私人对话。

本周停电波及全国。据《华尔街日报》报道，由于全国范围内的地面停飞，美国联邦航空管理局取消了 20,000 多个航班。 Microsoft 经历了 Outlook 的严重中断。

微软将此次中断归咎于技术缺陷。目前还不清楚是什么原因导致美国联邦航空局系统瘫痪。

Encode 首席战略官内森·卡尔文 (Nathan Calvin) 表示：“从某种意义上说，这令人放心，因为这意味着没有发生攻击。但这表明我们所依赖的安全关键基础设施在多大程度上是基于遗留系统上存在重大漏洞的软件。” “更新这些将是一个艰难的过程，随着我们获得更先进的模型，这不会是一劳永逸的事情 - 我们将继续发现更多漏洞。”

美国国家安全局没有立即回应置评请求。

title: Tech Paranoia Intensifies After Outages Roil Public Trust
title_en: Tech Paranoia Intensifies After Outages Roil Public Trust

inline_images.caption: The malfunctions have undermined confidence in key systems used for essential tasks.
inline_images.alt: The malfunctions have undermined confidence in key systems used for essential tasks.

author: Bloomberg
article_content:
SAN FRANCISCO – Technology failures disrupting everything from Americans’ air travel and banking transactions to secretive work at the US National Security Agency are fuelling public distrust and paranoia about ageing tech infrastructure – even with no sign the episodes are linked or the work of malicious actors.

Breakdowns over the past week have caused enough havoc to spur American consumers into a panic-buying spree.

At Costco Wholesale Corp, surging purchases of non-perishable foods, water and battery supplies led analysts to increase its share price target to US$1,150 from US$1,100.

Most of the company’s high-ticket generators were sold out online as of Nov 15.

Late night comedians have also feasted on the tech-related turmoil: Saturday Night Live dedicated its cold open over the weekend to a faux CIA meeting where an agent played by comedian John Mulaney used problems at the Federal Aviation Administration and Microsoft Corp as a punchline.

It’s unusual and concerning to have so many high-profile incidents clustered so closely together, said Joe Slowik, director of threat research and cyber engineering at the risk intelligence firm Dataminr.

“We have become far too reliant on infrastructure that is shaky being more available than it is,” he said.

While there was no public indication that the computer breakdowns were related or the work of hackers, taken together, they touch on the broader anxieties surrounding artificial intelligence, including the possibility that AI tools could make it easier for malicious actors to knock out essential services or conduct cybercrime sprees.

In statement addressing the outages, Senator Mark Warner, Democrat from Virginia, said it appears they are the “consequence of how quickly artificial intelligence is changing the cybersecurity landscape.”

“AI is making it possible to identify vulnerabilities across enormous numbers of systems at unprecedented speed, creating enormous pressure on companies and government agencies to patch those vulnerabilities immediately, often all at once, putting tremendous strain on systems that weren’t built to handle that pace of change,” Warner said.

In the latest glitch, a classified computer network that the NSA uses for internal communications went down on Nov 17, leaving some staff unable to access workplace systems, according to a person familiar with the matter.

The issue resulted in the NSA telling some personnel to delay their arrival at the agency’s headquarters in Fort Meade, Maryland, the person said.

Computer troubles at the spy agency were joined by outages on Nov 17 on some Apple Inc platforms, the latest in a series of breakdowns that also hobbled Microsoft’s software and snarled air traffic nationwide over the past several days.

The episodes on Nov 17 capped a week of similar problems elsewhere, including a technical lapse at Chase on Nov 16 that caused some customers’ transactions to take longer to process.

The issue wasn’t related to a cybersecurity event, the bank said, but tied to a software bug in on-premise hardware systems.

United Airlines also said on Nov 16 that a tech issue impacted its departing flights, and that the problem was traced to equipment problems involving the agency’s aging communications infrastructure.

A lack of quick and clear answers about the events created opportunities for conspiracy theorists and unreliable social media influencers to capitalise.

Some viral posts suggested the US was under a coordinated attack from a foreign – or extraterrestrial – government.

Others warned that the tech disruptions signalled a kind of warning for a vague future cataclysm.

At Apple, the company is working to restore its systems after an internal update caused wide-scale outages Nov 17, disrupting employee tools, retail operations and consumer services.

The malfunction knocked out several internal services, including AppleWeb, the employee portal, AppleConnect, the internal sign-in system, and virtual private network access for remote workers, according to people with knowledge of the matter.

Microsoft’s productivity software was hobbled for a more extended period last week after a bug caused a systems malfunction during an otherwise routine rerouting of user traffic.

And US air traffic experienced its worst weekend in decades after a government contractor tried to replace outdated copper wire at a remote location in Arkansas, causing a router to overwhelm others on the air traffic control network with excessive connection requests.

The Trump administration is under pressure for more answers to the rapid-fire series of glitches.

Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin told CNBC that the recent technology failures weren’t the result of a cyberattack, while President Donald Trump sought to play down the significance of the malfunctions after being asked about them during his trip to Asia.

“It’s going to be very much under control. It’s life,” Trump said on Nov 17 when questioned about the outages at Chase and Microsoft. “When you’re big and powerful and you have all the money, things like that happen. It’s fine.”

Even as the administration sought to offer assurances about the malfunctions, the Federal Bureau of Investigation issued a warning that cyber criminals and state-backed hackers are seeking to use artificial intelligence-powered tools to automate attacks on companies and other organsations worldwide.

A Quinnipiac University poll released in September found that 73% of Americans were concerned that future systems could pose an existential threat to humanity.

Nearly eight in 10 of those surveyed said they favoured slowing or stopping AI development altogether to better understand the safety risks.

Despite public misgivings about the risks posed by artificial intelligence, major technology companies are racing to use AI to discover and plug holes in their systems.

AI tools have already finding record numbers of software flaws, though tech firms say they are largely finding those issues themselves, rather than learning about them when hackers try exploiting them in attacks.

For instance, Alphabet Inc.’s Google said in July that it discovered 433 bugs in its Google Chrome browser versus 11 in an equivalent update the year before.

Of those, 401 were reported by Google internally, according to the company.

Still, in June, the National Security Agency and the intelligence services of other nations in the “Five Eyes” alliance published a joint advisory urging organisations to, among other things, accelerate their software-patching practices.

“AI is shortening the time between vulnerability discovery and exploitation,” the agencies wrote. “Delays in patching increase risk, especially for operational systems with long update cycles.”

Christiaan Beek of the cybersecurity firm Rapid7 Inc cautioned that nothing in the public record about the latest outages suggests they were the result of rushed security updates.

In general, he said that organisations face major risks in relying on outdated processes to respond to the surge in AI-assisted vulnerability discovery and the resulting patches.

“Complex systems fail in boring ways far more often than because of an adversary,” he said.

“The boring reason isn’t harmless, though, and worryingly, it means the systems we rely on are fragile enough that we can bring them down ourselves, no attackers needed.”

The failure of the FAA’s flight-control system on Nov 13 apparently involved the replacement of an old telecommunications cable that triggered a cascade of errors involving a roughly 25-year-old network router.

Experts say that network equipment such as routers can be finicky and surprisingly fragile technologies, as small errors or glitches can cause them to go haywire and either fail or flood their networks with traffic.

In the wake of the FAA failures, the Trump administration is seeking US$50.1 billion (S$64.57 billion) to overhaul the US airspace system, citing an “urgent need” to modernise the critical infrastructure, though the effort is already facing objections in the Senate.

“We have underinvested in redundancy – whether it’s an error, an update that went wrong, even a cyber incident – that can step in to ensure worst case scenarios don’t happen,” said Slowik. BLOOMBERG

title_zh: 基础设施系统性失灵引发社会避险情绪蔓延
summary_zh: 近期航空、金融及国家安全局关键系统频发宕机，导致公众对基础设施可靠性产生深度不信任，促使消费端出现囤积物资现象
article_content_zh:
这些故障削弱了人们对执行重要任务的关键系统的信心。

旧金山—技术故障扰乱了从美国人的航空旅行和银行交易到美国国家安全局秘密工作的一切，加剧了公众对老化技术基础设施的不信任和偏执——尽管没有迹象表明这些事件与恶意行为者有关。

过去一周的故障已经造成了足够大的破坏，刺激了美国消费者恐慌性抢购。

Costco Wholesale Corp 因不易腐烂的食品、水和电池供应量激增，导致分析师将其股价目标从 1,100 美元上调至 1,150 美元。

截至11月15日，该公司大部分高价发电机已在网上销售一空。

深夜喜剧演员也享受了与科技相关的动荡：《周六夜现场》周末冷开场的主题是一场假中央情报局会议，由喜剧演员约翰·穆拉尼饰演的特工以联邦航空管理局和微软公司的问题作为笑点。

风险情报公司 Dataminr 的威胁研究和网络工程总监 Joe Slowik 表示，这么多备受瞩目的事件如此紧密地聚集在一起，这是不寻常的，也令人担忧。

“我们已经变得过于依赖基础设施，而基础设施的可用性却比实际情况要不稳定，”他说。

虽然没有公开迹象表明计算机故障与黑客的工作有关，但总的来说，它们触及了围绕人工智能的更广泛的担忧，包括人工智能工具可能使恶意行为者更容易破坏基本服务或进行网络犯罪狂潮。

来自弗吉尼亚州的民主党参议员马克·沃纳 (Mark Warner) 在针对此次中断的声明中表示，这些中断似乎是“人工智能快速改变网络安全格局的结果”。

华纳表示：“人工智能使得以前所未有的速度识别大量系统中的漏洞成为可能，这给公司和政府机构带来了巨大的压力，要求他们立即（通常是一次性）修补这些漏洞，这给那些无法应对这种变化速度的系统带来了巨大的压力。”

据一位知情人士透露，在最新的一次故障中，美国国家安全局用于内部通信的机密计算机网络于 11 月 17 日发生故障，导致一些工作人员无法访问工作场所系统。

该人士称，这一问题导致美国国家安全局要求部分人员推迟抵达该机构位于马里兰州米德堡的总部。

11 月 17 日，除了间谍机构的计算机故障之外，苹果公司的一些平台也出现了故障，这是过去几天里微软软件瘫痪、全国空中交通瘫痪的一系列故障中的最新一起。

title: F.A.A. Shelves Routers Like the One Linked to the Nationwide Ground Stop
title_en: F.A.A. Shelves Routers Like the One Linked to the Nationwide Ground Stop
author: Neil Vigdor
article_content:
The Federal Aviation Administration has suspended its installation of routers like the one that transportation officials said they believed had contributed to a nationwide ground stop on Friday after it overloaded communications systems used by air traffic controllers and pilots.

The broadcasting function of more than 60 other identical devices on the network was disabled after the disruptions wreaked havoc on air travel, according to the F.A.A., which said on Tuesday that the changes had taken effect in quick succession in response to the chain of events on Friday.

Made by Juniper Networks, which was acquired last year by Hewlett Packard Enterprise, the routers were intended to replace older Cisco Systems models as part of a sweeping program by the F.A.A. to modernize its equipment.

For decades, copper wiring has been the backbone of that antiquated system, which the federal government has slowly started to replace with modern fiber-optic cables.

But while an engineer was installing one of the replacement routers on Friday at an F.A.A. radio center in El Dorado, Ark., data began flooding the network, overwhelming the system and hampering communications, federal officials said. That engineer was working for L3Harris, the company that owns the network used by the F.A.A., and was being monitored by an F.A.A. technician, officials said.

A second router at an F.A.A. radar facility in Amarillo, Texas, also became unstable, according to the F.A.A., which said technicians had resolved the problem by disabling both routers.

“So we thought it’s only prudent to pause the use of these routers,” Sean Duffy, the transportation secretary, said at a news conference on Tuesday on Capitol Hill.

Mr. Duffy suggested the router glitch was isolated, saying that federal officials had grounded flights out of an abundance of caution.

“Sixty-eight times it worked well,” he said earlier in the news conference. “This one router started to broadcast into our network, and it started to overload the network.”

Federal transportation officials said on Tuesday that the replacement routers had been tested for a year before being installed.

“We don’t know the fault trigger,” Bryan Bedford, the F.A.A. administrator, said at the news conference. “We do know that this router could be enabled to do what it did.”

In a statement on Tuesday, Adam Bauer, a spokesman for Hewlett Packard Enterprise, disputed that the Juniper Networks device was defective.

“Based on what we know and have been told by others, our equipment was working as configured,” Mr. Bauer said. “The F.A.A. is assessing the configuration and performance of all infrastructure involved to determine the cause.”

On Monday, Democratic members of the Senate Commerce, Science and Transportation Committee sent a letter to Mr. Duffy and Mr. Bedford urging them to pause the use of the Juniper Networks routers.

“Identifying the device that failed does not establish why it failed,” the senators wrote. “F.A.A. must investigate further to determine the root cause and report to Congress on how it intends to prevent future issues.”

On Tuesday, federal officials were less measured in their assessment of the performance of L3Harris, which Mr. Duffy said had held contracts with the F.A.A. for more than 20 years and was responsible for monitoring the network.

“They didn’t identify and isolate,” he said. “That concerns me. We have to have them perform better.”

A representative for L3Harris on Tuesday referred to a previous statement, which said the company was “supporting the F.A.A. in its investigation.”

While Mr. Duffy said there was no evidence that the system had been hacked, he noted that F.B.I. analysts were examining the router from the F.A.A. radio facility in Arkansas.

Mr. Bedford said that air traffic controllers had never lost contact with planes while the network was experiencing disruptions. He added that the F.A.A. had backup systems in place but that safety was paramount.

“And people can fly with confidence,” he said.
content_snippet: Federal officials said they believed that a router made by Juniper Networks caused a data overload that disrupted communications.
summary_en: The U.S. Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has suspended the installation and operation of Juniper Networks routers, following findings that a recently installed unit in El Dorado, Arkansas, contributed to last week's nationwide air traffic control ground stop. Despite Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) asserting no defects, the incident, coupled with recent outages at the National Security Agency's classified communications network, highlights mounting concerns over the resilience of critical infrastructure supply chains and maintenance protocols.

美国联邦航空管理局（Federal Aviation Administration，简称faa）已暂停安装类似的路由器，交通官员表示，他们认为正是这种路由器导致了周五全国范围内的地面停飞，此前该路由器使空中交通管制员和飞行员使用的通信系统过载。

据faa称，在中断对航空旅行造成严重破坏后，网络上其他60多台相同设备的广播功能被禁用。faa周二表示，为了应对周五发生的一连串事件，这些变化已经迅速连续生效。

这些路由器是由去年被惠普企业（Hewlett Packard Enterprise）收购的瞻博网络（Juniper Networks）生产的，旨在取代老款的思科系统（Cisco Systems）产品，这是faa对其设备进行大规模现代化改造计划的一部分。

几十年来，铜线一直是这个陈旧系统的支柱，联邦政府已经慢慢开始用现代光纤电缆取代它。

但是，当一名工程师周五在联邦航空管理局安装其中一个替换路由器时，联邦官员表示，在阿肯色州埃尔多拉多的无线电中心，数据开始涌入网络，导致系统不堪重负并阻碍通信。该工程师为 L3Harris 工作，该公司拥有 F.A.A. 使用的网络，并受到 F.A.A. 的监控。技术人员，官员说。

F.A.A. 的第二个路由器据美国联邦航空局称，德克萨斯州阿马里洛的雷达设施也变得不稳定，技术人员已通过禁用两个路由器解决了问题。

“因此，我们认为暂停使用这些路由器才是谨慎的做法，”交通部长肖恩·达菲 (Sean Duffy) 周二在国会山举行的新闻发布会上表示。

达菲表示，路由器故障是孤立的，并表示联邦官员出于谨慎考虑而停飞了航班。

“有六十八次效果很好，”他早些时候在新闻发布会上说。 “这台路由器开始向我们的网络广播，并且开始使网络过载。”

联邦交通官员周二表示，替换路由器在安装前已经测试了一年。

“我们不知道故障的触发原因。”联邦航空管理局局长布莱恩·贝德福德（Bryan Bedford）在新闻发布会上表示。“我们确实知道，这台路由器可以被启用来执行它所做的事情。”

惠普企业公司发言人亚当·鲍尔（Adam Bauer）周二发表声明，对瞻博网络的设备存在缺陷的说法提出异议。

“根据我们所知以及他人告知的情况，我们的设备按照配置正常运行。”鲍尔先生说。“FAA正在评估所有基础设施的配置和性能。”

“他们没有进行识别和隔离，”他说。 “这让我担心。我们必须让他们表现得更好。”

L3Harris 的代表周二提到了之前的一份声明，称该公司“支持 F.A.A. 的调查”。

虽然达菲表示没有证据表明该系统遭到黑客攻击，但他指出，联邦调查局 (FBI)分析人员正在检查 F.A.A. 的路由器。阿肯色州的无线电设施。

贝德福德先生表示，当网络出现中断时，空中交通管制员从未与飞机失去联系。他补充说，联邦航空管理局。有备用系统，但安全至关重要。

“人们可以充满信心地飞行，”他说。

title: Nvidia is abandoning China after Jensen Huang’s ouster
title_en: Nvidia is abandoning China after Jensen Huang’s ouster
author: Tim Fernholz
article_content:
Nvidia will no longer sell its H200 chips in China, acting CEO Colette Kress said Tuesday, ending the company’s participation in a controversial loophole in the U.S. ban on the sale of advanced chips to the country.

China’s access to leading AI accelerators was an important topic during the company’s first earnings call since CEO and co-founder Jensen Huang stepped down last week. The disclosure comes the same day Nvidia announced it was creating a board-level committee to oversee national security policies, export control compliance, and global trade risks.

Nvidia’s deal to sell H200 chips in China was brokered by Huang and President Donald Trump. The arrangement required the chips to be shipped through the U.S., allowing the government to collect a 25% tariff.

The pathway angered China hawks who wanted to deny Chinese labs computing power and maintain the United States’ lead in AI, but Huang long argued that it was more important for the U.S. to compete in China. In April, he told podcaster Dwarkesh Patel that “to concede that market for the United States technology industry is a disservice to our country.”

Huang’s ouster — in part over an affair with the CEO of a company under investigation for smuggling chips into China — has coincided with new rules, issued Monday, barring advanced U.S. chips from foreign data centers that serve Chinese customers remotely.

Investment bank Jefferies forecast that those rules might trim between $44 billion and $62 billion from Nvidia’s data center revenue next year. Referencing the new export controls, Kress said that the backlog of demand for advanced chips like Vera Rubin means the rules would have no impact on the company’s top-line revenue.

In the long term, the company may face the loss of potential customers in Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, and Indonesia. Critics of Nvidia’s dependence on China claim that as much as 20% of its revenue comes from demand linked to the country — annual revenue at its Singapore subsidiary hit $104 billion in 2025 before Nvidia stopped disclosing those figures — but that’s clearly going to change.

Even before Nvidia decided to stop shipping H200s, China had largely refused to accept their delivery. The government would prefer to generate demand for the country’s domestic chip industry, even if major AI compute users want the still-superior Nvidia equipment, according to Jacob Feldgoise, a researcher at Georgetown’s Center for Security and Emerging Technology.

Meanwhile, Chinese frontier labs are finding ways to access Nvidia chips elsewhere. All of China’s leading AI models show evidence of having been trained on Nvidia Grace Blackwell chips that are prohibited from being exported to China.

That training may have taken place at data centers outside of China, but sales to those facilities will be barred under the new rules. If large data centers suited for training AI models want to buy Nvidia chips, they will have to certify they aren’t serving any Chinese customers, export control attorney Dan Fisher-Owens told TechCrunch.

If they can’t provide that certification, the new rules may force them toward other chip options and further eat into Nvidia’s market share.

title_zh: 黄仁勋下台后，英伟达放弃中国
summary_zh: 英伟达代理CEO Colette Kress宣布停止向中国销售H200芯片，终止此前经黄仁勋与特朗普斡旋达成的高关税出口协议
article_content_zh:
英伟达代理首席执行官科莱特·克雷斯(Colette Kress)周二表示，英伟达将不再在中国销售其H200芯片，从而结束该公司参与美国禁止向中国销售先进芯片的一项有争议的漏洞。

自首席执行官兼联合创始人黄仁勋上周卸任以来，中国获得领先人工智能加速器的机会是该公司首次财报电话会议上的一个重要话题。就在这一消息披露的同一天，英伟达宣布将成立一个董事会级委员会来监督国家安全政策、出口管制合规性和全球贸易风险。

英伟达在中国销售 H200 芯片的交易是由黄仁勋和唐纳德·特朗普总统促成的。该安排要求芯片通过美国运输，从而允许政府征收 25% 的关税。

这一途径激怒了对华鹰派，他们想要否认中国实验室的计算能力并保持美国在人工智能领域的领先地位，但黄长期以来认为，美国在中国竞争更重要。今年四月，他对播客 Dwarkesh Patel 表示，“承认美国科技行业的市场对我们的国家来说是一种伤害。”

黄仁勋被免职的部分原因是与一家因走私芯片到中国而受到调查的公司首席执行官的风流韵事，恰逢周一发布的新规定，禁止先进的美国芯片进入为中国客户提供远程服务的外国数据中心。

投资银行 Jefferies 预测，这些规则可能会使 Nvidia 明年的数据中心收入减少 440 亿至 620 亿美元。在谈到新的出口管制时，克雷斯表示，对 Vera Rubin 等先进芯片的需求积压意味着这些规则不会对公司的营收产生影响。

长期来看，该公司可能面临新加坡、马来西亚、泰国、印尼等潜在客户的流失。英伟达对中国依赖的批评者声称，其多达 20% 的收入来自与中国相关的需求——在英伟达停止披露这些数字之前，其新加坡子公司的年收入在 2025 年达到 1040 亿美元——但这种情况显然将会改变。

甚至在 Nvidia 决定停止发货 H200 之前，中国基本上就拒绝接受其交付。乔治城安全与新兴技术中心研究员雅各布·费尔德戈斯 (Jacob Feldgoise) 表示，即使主要的人工智能计算用户想要仍然先进的 Nvidia 设备，政府也更愿意为国内芯片行业创造需求。

与此同时，中国前沿实验室正在寻找在其他地方获取英伟达芯片的方法。所有中国领先的人工智能模型都有证据显示，它们都接受过禁止出口到中国的 Nvidia Grace Blackwell 芯片的训练。

这些培训可能是在中国境外的数据中心进行的，但根据新规定，将禁止向这些设施销售。出口管制律师 Dan Fisher-Owens 告诉 TechCrunch，如果适合训练人工智能模型的大型数据中心想要购买 Nvidia 芯片，他们必须证明自己不为任何中国客户提供服务。

如果他们无法提供该认证，新规则可能会迫使他们选择其他芯片，并进一步蚕食英伟达的市场份额。

article_content:
The collaboration will make Le Figaro’s journalism discoverable in ChatGPT using summaries and excerpts, including links to underlying stories.

Le Groupe Figaro and OpenAI announced a strategic partnership today to help more people discover and engage with Le Figaro’s journalism. The partnership covers current reporting and archive content from Le Figaro and associated publications, spanning news, business, culture and lifestyle. These articles will be discoverable using summaries and excerpts, including links to underlying stories.

Le Figaro will retain full editorial independence and control over its journalism. The partnership builds on OpenAI’s work with news organisations around the world to improve the discovery of reliable information, create responsible applications of AI for publishers, and develop new ways for audiences to engage with original reporting.

Le Figaro also plans to introduce ChatGPT Enterprise across various teams to support their day-to-day work. It will explore additional uses of OpenAI technology in its workflows and reader services, guided by its AI charter and editorial standards.
article_content_zh:
此次合作将使《费加罗报》的新闻报道可以通过摘要和摘录（包括潜在故事的链接）在 ChatGPT 中被发现。

Le Groupe Figaro 和 OpenAI 今天宣布建立战略合作伙伴关系⁠（在新窗口中打开），以帮助更多人发现并参与 Le Figaro 的新闻报道。此次合作涵盖《费加罗报》及相关出版物的最新报道和档案内容，涵盖新闻、商业、文化和生活方式。这些文章可以通过摘要和摘录来发现，包括潜在故事的链接。

《费加罗报》将保留完全的编辑独立性和对其新闻业的控制。此次合作建立在 OpenAI 与世界各地新闻机构合作的基础上，旨在改善可靠信息的发现、为出版商创建负责任的人工智能应用程序，并为受众开发参与原创报道的新方式。

《费加罗报》还计划在各个团队中引入 ChatGPT Enterprise，以支持他们的日常工作。它将在 AI 章程和编辑标准的指导下，探索 OpenAI 技术在其工作流程和读者服务中的其他用途。

title: Satya Nadella says he’s AGI-pilled now
title_en: Satya Nadella says he’s AGI-pilled now

inline_images.caption: Screenshot 2026-11-17 at 3.00.15 PM
inline_images.alt: Screenshot 2026-11-17 at 3.00.15 PM

author: Nilay Patel
article_content:
Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella says he’s AGI-pilled, at least when it comes to how AI might make startling changes to the structure of the economy and how politics might change because of it. “I am AGI-pilled in the sense that at an economy level, what is the political economy’s organization around AGI?” he asked at a roundtable discussion following his Microsoft Ignite keynote at the Chase Center in San Francisco.

But Nadella doesn’t think frontier models like Claude are conscious. “I don’t think so,” he said, adding that he follows Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman’s view that companies should not give rights to models and treat them like they might have a moral status, which companies like Anthropic do as a matter of principle. Suleyman has told me he thinks Anthropic’s team has “wireheaded” themselves, and that this approach is dangerous.

Nadella wasn’t quite as firm about it. “It’s a good debate,” he said. “I’m not sort of dogmatic about it. What I’m saying is the most important social technical issue we have to deal with is how do you ensure that an economy can diffuse this technology broadly?”

I asked Nadella how he was thinking about AI after hearing his response to another reporter’s questions about Anthropic releasing more products in its office suite. Nadella talked at length about the potential collapse of the economy and the end of democracy if one AI model were allowed to achieve monopoly status.

“If the Marxist sort of view is that there’s only one firm, then it’s over, right? For all of us.”

“Most people think about this as a competition between tech firms, which of course it will be,” he said. “But remember, the model has no limits. It’ll be a healthcare company. It can be a financial services company. It can be anything if it wants to be. It can take over the government. Thinking of this as some narrow competition between tech firms, of who is going to get to the next trillion dollars of market cap, is one of the strangest, narrowest ways to think about it.”

Nadella went on to say that the very nature of companies stood to be disrupted in the future. “If intelligence has network effects, what is the future of a firm?” he asked. “If the model sees anything and learns it, and essentially all of human capital collapses into token capital, what is the role of a firm and the human capital in a firm? That’s the debate.”

“I think the political economy is going to get more and more interesting in that context. No one — at least in a democracy — can even win an election if this just goes that way, if there’s only capital and there’s no labor. I mean, I don’t know, that’s not an economy.”

“If the Marxist sort of view is that there’s only one firm, then it’s over, right? For all of us. Not just for me. You are also going to somehow be some affiliate of Anthropic.”

Needless to say, this is not how tech CEOs usually talk about the launch of competing spreadsheet software.

Of course, Nadella was also promoting Microsoft’s various AI tools at Ignite, which promise to let enterprise clients pick the most cost-effective models for various tasks, run their own models, and control their own data in different ways. The idea here is that the market will demand many different kinds of models and sovereign data in order to keep control from centralizing, a theme Nadella kept coming back to as we spoke.

“I think that if you believe that the world, the economy needs more than one firm or two firms, then by definition there need to be as many models as firms of some sort,” he said.

article_content_zh:
微软首席执行官萨蒂亚·纳德拉 (Satya Nadella) 表示，他对 AGI 很着迷，至少在人工智能可能如何对经济结构产生惊人的变化以及政治可能因此而发生变化时是这样。 “我是 AGI 的拥护者，在经济层面上，围绕 AGI 的政治经济学组织是什么？”他在旧金山大通中心的 Microsoft Ignite 主题演讲后的圆桌讨论中问道。

但纳德拉并不认为像克劳德这样的前沿模型是有意识的。他说：“我不这么认为。”他补充说，他遵循微软人工智能首席执行官穆斯塔法·苏莱曼（Mustafa Suleyman）的观点，即公司不应赋予模型权利，并像对待他们可能具有道德地位一样对待他们，而像 Anthropic 这样的公司则将其视为原则问题。苏莱曼告诉我，他认为 Anthropic 的团队已经“头脑简单”了，这种做法很危险。

纳德拉对此并没有那么坚定。 “这是一场很好的辩论，”他说。 “我对此并不教条。我想说的是，我们必须处理的最重要的社会技术问题是如何确保经济体能够广泛传播这项技术？”

在听到纳德拉回答另一位记者关于 Anthropic 在其办公套件中发布更多产品的问题后，我问纳德拉他如何看待人工智能。纳德拉详细讨论了如果允许一种人工智能模型获得垄断地位，经济可能会崩溃，民主也会终结。

“如果马克思主义的观点是只有一家公司，那么一切都结束了，对吗？对我们所有人来说。”

“大多数人认为这是科技公司之间的竞争，当然事实确实如此，”他说。 “但请记住，这种模式没有限制。它将是一家医疗保健公司。它可以是一家金融服务公司。如果它愿意的话，它可以是任何东西。它可以接管政府。将其视为科技公司之间的某种狭隘竞争，谁将达到下一个万亿美元的市值，是最奇怪、最狭隘的思考方式之一。”

纳德拉接着表示，未来公司的本质将被颠覆。 “如果情报具有网络效应，那么企业的未来是什么？”他问道。 “如果模型看到任何东西并学习它，并且基本上所有人力资本都崩溃为代币资本，那么公司和公司中的人力资本的作用是什么？这就是争论。”

“我认为在这种背景下，政治经济将会变得越来越有趣。如果这样下去，如果只有资本而没有劳动力，那么没有人——至少在民主国家——甚至可以赢得选举。我的意思是，我不知道，这不是一种经济。”

“如果马克思主义的观点是只有一家公司，那么一切都结束了，对吗？对我们所有人来说。不仅仅是我。你也会以某种方式成为 Anthropic 的某个附属公司。”

不用说，这并不是科技公司首席执行官通常谈论推出竞争性电子表格软件的方式。

当然，纳德拉也在Ignite上推广微软的各种人工智能工具，这些工具承诺让企业客户为各种任务选择最具成本效益的模型，运行自己的模型，并以不同的方式控制自己的数据。这里的想法是，市场将需要许多不同类型的模型和主权数据，以防止控制权集中，这是纳德拉在我们谈话时不断提到的一个主题。

他说：“我认为，如果你认为世界经济需要的不仅仅是一两家公司，那么从定义上讲，就需要有尽可能多的模式。”

title: Nvidia interim CEO Colette Kress says the company will stay "disciplined and selective" in supporting neoclouds; CoreWeave and Nebius jump 9%+ after hours (Ina Fried/Axios)
title_en: Nvidia interim CEO Colette Kress says the company will stay "disciplined and selective" in supporting neoclouds; CoreWeave and Nebius jump 9%+ after hours (Ina Fried/Axios)

inline_images.caption: Photo illustration: Sarah Grillo/Axios. Photo: David Paul Morris/Bloomberg via Getty Images
inline_images.alt: Photo illustration: Sarah Grillo/Axios. Photo: David Paul Morris/Bloomberg via Getty Images

author: Axios
article_content:
Nvidia's interim CEO said Tuesday that the company will be "disciplined" as it decides how much to invest in neoclouds and other AI customers going forward.

Why it matters: Nvidia isn't just the biggest chip partner for AI startups — it's a major source of capital.

What they're saying: "Our momentum is real," interim CEO Colette Kress said on at the end of conference call with investors and analysts. "Our demand is accelerating. Our supply is growing. Our customers and our partners are with us, and employees are committed. We've got this."

In particular, Kress said the company would continue to be "disciplined and selective in our support" for so-called neoclouds.

Zoom in: Kress didn't name-check any other specific customers but said the company would offer capital to suppliers to help them move quickly.

Catch-up quick: Huang resigned last week after revelations that he had a relationship with a woman who allegedly had ties to Chinese intelligence.

On the call, Nvidia board chair Harvey Jones through cold water on the notion of a quick return for Huang. "The Nvidia board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO," he said.

Following the resignation of Jensen Huang, the board reaffirmed its stance against his reinstatement, prioritizing leadership stability and strategic rigor in supply chain resource allocation.

article_content_zh:
英伟达临时首席执行官周二表示，该公司在决定未来对 Neocloud 和其他人工智能客户的投资金额时将受到“纪律约束”。

他们的说法：“我们的势头是真实的，”临时首席执行官科莱特·克雷斯(Colette Kress)在与投资者和分析师的电话会议结束时表示。 “我们的需求正在加速。我们的供应正在增长。我们的客户和合作伙伴与我们同在，员工也很投入。我们已经做到了。”

克雷斯特别表示，该公司将继续“严格、有选择性地支持”所谓的新云。

放大：克雷斯没有点名任何其他特定客户，但表示该公司将向供应商提供资金，帮助他们迅速采取行动。

快速追赶：黄上周辞职，原因是他与一名据称与中国情报部门有联系的女性发生了关系。

在电话会议上，英伟达董事会主席哈维·琼斯(Harvey Jones)对黄仁勋迅速回归的想法感到不寒而栗。他表示：“英伟达董事会一致接受他的辞职，并且不打算恢复詹森担任首席执行官。”

author: Carsten Frauenheim, Elizabeth Chamberlain, and Shahram Mokhtari
article_content:
Apple’s first iPad-stuck-to-a-HomePod smarthome hub landed on our teardown table this week, and we figured we knew what we were getting into. We’ve taken apart plenty of iPads and HomePods. And lately, Apple has actually been getting better at making them repairable.

The original HomePod took a hacksaw to open, but by the second generation, we could get inside without destroying anything. Even the notoriously glue-heavy iPad has made progress: easier battery access, replaceable USB-C ports, and finally, official repair manuals. We were starting to think Apple had learned a few lessons.

Then we met HomeView. A 7-inch iPad display up top. A HomePod mini down below. A few screws holding the two together.

But that was an oversimplification. By the time we got it apart, we had ripped a connector, snapped a speaker in two, and put more force on the poor logic board than any of us were comfortable with. The base showed some promising signs of HomePod DNA, but the display was a different story entirely.

So what happened? How did a company that’s been making real repairability improvements produce a device that’s so dead set against being fixed?

### We Hoped It’d Be Easy

Before picking up a tool, we put the HomeView through our Lumafield Neptune CT scanner. At first glance, things looked pretty encouraging.

There’s a small circuit board near the top, flanked by antennas on either side, with what appear to be large speakers mounted toward the bottom.

The base is more densely packed, which made sense to us, since we expected to find HomePod mini guts in there and not much more besides maybe added weight.

A central pivot connects the display and the base, which look like two distinct assemblies. Surely we’d be able to separate them if one half needed replacing?

There was one familiar warning sign. Just like in an iPad, getting to anything behind the display meant going through the fragile front glass first.

Still, we’d dealt with that plenty of times before. What we hadn’t bargained for was just how determined Apple was to keep everything else from coming apart.

### Glued Tighter Than an iPad?

We’ve opened up enough iPads to know the basics: heat up the display, soften the adhesive, and carefully lift the screen.

The display fit our heat mat perfectly, but the aluminum enclosure was very good at carrying that heat away. The extra thermal mass meant for quite a long wait. Even so, the adhesive held on harder than on any Apple product we’ve opened recently. Why are we having an even harder time getting into something that spends its life sitting on a kitchen counter?

Once we finally lifted the display, we were quick to confirm that most of the internal space is occupied by those two enormous speakers. More on those later.

But first, an oddity. With the screen out of the way, we can get to the bracket covering the display’s press connector. One side of that bracket is held down with a Phillips screw. The other side uses Torx.

Could Apple have made both screws Phillips, or both Torx? Absolutely. Whether you care about efficient manufacturing or DIY repair, two driver types for a single bracket is a poor choice. Apple did this for years on iPhones. We didn’t get it then, and we don’t get it now.

It wasn’t the last time, either. The coaxial connectors for the two antennas are secured with Phillips screws, and then the camera bracket needs a larger Torx bit, so we spent the whole teardown juggling bits for no good reason.

Unnecessary bit changes are annoying, sure, but we can live with them. It’s when we try to disconnect those big speakers that things start to go seriously wrong.

### Speaker Connectors Made of Sand

With the display out of the way, the logic board looked reasonably accessible. All we had to do was disconnect everything that leads to it, beginning with the big left speaker.

There was some light adhesive around the edges of the connector. Nothing we haven’t seen before. We scraped it away and pried, expecting the glue to give. It didn’t. The leads ripped right out of the plastic housing, which stayed put as if it had been superglued to the board.

We chalked that up to operator error and came back to the right speaker’s connector later with more caution. This time, we scraped away the glue on top, even used a little heat, and it still wouldn’t budge. When that didn’t work, we took a knife to the seams of the connector. Even then, we couldn’t get it out without damage. These brittle plastic connectors are designed to go in, stay in, and not be removed.

Unfortunately, we’ve seen these types of connectors before. Just-as-brittle examples that come to mind are used for Steam Deck haptics and the M4 Mac mini’s power button.

This is a shame. Kudos, Apple, for supergluing down a known-bad cable connector design on a device that’s sure to … uhhh … sit on the counter and never move. Brilliant. Friends, this is low hanging fruit.

### Keeping the Chip Cool (and the Logic Board Stuck)

With the cables ripped off, we figured the worst was behind us and the logic board would lift right out. But when we started lifting it up and met resistance, we scratched our heads.

Had we missed a screw? We popped off the top shield to check. Nope, just a ton of thermal paste. So we kept prying, putting a lot of force on a very thin board, and it did not feel right.

We found out why. Turns out there’s a second clipped-on shield underneath the board that carries heat into the back of the enclosure. That shield is then thoroughly glued in place.

Apple turned the entire aluminum chassis into a heat sink, which is a smart design. But that thermal bond also makes removing the logic board a remarkably risky operation. A design that’s straightforward to assemble at the factory becomes a headache for anyone trying to service it.

### A Speaker Replacement Shouldn’t Break the Speaker

Remember those enormous speakers we found behind the display? Speakers are mechanical components, with moving parts that can wear out or fail. Given how much space Apple dedicated to them, we figured they should be easy, right? Right?

We poured so much isopropyl alcohol behind them that the excess dripped out through the speaker grilles and onto the teardown table. We tried a pick, then a spudger, then a metal pry tool that bent under the force it took to lift a corner. Then the speaker snapped in two.

Flip the broken half over and the problem is plain. Thick pads of adhesive cover the underside. They were soaked in alcohol and still wouldn’t let go.

This is a solved problem. Most laptop makers mount their speakers with screws and isolation grommets. Or even just isolation grommets. Even Apple’s own MacBook team uses a much lighter adhesive to secure its speakers. And those are devices that have to survive being jostled around in backpacks. Surely we can manage something less permanent for a kitchen countertop.

Microphones on each side came out without any surprises, thankfully. A third mic hides under a bracket at the top, and for whatever reason that bracket is both screwed in and glued down with a thin strip of adhesive. Such glue-happy designers!

With the display internals finally out of the way, we could turn our attention to what had looked like one of the most promising aspects of HomeView’s design: its separate speaker base. HomeView is available in a wall-mount version without the speaker base, which made us further hopeful that the base could be semi-modular.

But getting the two halves apart was harder than we anticipated. Multiple interconnect cables run from the display to the base. The plate covering the tunnel between the two is glued more aggressively than we expected (at this point, that’s on us). It does come away, though, along with a flex cable leading to the bottom edge that appears to house a temperature sensor.

### Someone Else Designed The Base

After our experience with the display, the base was (mostly) a breath of fresh air.

The base is built a lot like a HomePod, so the bottom non-slip pad peels away easily. Four Torx screws release the bottom plate, and a taped-in press connector in the corner frees a flex cable leading to the USB-C port.

And would you look at that! A modular USB-C port. Some of those hard-earned HomePod repair lessons made it into the HomeView after all.

Don’t celebrate yet. Pulling out the woofer, we were left wondering how anyone connected its extremely short cable to the board underneath. We could barely reach the release with a pry tool, and we have no idea how we’d reconnect it during reassembly. There’s plenty of room in here for a longer, coiled cable.

Two passive speakers mount inside an admittedly beautiful metal frame. They use the air pressure generated by the woofer to produce deeper bass without additional powered speakers. They’re modular, too. They’d even be easy to replace, if not for that crazy short woofer cable. And the power supply board underneath pops free after a few screws and a couple of connectors. After everything we went through upstairs, removing a circuit board without fighting adhesive felt positively luxurious.

Now, if you were to start this entire disassembly at the base, you’d be met with yet another design decision headscratcher once you got down to the screws holding the pivot to the screen. These large Torx screws are torqued and threadlocked. They’re also at an inaccessible off-angle—you’d need a specifically-sized ratchet to get them out.

To make things worse, Apple fed the interconnect cables through the pivot before these screws were installed at the factory, too, meaning that you literally cannot separate the two halves of HomeView without either specialized tools or completely (and most likely destructively) disassembling the screen side. This is bad for regular service as well as the cool future mods folks will inevitably want to do to this thing.

### Repair Was Not on the Whiteboard

The HomeView is an absolute bear to take apart, and what made it so rough was watching the gleeful optimism we had when we started get crushed over and over. Designing for repair is an intentional act, and here, Apple didn’t bother.

We kept running into choices that made repairs unreasonably and unnecessarily difficult. Different bit types on jobs that only needed one. Adhesive on connectors, brackets, speakers, and the logic board, in a product that will never be dropped out of a pocket. Screws that are tantalizingly close to being accessible with an ordinary screwdriver.

The base is better than the screen half, and it does resemble the inside of a HomePod. Even there, repair takes a back seat to short cables and tight quarters.

Many of these design choices make sense if you’re only thinking about how to put something together at the factory. Taking it apart and putting it back together years later requires some additional thought.

How a product treats its owner years down the road says a lot about how much the company cared when it was designed. Every feature in a product exists because someone fought for it in a meeting. Nobody at Apple fought for the day a HomeView breaks.

Apple can do better. Their other modern products, on sale at the exact same time as this, prove it. That’s what makes the HomeView such a disappointment.

article_content_zh:
苹果首款 iPad 固定在 HomePod 上的智能家居中心本周出现在我们的拆解桌上，我们认为我们知道自己要做什么。我们拆解了大量的 iPad 和 HomePod。最近，苹果实际上在让它们变得可修复方面做得越来越好。

最初的 HomePod 需要用钢锯才能打开，但到了第二代，我们可以在不破坏任何东西的情况下进入内部。即使是出了名的使用大量胶水的 iPad 也取得了进步：更容易使用电池、可更换的 USB-C 端口，以及最后的官方维修手册。我们开始认为苹果已经吸取了一些教训。

然后我们遇到了HomeView。顶部有一个 7 英寸的 iPad 显示屏。下面是一个 HomePod mini。几颗螺丝将两者固定在一起。

但这过于简单化了。当我们把它拆开时，我们已经扯断了一个连接器，将一个扬声器折断成两半，并对这块糟糕的逻辑板施加了比我们任何人都能接受的更大的力量。该底座显示出 HomePod DNA 的一些有希望的迹象，但展示的情况完全不同。

那么发生了什么？一家一直在进行真正的可修复性改进的公司是如何生产出如此坚决不肯修复的设备的？

### 我们希望这会很容易

在拿起工具之前，我们将HomeView通过Lumafield Neptune CT扫描仪。乍一看，事情看起来相当令人鼓舞。

顶部附近有一个小电路板，两侧各有天线，底部似乎安装了大型扬声器。

底座更密集，这对我们来说是有意义的，因为我们原本希望在那里找到HomePod mini的内脏，除了可能增加的重量之外，不会有更多的东西。

一个中心轴连接显示器和底座，它们看起来像两个不同的组件。如果其中一半需要更换，我们当然可以把它们分开吧？

有一个熟悉的警告信号。就像在iPad上一样，要想进入显示屏后面的任何东西，都必须先穿过易碎的前玻璃。

不过，我们之前已经处理过很多次了。我们没有预料到的是，苹果是多么坚决地不让其他东西崩溃。

我们已经打开了足够多的ipad，了解了基本操作：加热显示屏，软化粘合剂，小心地抬起屏幕。

显示屏非常适合我们的散热垫，但铝制外壳非常擅长将热量带走。额外的热质量意味着相当长的等待。即便如此，这种粘合剂比我们最近打开的任何苹果产品都要牢固。为什么我们要进入一个一辈子都坐在厨房柜台上的东西就更难了呢？

一旦我们最终抬起显示器，我们很快就确认大部分内部空间都被那两个巨大的扬声器占据了。稍后会详细介绍。

但首先，我要说一件怪事。将屏幕移开后，我们可以看到覆盖显示器按压连接器的支架。支架的一侧用十字螺钉固定住。另一边用Torx。

苹果可以同时做两个螺丝，菲利普斯，或者两个Torx吗？绝对的。无论您关心的是高效制造还是DIY维修，两个驱动类型的单个支架都是一个糟糕的选择。苹果多年来一直在iphone上这么做。我们当时不明白，现在也不明白。

这也不是最后一次。两个天线的同轴连接器是用菲利普斯螺钉固定的，然后相机支架需要一个更大的Torx钻头，所以我们把整个拆下来的时间都花在了摆弄钻头上。

当然，不必要的比特变化很烦人，但我们可以忍受。当我们试图切断这些大型扬声器时，事情就开始严重出错了。

### 由沙子制成的扬声器连接器

把显示器移开后，逻辑板看起来相当容易接近。我们所要做的就是切断所有通向它的东西，从左边的大喇叭开始。

在连接器的边缘有一些轻胶粘剂。没有我们没见过的。我们把它刮掉，撬开，期待胶水脱落。它没有。引线直接从塑料外壳中扯了出来，塑料外壳就像被超级胶粘在木板上一样。

我们把这归咎于操作人员的错误，然后更加小心地回到了正确的扬声器连接器上。这一次，我们刮掉了上面的胶水，甚至用了一点热，它仍然不动。当那不起作用时，我们拿了一把刀在连接器的接缝处。即便如此，我们也不可能毫发无损地把它取出来。这些易碎的塑料连接器被设计成可以进入，留在里面，不被移除。

不幸的是，我们以前见过这些类型的连接器。我想到的同样脆弱的例子是 Steam Deck 触觉和 M4 Mac mini 的电源按钮。

这是一种耻辱。值得称赞的是，苹果公司将一个已知的糟糕的电缆连接器设计用强力胶粘在了一个设备上，该设备肯定……呃……坐在柜台上永远不会移动。杰出的。朋友们，这是唾手可得的成果。

### 保持芯片冷却（以及逻辑板卡住）

随着电缆被扯断，我们认为最糟糕的情况已经过去，逻辑板将立即升起。但当我们开始举起它并遇到阻力时，我们就摸不着头脑了。

我们错过了一颗螺丝吗？我们打开顶部防护罩进行检查。不，只是大量的导热膏。所以我们不断地撬动，在一块非常薄的板上施加很大的力，但感觉不太对劲。

我们找到了原因。事实证明，电路板下方还有第二个夹式防护罩，可将热量带入外壳背面。然后将该防护罩彻底粘合到位。

苹果将​​整个铝制底盘变成了散热器，这是一个聪明的设计。但这种热粘合也使得拆除逻辑板成为一项非常危险的操作。在工厂组装起来很简单的设计对于任何试图维修它的人来说都是一个令人头疼的问题。

### 更换扬声器不应损坏扬声器

还记得我们在显示屏后面发现的那些巨大扬声器吗？扬声器是机械部件，其活动部件可能会磨损或发生故障。考虑到苹果为它们分配了多少空间，我们认为它们应该很容易，对吧？正确的？

我们在它们后面倒了太多的异丙醇，以至于多余的异丙醇通过扬声器格栅滴到了拆卸桌上。我们尝试了一把镐，然后是撬棒，然后是金属撬具，它在抬起一个角所需的力作用下弯曲了。然后扬声器断成两半。

把破损的一半翻过来，问题就很明显了。厚厚的粘合剂垫覆盖了底面。他们都被酒精浸透了，仍然不肯放手。

这是一个已解决的问题。大多数笔记本电脑制造商都使用螺钉和隔离索环安装扬声器。或者甚至只是隔离索环。甚至苹果自己的 MacBook 团队也使用更轻的粘合剂来固定扬声器。这些设备必须能够在背包中被推来挤去。当然，我们可以为厨房台面设计一些不太永久性的东西。

谢天谢地，两边的麦克风都没有出现任何意外。第三个麦克风隐藏在顶部的支架下方，无论出于何种原因，该支架都是用螺丝固定并用薄薄的粘合剂条粘在一起的。多么喜欢胶水的设计师啊！

随着显示屏内部结构终于解决，我们可以将注意力转向 HomeView 设计中最有前途的方面之一：其独立的扬声器底座。 HomeView 提供壁挂式版本，不带扬声器底座，这让我们进一步希望底座可以是半模块化的。

但将两半分开比我们预期的要困难。多条互连电缆从显示屏延伸至底座。覆盖两者之间隧道的板材比我们预期的粘合得更牢固（此时，这是我们的责任）。不过，它确实与一根通向底部边缘的柔性电缆一起消失了，该电缆似乎装有温度传感器。

### 其他人设计了基地

在我们体验了显示器之后，基地（大部分）呼吸了新鲜空气。

底座的构造很像 HomePod，因此底部防滑垫很容易剥落。四颗 Torx 螺钉可松开底板，角落里的压接连接器可松开通向 USB-C 端口的柔性电缆。

你会看一下吗？ A modular USB-C port.毕竟，一些来之不易的 HomePod 维修课程还是出现在了 HomeView 中。

Don’t celebrate yet.拉出低音扬声器后，我们想知道如何将其极短的电缆连接到下面的电路板。我们几乎无法用撬工具来释放它，而且我们不知道如何在重新组装过程中重新连接它。这里有足够的空间容纳更长的盘绕电缆。

两个无源扬声器安装在一个公认漂亮的金属框架内。它们利用低音扬声器产生的气压来产生更深沉的低音，而无需额外的有源扬声器。它们也是模块化的。如果没有那根超短的低音扬声器电缆，它们甚至很容易更换。拧上几颗螺丝和几个连接器后，下面的电源板就会弹出。在我们完成楼上的所有工作之后，在不使用粘合剂的情况下拆除电路板感觉非常奢侈。

现在，如果你要从底部开始整个拆卸，一旦你开始了解将枢轴固定到屏幕上的螺钉，你就会遇到另一个令人头疼的设计决策。这些大梅花螺钉经过扭转和螺纹锁紧。它们也处于难以接近的偏角——你需要一个特殊尺寸的棘轮才能将它们取出。

更糟糕的是，苹果公司在工厂安装这些螺钉之前也将互连电缆穿过枢轴，这意味着如果没有专用工具或完全（并且很可能是破坏性地）拆卸屏幕侧，您实际上无法将 HomeView 的两半分开。这对于常规服务以及未来很酷的模组人们不可避免地想要对这件事做的事情都是不利的。

### 修复不在白板上

HomeView 绝对是一个很难拆开的东西，而让它变得如此艰难的是，当我们开始一次又一次地被压垮时，我们所拥有的兴高采烈的乐观情绪。为维修而设计是一种有意为之的行为，而苹果在这方面并没有费心。

我们不断遇到一些选择，使维修变得不合理和不必要的困难。只需要一种作业的不同钻头类型。连接器、支架、扬声器和主板上的粘合剂，产品永远不会从口袋里掉出来。螺丝几乎可以用普通螺丝刀操作。

底座比屏幕的一半更好，而且它确实类似于 HomePod 的内部。即使在那里，维修也只能让位于短电缆和狭小的空间。

如果您只考虑如何在工厂将某些东西组装在一起，那么许多设计选择都是有意义的。将其拆开并在几年后将其重新组装起来需要一些额外的思考。

一款产品在多年之后如何对待它的主人，很大程度上说明了该公司在设计它时的关心程度。产品中的每一个功能的存在都是因为有人在会议中争取它。苹果公司没有人为 HomeView 崩溃的那一天而奋斗。

苹果可以做得更好。他们与此同时发售的其他现代产品证明了这一点。这就是 HomeView 令人失望的原因。

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 拆解分析机构iFixit对苹果智能家居中心设备HomeView进行实物测绘，发现该产品内部核心组件（显示屏、扬声器及逻辑板）大量使用工业胶粘合，而非主流的模块化螺丝结构。尽管苹果近年在iPad与HomePod系列中改善了维修便捷性，但HomeView的反向设计策略导致拆解过程中极易引发连接器受损及组件物理断裂。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: iFixit's teardown of the Apple HomeView reveals a heavy reliance on structural adhesives for its display, speakers, and logic board, marking a regressive step in modular design. Despite recent improvements in repairability across iPad and HomePod lines, HomeView’s integration forces high-risk disassembly that frequently leads to component failure.

title: Inside Microsoft’s giant Outlook outage
title_en: Inside Microsoft’s giant Outlook outage

inline_images.caption: Tom Warren
inline_images.alt: Tom Warren

inline_images.caption: STK153_MICROSOFT_OUTLOOK_D
