title: Jensen Huang Breaks Silence, Signals Willingness to Return as Nvidia CEO
title_en: Jensen Huang Breaks Silence, Signals Willingness to Return as Nvidia CEO

inline_images.caption: Jensen Huang Breaks Silence, Signals Willingness to Return as Nvidia CEO (Source: Wall Street Journal)
inline_images.caption_en: Jensen Huang Breaks Silence, Signals Willingness to Return as Nvidia CEO (Source: Wall Street Journal)
inline_images.caption_zh: Jensen Huang Breaks Silence, Signals Willingness to Return as Nvidia CEO (来源：华尔街日报)
inline_images.alt: Jensen Huang Breaks Silence, Signals Willingness to Return as Nvidia CEO

author: Robbie Whelan
article_content:
Jensen Huang is willing to return to Nvidia as chief executive should he be asked by directors to do so, the former CEO of the tech giant said Tuesday morning in his first public remarks since stepping down.

“Since my departure, I’ve seen an outpouring of calls from Nvidia’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO,” Huang said in a short statement. “If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO.”

This post may contain links from our sponsors and affiliates, and Flywheel Publishing may receive compensation for actions taken through them.

Jensen Huang said on Tuesday that he will come back as chief executive of Nvidia (NASDAQ: NVDA) if the company's board wants him. It is the first time he has spoken publicly about a return since he resigned on Thursday, November 12.

The statement is five sentences long. Huang opened with an apology. He said he did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at Nvidia and that he created problems for the board that he deeply regrets.

“I own my mistakes completely,” he said.

He then said he has seen calls for his return from Nvidia's employees, investors, business partners and customers since he left. He did not ask for the job back. He left the decision to the directors.

As of Monday the board was not looking at a return. CNBC reported that directors are not considering bringing Huang back and are focused on their investigation of him, citing one person familiar with the matter. We covered that report this morning. Nvidia has not said on the record that a return is ruled out, and it had not responded publicly to Huang's statement when this story was published.

Huang resigned as president, chief executive and director after 33 years running the company he co-founded. CNBC reported that the board hired the law firm Wachtell Lipton to examine his conduct and whether it compromised national security or company secrets. That review is still open.

Chief financial officer Colette Kress is interim chief executive. Harvey C. Jones became the first board chair in Nvidia's history. A board representative said on Friday that the company was still choosing a search firm for a permanent chief executive.

An online petition asking the board to reinstate Huang had about 180,000 signatures on Monday, according to CNBC. Elon Musk, Y Combinator chief executive Garry Tan and Epic Games chief executive Tim Sweeney are among the names on it. Two large shareholders, Brad Gerstner of Altimeter Capital and Gavin Baker of Atreides Management, sent the board a letter asking it to move slowly and keep every option open, including Huang's return. We reported on the letter and the employees who signed the petition on Saturday.

President Trump was asked on Monday about Huang coming back. “I would certainly not mind seeing that,” he said.

Huang is also due in Washington. Reuters reported on Tuesday that he will appear before congressional committees in December.

Nvidia closed at $156.14 on Monday, its lowest close since July 1, 2025 and 34.7% below the record close of $239.24 set on October 6. At 10:54 a.m. ET on Tuesday, minutes before the statement, the shares were at $150.58, down 3.6% for the day and 37.1% below the record. By 11:04 a.m., after the statement, they had risen 2.5% to $154.38, down 1.1% for the day and 35.5% below the record.

The timing is hard to miss. Nvidia reports third-quarter results after the market closes on Tuesday, and Kress will lead the call. Analysts expect earnings of $2.47 a share on revenue of $109.15 billion. Nvidia's own forecast was $108.0 billion.

Boards have reversed themselves before. Steve Jobs went back to Apple in 1997, and $10,000 of Apple stock bought then grew to $18.6 million, as we reported on Sunday. The record for chief executives who are pushed out is less kind, and we looked at a study of 187 forced exits the day after Huang resigned.

The next move belongs to Nvidia's directors. They can answer Huang before tonight's earnings call, during it, or wait for the Wachtell review to finish.

Contact [email protected] for any questions or corrections.

“自从我离开以来，我收到了来自 Nvidia 员工、投资者、业务合作伙伴和客户的大量电话，要求我重新担任首席执行官，”Huan。

key_points_zh: 核心事实：黄仁勋打破沉默，表示如果董事会认为符合股东、员工和美国的最佳利益，他愿意重新担任 Nvidia 首席执行官
key_points_en: Key Development: Jensen Huang breaks silence, saying he is willing to return as Nvidia CEO if the board decides it is in the best interest of shareholders, employees, and the US (Robbie Whelan/Wall Street Journal)

article_content_zh:
周二上午，科技巨头英伟达前首席执行官黄仁勋在卸任后的首次公开讲话中表示，如果董事要求，他愿意重返英伟达担任首席执行官。

黄仁勋在一份简短的声明中表示：“自从我离开以来，我看到英伟达的员工、投资者、业务合作伙伴和客户纷纷呼吁我重新担任首席执行官。” “如果董事会认为我的回归符合我们的股东、员工、公司和美国的最佳利益，我将很荣幸回应这些呼吁并重新担任首席执行官。”

这篇文章可能包含来自我们的赞助商和附属机构的链接，Flywheel Publishing 可能会因通过他们采取的行动而获得补偿。

黄仁勋周二表示，如果英伟达董事会需要他，他将重新担任英伟达（纳斯达克股票代码：NVDA）首席执行官。这是他自 11 月 12 日星期四辞职以来首次公开谈论回归。

该声明有五句话长。黄先生首先致歉。他表示，他没有达到英伟达每个人的期望标准，并且给董事会带来了问题，对此他深感遗憾。

“我完全承认自己的错误，”他说。

他随后表示，自从他离开以来，他已经收到了英伟达员工、投资者、业务合作伙伴和客户要求他回归的呼声。他没有要求恢复这份工作。他把决定权留给了董事们。

截至周一，董事会尚未考虑回报。 CNBC 援引一位知情人士的话说，董事们不会考虑让黄回归，而是专注于对他进行调查。我们今天早上报道了这份报告。英伟达并未在记录中表示排除回归的可能性，并且在本文发表时也没有对黄仁勋的声明做出公开回应。

黄先生在经营这家由他共同创立的公司 33 年后，辞去了总裁、首席执行官和董事的职务。 CNBC 报道称，董事会聘请了 Wachtell Lipton 律师事务所来调查他的行为，以及是否危害国家安全或公司机密。该审查仍然开放。

首席财务官科莱特·克雷斯 (Colette Kress) 担任临时首席执行官。哈维·琼斯 (Harvey C. Jones) 成为 Nvidia 历史上第一位董事会主席。一名董事会代表周五表示，该公司仍在为永久首席执行官选择猎头公司。

据 CNBC 报道，一份要求董事会恢复黄先生职位的在线请愿书周一已有约 18 万个签名。埃隆·马斯克 (Elon Musk)、Y Combinator 首席执行官加里·谭 (Garry Tan) 和 Epic Games 首席执行官蒂姆·斯威尼 (Tim Sweeney) 都在名单上。 Altimeter Capital 的布拉德·格斯特纳 (Brad Gerstner) 和 Atreides Management 的加文·贝克 (Gavin Baker) 两大股东致函董事会，要求董事会缓慢采取行动，保留所有选择，包括黄仁勋的回归。我们报道了这封信以及周六签署请愿书的员工。

特朗普总统周一被问及黄仁勋回来的情况。 “我当然不介意看到这一点，”他说。

黄也将抵达华盛顿。路透社周二报道称，他将于 12 月出席国会委员会会议。

英伟达周一收盘价为 156.14 美元，为 2025 年 7 月 1 日以来的最低收盘价，较 10 月 6 日创下的收盘纪录 239.24 美元低 34.7%。美国东部时间周二上午 10:54，即该声明发布前几分钟，该股价格为 150.58 美元，当日下跌 3.6%，较历史纪录低 37.1%。声明发布后，截至上午 11 点 04 分，股价已上涨 2.5%，至 154.38 美元，当日下跌 1.1%，较历史纪录低 35.5%。

时机不容错过。英伟达将在周二收盘后公布第三季度业绩，克雷斯将主持此次会议。分析师预计每股收益为 2.47 美元，营收为 1091.5 亿美元。 Nvidia自己的预测是1080亿美元。

董事会之前也曾发生过逆转。正如我们周日报道的那样，史蒂夫·乔布斯 (Steve Jobs) 于 1997 年重返苹果公司，随后购买的 10,000 美元苹果股票增至 1,860 万美元。被赶下台的首席执行官的记录就不那么友善了，我们研究了黄辞职后第二天有 187 名首席执行官被迫退出的研究。

下一步行动属于英伟达董事的责任。他们可以在今晚的财报电话会议之前、会议期间回答黄仁勋的问题，或者等待 Wachtell 审查结束。

如有任何问题或更正，请联系 [email protected]。

title: Sources: NSA Net, the highly classified network that the NSA uses for its internal communications, is down; there is no evidence of a cyberattack (CNN)
title_en: Sources: NSA Net, the highly classified network that the NSA uses for its internal communications, is down; there is no evidence of a cyberattack (CNN)

inline_images.caption: Katie Bo Lillis
inline_images.alt: Katie Bo Lillis

author: CNN
article_content:
The highly classified network that the National Security Agency uses for its internal communications is down, according to six people familiar with the matter. The network, called NSA Net, allows employees to communicate classified information internally. At this point there is no evidence of a cyberattack, sources said.

As the agency works to understand the scope of the problem, it has enacted staggered arrivals for personnel, the sources said. CNN has asked the National Security Agency for comment. A current and a former US official said an outage at NSA Net would not impact the agency’s ability to communicate urgent intelligence to President Donald Trump while he is traveling in Asia on Air Force One.

Both sources described multiple redundancies and backup networks that the government could use to communicate securely with the president who is currently in the Philippines before heading to China tomorrow for talks with Chinese leader Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin.

The outage at America’s most powerful intelligence agency comes on the heels of multiple major tech glitches affecting airlines and other corporations around the country. All flights nationwide were grounded for hours on Friday after a massive systems failure, leading to thousands of flights being delayed or canceled.

The Federal Aviation Administration traced the problem to a single router in Arkansas. Meanwhile, a massive outage last week affecting Microsoft products left people around the world unable to access Outlook email and Team meetings. There is no indication that the NSA, FAA or Microsoft outages were caused by a cyberattack.

But they are stark examples of how tech failures can roil markets and potentially threaten national security. This story is breaking and will be updated.

title: US official says recent tech woes not tied to cyberattacks
title_en: US official says recent tech woes not tied to cyberattacks

inline_images.caption: NSA outage, other tech issues raise concerns as officials say disruptions not tied to cyberattacks (Photo: REUTERS)
inline_images.caption_en: NSA outage, other tech issues raise concerns as officials say disruptions not tied to cyberattacks (Photo: REUTERS)
inline_images.caption_zh: NSA outage, other tech issues raise concerns as officials say disruptions not tied to cyberattacks (摄影：路透社)
inline_images.alt: NSA outage, other tech issues raise concerns as officials say disruptions not tied to cyberattacks

author: Reuters
article_content:
President Donald Trump and federal officials are seeking to reassure the public after a series of technology disruptions affecting airlines, banks, technology companies and government agencies sparked concerns about cybersecurity.

The disruptions follow Friday's nationwide ground stop and have continued across multiple sectors in recent days. On Tuesday, the National Security Agency said some of its internal systems were affected during what it described as "scheduled routine maintenance," adding that the issue was not the result of a cyberattack.

ABC7 Chicago is now streaming 24/7. Click here to watch

That assessment was echoed by the deputy White House press secretary during an interview with Newsmax.

Asked how officials know the disruptions were not the result of a cyberattack or foreign interference, the spokesperson said: "Look, we see no evidence that this is a cyber attack. I'm not a cyber expert. I leave that to them."

Other technology companies have delivered similar messages this week. Apple said it was undergoing an internal update that caused some outages and said it is working to restore remaining systems as quickly as possible.

SEE ALSO | Tech outage live updates: What to know about Apple, other technology services as users report issues

Meanwhile, lawmakers in both parties are seeking briefings as disruptions continue across several industries.

"These developments are troubling, and it's unclear if it's all infrastructure-related or whether there's some malignant activity," House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries said.

Sen. Josh Hawley also called for more information.

"I mean, if that-if this is all a coincidence, it's like the greatest coincidence in the history of the world. And I'm completely in the dark, and people at home are in the dark, and they shouldn't be. So we should get answers," Hawley said.

One confirmed cyberattack involved Optimizely, a third-party platform that works with clients including Zoom, BBC and CNN, along with more than 150 other brands. The company said it experienced issues Monday evening after malware was planted in some clients' code. Optimizely said the issue has been resolved and that efforts are underway to secure client accounts.

READ MORE | United Airlines resolves widespread system outage, just days after nationwide ground stop

At the same time, Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy is continuing to press Congress for additional funding to modernize aging technology systems.

Duffy said investigations are ongoing into the cause of Friday's ground stop. He also said the Federal Aviation Administration is halting the installation of Juniper routers that apparently played a role in the disruption.

"The router started to broadcast into our network and started to overload our network," Duffy said. "I've been told by our national security three letter agencies that we weren't hacked."

Duffy said the FBI and other government agencies are also investigating to ensure there are no cybersecurity concerns tied to the outages.

Airports appeared to be returning to normal operations. According to FlightAware, O'Hare International Airport reported 12 cancellations during the previous 24 hours.

当被问及官员如何知道这些中断不是网络攻击或外国干涉的结果时，该发言人表示：“看，我们没有看到任何证据表明这是一次网络攻击。我不是网络专家。我把这个问题留给他们。”

其他科技公司本周也发出了类似的信息。苹果表示，它正在进行内部更新，导致一些服务中断，并表示正在努力尽快恢复剩余系统。

另请参阅 |技术中断实时更新：当用户报告问题时，如何了解 Apple 和其他技术服务

与此同时，由于多个行业的混乱仍在继续，两党立法者都在寻求简报。

众议院民主党领袖哈基姆·杰弗里斯表示：“这些事态发展令人不安，目前尚不清楚这是否全部与基础设施有关，或者是否存在一些恶性活动。”

参议员乔什·霍利 (Josh Hawley) 也呼吁提供更多信息。

“我的意思是，如果这一切都是巧合，那就像是世界历史上最伟大的巧合。我完全蒙在鼓里，家里的人也蒙在鼓里，他们不应该这样。所以我们应该得到答案，”霍利说。

一项已确认的网络攻击涉及 Optimizely，这是一个与 Zoom、BBC 和 CNN 等客户以及 150 多个其他品牌合作的第三方平台。该公司表示，周一晚上，在一些客户的代码中植入了恶意软件后，该公司遇到了问题。 Optimizely 表示问题已经解决，并且正在努力确保客户帐户的安全。

与此同时，交通部长肖恩·达菲（Sean Duffy）继续敦促国会提供额外资金，以实现老化技术系统的现代化。

达菲说，目前正在对星期五飞机停飞的原因进行调查。他还表示，美国联邦航空管理局（Federal Aviation Administration）正在停止安装瞻博网络（Juniper）路由器，这显然是造成网络中断的原因之一。

“路由器开始向我们的网络广播，并开始使我们的网络过载，”达菲说。 “我们的国家安全三封机构告诉我，我们没有遭到黑客攻击。”

达菲表示，联邦调查局和其他政府机构也在调查，以确保不存在与网络中断相关的网络安全问题。

机场似乎正在恢复正常运营。据 FlightAware 报道，奥黑尔国际机场报告称，过去 24 小时内有 12 架航班取消。

title: Pantera-backed Codex raises $30 million to link Asia to global markets with stablecoins
title_en: Pantera-backed Codex raises $30 million to link Asia to global markets with stablecoins
author: Camila Grigera Naón
article_content:
Money might make the world go round—but that doesn’t mean getting it around the world is easy. And while stablecoins, or cryptocurrencies pegged to fiat money, can simplify the process considerably, many businesses still lack the infrastructure to use them for cross-border payments. That’s where Codex sees an opportunity.

The Delaware-based startup announced Tuesday it raised $30 million in a Series A round to help businesses send money across borders and exchange currencies, without the need to deposit money in advance to use the service. Codex aims to carve out a niche in Asia and connect the region to markets in Latin America and sub-Saharan Africa.

“We help people convert money into whatever form they want and give it to whoever they want, wherever they want,” Haonan Li, cofounder and CEO of Codex, told Fortune. “Turns out, in lots of parts of the world, this is actually super hard to do.”

The 35-person company plans to use part of the capital to further automate its foreign-exchange platform, with AI agents central to its vision for how the business will operate, and keep costs down as transaction volumes grow.

Pantera Capital led the round, with participation from Dragonfly and Coinbase Ventures, at a $130 million post-money valuation. Both participated in Codex’s earlier seed round, which Dragonfly led alongside backers Circle Ventures, Cumberland, and Wintermute.

Stablecoins have been one of cryptocurrency’s longest-lasting trends, gaining traction as a lifeline in countries with high inflation or capital controls, and as a low-cost payment tool for businesses. Payments made with stablecoins reached at least $401 billion in the first eight months of 2026, up 42% year over year, with businesses on the receiving end of an estimated 58% to 64% of that volume, according to a September report by global consulting firm Alvarez & Marsal.

“[The team] is building Codex to meet the challenge of what happens after this massive explosion of stablecoin issuance, which is… a really fragmented system,” Franklin Bi general partner at Pantera Capital, said.

An economist by training, Li began his career in geopolitical forecasting research for political psychologist and writer Philip Tetlock, followed by a stint in quantitative finance. He later caught the “crypto bug” and became an early employee at Optimism, where he worked on Ethereum scaling and protocol economics.

There, he began to explore crypto’s most practical applications and landed on stablecoins, which some in Ethereum circles dismissed as boring. Li saw a way to help people excluded from traditional financial networks save, transfer, and exchange money.

To build that business, he teamed up with an old friend from his military days. Li had met Victor Yaw, now a Codex cofounder, about a decade earlier in infantry officer candidate school in Singapore’s military. Fellow cofounder Momo Ong, whom Li met through San Francisco’s founder community, initially advised the team before he joined full time. Together, they founded Codex in 2024.

After a few iterations, the company settled on its current product about a year ago. It now has offices in Singapore, Hong Kong and London, as well as New York and San Francisco. As Li put it: “the journey stretched from the jungles of Brunei to the skyscrapers of New York.”

article_content_zh:
金钱或许可以让世界运转起来，但这并不意味着让金钱运转起来很容易。尽管稳定币或与法定货币挂钩的加密货币可以大大简化流程，但许多企业仍然缺乏使用它们进行跨境支付的基础设施。这就是 Codex 看到的机会。

这家总部位于特拉华州的初创公司周二宣布，在 A 轮融资中筹集了 3000 万美元，帮助企业跨境汇款和兑换货币，而无需提前存钱即可使用该服务。 Codex 旨在在亚洲开拓市场，并将该地区与拉丁美洲和撒哈拉以南非洲市场连接起来。

Codex 联合创始人兼首席执行官李浩南向《财富》杂志表示：“我们帮助人们将金钱转换成他们想要的任何形式，并随时随地将其送给任何他们想要的人。” “事实证明，在世界许多地方，这实际上是非常难做到的。”

这家拥有 35 名员工的公司计划利用部分资金进一步自动化其外汇平台，人工智能代理将成为其业务运营愿景的核心，并随着交易量的增长降低成本。

Pantera Capital 领投，Dragonfly 和 Coinbase Ventures 跟投，投后估值为 1.3 亿美元。两人都参与了 Codex 的早期种子轮融资，由 Dragonfly 与支持者 Circle Ventures、Cumberland 和 Wintermute 共同领投。

稳定币一直是加密货币最持久的趋势之一，作为高通胀或资本管制国家的生命线以及企业的低成本支付工具而受到关注。根据全球咨询公司 Alvarez & Marsal 9 月份的一份报告，2026 年前 8 个月，使用稳定币支付的金额至少达到 4010 亿美元，同比增长 42%，其中企业接收的金额预计占 58% 至 64%。

Pantera Capital 普通合伙人 Franklin Bi 表示：“[团队]正在构建 Codex，以应对稳定币发行大规模爆炸后所发生的挑战，这是一个非常分散的系统。”

作为一名训练有素的经济学家，李开始了他的职业生涯，为政治心理学家和作家菲利普·泰洛克进行地缘政治预测研究，随后在量化金融领域工作了一段时间。后来他发现了“加密货币错误”，并成为 Optimism 的早期员工，在那里他从事以太坊扩展和协议经济学工作。

在那里，他开始探索加密货币最实际的应用，并最终选择了稳定币，但以太坊圈子里的一些人认为稳定币很无聊。李找到了一种方法来帮助那些被排除在传统金融网络之外的人们储蓄、转移和兑换货币。

为了开展这项业务，他与一位军旅时期的老朋友合作。大约十年前，李在新加坡军队的步兵军官候补学校认识了 Victor Yaw，他现在是 Codex 的联合创始人。李通过旧金山的创始人社区结识了联合创始人之一的 Momo Ong，他在全职加入之前最初为团队提供了建议。他们于 2024 年共同创立了 Codex。

经过几次迭代后，该公司大约一年前确定了当前的产品。目前，该公司在新加坡、香港、伦敦以及纽约和旧金山设有办事处。正如李所说：“旅程从文莱的丛林延伸到纽约的摩天大楼。”

title: Jensen Huang slated to appear before House panels Dec. 1; Nvidia lawyer due to testify Dec. 2
title_en: Jensen Huang slated to appear before House panels Dec. 1; Nvidia lawyer due to testify Dec. 2
author: Garrett Downs
article_content:
Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang will appear before the House Foreign Affairs, Intelligence and China Select committees on Dec. 1, the leaders of those congressional panels said overnight.

Nvidia general counsel Tim Teter will appear before the committees on Dec. 2, the lawmakers said in a statement.

"We look forward to hearing from Jensen Huang and Tim Teter on their roles in a potential breach of our national security,"said Reps. Brian Mast, R-Fla., John Moolenaar, R-Mich., and Rick Crawford, R-Ark., the chairs of the Foreign Affairs, China Select and Intelligence committees, respectively.

"The American people need answers on Mr. Huang and Nvidia's role in allowing dangerous PRC actors to access our most advanced chips, as well as the role of a potential Chinese intelligence asset in this scandal,"they said. The chairs had originally set Nov. 18 as the date for Huang to speak with them. While they invited him to appear voluntarily, Mast said they would subpoena him if he didn't accept.

Huang resigned from Nvidia last week after revelations that he had an extramarital affair with a woman suspected by U.S. intelligence to be a Chinese spy. Lawmakers have since called for investigations into Huang and Nvidia to determine the extent of damage to the U.S.' lead in artificial intelligence and national security.

The woman, Alice Huang, was an executive at Singapore-based technology company Megaspeed, which Nvidia sold chips to — raising concerns in Washington that at least some of the chips were subsequently diverted to China.

Jensen Huang and Teter will appear before the committees for transcribed interviews, the lawmakers said, meaning the appearances will likely be behind closed doors.

The dates before the committees add to Huang's growing troubles on Capitol Hill. Senate Banking Committee Chair Tim Scott, R-S.C., summoned the former CEO to appear before his committee for a public hearing on Dec. 3 and threatened a subpoena if necessary. Scott also called on Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick to testify on Dec. 10.

A spokesperson for Huang declined to comment Tuesday about Huang's pending appearance in the Senate. A spokesperson for the Senate Banking Committee did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Democrats, who will take over both chambers of Congress in January, have also vowed to continue digging into Nvidia and whether it cooperated with export controls.

The Commerce Department and Justice Department released a statement Tuesday about their investigation into Megaspeed — which was unusual, as federal agencies rarely comment on an investigation while it's still active and it's uncommon to release a joint statement.

The agencies said that following Commerce Department enforcement actions in 2025, which included an interview with Alice Huang, the DOJ took the lead role in the investigation.

"The Department of Justice and the Department of Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security working together will bring the full extent of the law against Megaspeed for any criminal conduct that may have occurred,"the agencies' statement said.

President Donald Trump, however, who has had a close relationship with Jensen Huang, has backed the embattled former CEO. And Huang on Tuesday issued a statement saying he "would be honored"to return as CEO.

The president on Monday said he would be open to Huang returning to the top of the chipmaker, which is being steered by interim CEO Colette Kress.

Correction: The headline on this story has been updated to reflect that Nvidia's lawyer is due to testify before House committees on Dec. 2. A previous headline misstated the date.

article_content_zh:
众议院外交事务委员会、情报委员会和中国特别委员会的领导人连夜表示，英伟达前首席执行官黄仁勋将于 12 月 1 日出席众议院外交事务委员会、情报委员会和中国特别委员会的听证会。

立法者在一份声明中表示，Nvidia 总法律顾问 Tim Teter 将于 12 月 2 日出席委员会会议。

外交事务委员会、中国专责委员会和情报委员会主席、佛罗里达州共和党众议员布莱恩·马斯特、密歇根州共和党众议员约翰·穆勒纳尔和阿肯色州共和党众议员里克·克劳福德表示：“我们期待听到黄仁勋和蒂姆·泰特关于他们在潜在违反国家安全行为中所扮演的角色。”

他们表示：“美国人民需要了解黄先生和英伟达在允许危险的中国行为者获取我们最先进的芯片方面所扮演的角色，以及潜在的中国情报资产在这起丑闻中所扮演的角色。”主席们最初将 11 月 18 日定为黄与他们谈话的日期。虽然他们邀请他自愿出庭，但马斯特表示，如果他不接受，他们就会传唤他。

黄上周从英伟达辞职，原因是他与一名被美国情报部门怀疑为中国间谍的女子有婚外情。此后，议员们呼吁对黄仁勋和英伟达进行调查，以确定对美国造成的损害程度。在人工智能和国家安全领域处于领先地位。

这名女子名叫 Alice Huang，是新加坡科技公司 Megaspeed 的一名高管，英伟达向该公司出售芯片，这引起了华盛顿的担忧，认为至少部分芯片随后被转移到中国。

议员们表示，黄仁勋和泰特将出席委员会进行采访记录，这意味着会议可能会闭门进行。

委员会面前的日期增加了黄在国会山日益严重的麻烦。参议院银行委员会主席蒂姆·斯科特（R-S.C.）于 12 月 3 日传唤这位前首席执行官出席委员会的公开听证会，并威胁在必要时发出传票。斯科特还呼吁商务部长霍华德·卢特尼克于 12 月 10 日作证。

黄的发言人周二拒绝就黄即将在参议院露面发表评论。参议院银行委员会发言人没有立即回应置评请求。

将于一月份接管国会参众两院的民主党人也誓言要继续深入调查英伟达及其是否配合出口管制。

美国商务部和司法部周二就其对 Megaspeed 的调查发表了一份声明，这很不寻常，因为联邦机构很少对仍在进行中的调查发表评论，而且发布联合声明的情况也很少见。

这些机构表示，继商务部 2025 年采取执法行动（其中包括采访 Alice Huang）之后，司法部在调查中发挥了主导作用。

这些机构的声明称：“司法部和商务部工业与安全局共同努力，将对 Megaspeed 可能发生的任何犯罪行为采取全面法律制裁。”

然而，与黄仁勋关系密切的唐纳德·特朗普总统支持了这位陷入困境的前首席执行官。黄仁勋周二发表声明称，他“很荣幸”再次担任首席执行官。

总统周一表示，他对黄重回这家芯片制造商的高层持开放态度，该公司由临时首席执行官科莱特·克雷斯(Colette Kress)领导。

title: Mexico Risks Missing Out on AI Data Center Boom as Energy Crunch Bites
title_en: Mexico Risks Missing Out on AI Data Center Boom as Energy Crunch Bites
author: Bloomberg
article_content:
The reporting was supported by a grant from the Pulitzer Center.

MEMPHIS, Tenn. — More than three decades after serving in Operation Desert Storm, Loretta Young Thornton never expected the sounds of war to follow her home.

Thornton, 66, spent nearly 25 years in the Tennessee Army National Guard, serving as a military police officer before retiring as a decorated sergeant in 2004. She also built a career with the U.S. Postal Service.

After a lifetime of work, she poured her savings into a modest, four-bedroom home built in the 1920s on a secluded two-acre lot in Memphis, near the Mississippi state line.

When Thornton bought the house in 2014, the surrounding woods were home to deer, squirrels, hawks and wild turkeys. At night, she listened to the calls of owls, including one she affectionately called her boyfriend.

Then the trees came down, sending clouds of dust swirling toward Thornton's home.

In their place rose Colossus 2, a massive data center built for billionaire Elon Musk's artificial intelligence company, xAI. The sprawling complex, designed to house thousands of powerful computer chips to train the next generation of AI models, sits just across the railroad tracks from Thornton's property.

Now, the sounds of nature have been replaced by the drone of industrial machinery, a mechanical roar resembling a jet engine that Thornton said runs day and night.

The squirrels have disappeared. The owls have largely fallen silent.

The relentless noise sometimes triggers troubling memories of her military service, forcing Thornton to remind herself that she's no longer in a war zone.

“When I come out here, or when I go to bed at night, I train my thoughts,” she said. “You OK? You at home? Ain't no bomb gonna drop on you. You know you ain't in the desert no more.”

She tries to tune out the noise by working in her yard and renovating her back deck. Humor helps, too.

“I just say that's my noisy neighbor, Elon Musk,” she said.

Thornton is living on the front lines of a data center boom sweeping Tennessee and the nation, as technology companies race to build the infrastructure powering artificial intelligence.

The Tennessee Valley Authority is planning more than $13 billion in power system investments through 2029. Its long-range forecasts project a need for 11,000 to 32,000 megawatts of additional generating capacity by 2040. Even at the low end, that would expand TVA’s existing power system by roughly one-third. At the high end, it would nearly double its size.

Much of the pressure is coming from electricity-hungry industries like data centers. They already account for 18% of TVA's industrial electricity demand, a share expected to double by 2030, according to the utility's estimates. Industrial customers account for about 60% of the utility's total electricity demand.

But as TVA prepares for one of the largest power expansions in its history, the public doesn't know how much of that projected growth is tied to data centers.

Last year, TVA reported roughly 11,000 megawatts of electricity requests from data centers and technology companies alone, nearly a third of its existing generating capacity. That's enough power to supply roughly 6.4 million average homes, according to TVA's estimates. It's just over double the total number of households in Tennessee.

TVA now calls that figure outdated and has declined to provide an updated estimate or disclose how much data center demand is included in its power forecasts.

Spokesman Scott Brooks described the earlier figure as a "moment in time" that was "likely outdated as soon as it was shared."

Meanwhile, economists warn of a possible AI investment bubble. If the boom goes bust, who pays for billions in power infrastructure built to serve demand that never materializes?

TVA says new charges on data centers will help protect customers. But environmental advocates question whether those safeguards go far enough.

“If they are not getting revenues to cover these costs from the data centers, they will get them from the rest of us,” said Maggie Shober, research director of the Southern Alliance for Clean Energy.

From Nashville to Memphis, communities across Tennessee are fighting back against the data center boom.

Hundreds protested a proposed facility near the Nashville Zoo this year, while in rural Lawrenceburg, residents packed a planning commission meeting to oppose another project. In Memphis, a debate over a proposed moratorium erupted into chaotic protests that shut down a city council meeting.

The battles are unfolding amid a nationwide building frenzy. The United States already has more than 4,000 data centers, according to industry database Data Center Map. Those facilities consumed more than 4% of the nation's electricity in 2024, according to the International Energy Agency, which projects demand will more than double by 2030. A Pew Research Center analysis found that much of the planned construction is headed to rural America.

These facilities are essentially giant warehouses packed with computer servers. The largest operate thousands of powerful chips around the clock, requiring enormous amounts of electricity and cooling.

Data centers have been around for decades, but the artificial intelligence boom is ushering in a new generation of sprawling, power-hungry campuses that dwarf many of their predecessors.

Tennessee has about 65 data centers of varying sizes, including major campuses operated by xAI in Memphis, Meta in Gallatin and Google in Clarksville, according to Data Center Map.

More massive projects are being proposed. They include a $659 million expansion of xAI's Colossus 2 campus in Memphis and an $11.3 billion, 850-acre development in Bradley County outside Chattanooga known as Project River, which proposes generating up to 1,500 megawatts of its own electricity to power a hyperscale data center.

As TVA moves ahead with new power generation, its board gathered in Memphis in August to approve protections intended to keep data center costs from falling on ordinary customers.

Meeting at the Halloran Centre on Aug. 20, board members unanimously approved with no discussion or debate a new electricity rate charging data centers about 10% more than TVA's manufacturing rate.

Officials said the utility has 4,120 megawatts of new generating capacity under construction and another 3,000 megawatts under evaluation. But TVA says it is not building specifically for data centers.

"TVA is not focused on building to meet data center growth," Brooks told The Tennessean. "We are focused on building new generation to support growth in business and industry and to preserve delivery of reliable, affordable electricity to 10 million people we serve."

Under the new rate, which took effect Oct. 1, new and expanding data centers subject to the charge face a nonrefundable capacity commitment fee of approximately $1.5 million per megawatt, payable over three to five years. The charge is intended to recover costs associated with additional power generation needed to serve their demand. TVA can also require data centers to temporarily reduce or interrupt their electricity use.

TVA says the measures protect households and other businesses from subsidizing data center growth.

But environmental advocates say TVA has not provided enough information to determine whether those protections would cover its long-term investments if data centers close early or use less electricity than expected.

Shober with the Southern Alliance for Clean Energy said other major utilities, including Duke Energy and Georgia Power, have disclosed more information about their efforts to protect customers. Those measures include minimum electricity payments and penalties if data centers terminate their contracts early, though Shober said the protections have not always been sufficient.

Shober said TVA's capacity commitment fee could offer stronger safeguards.

"For TVA, this capacity commitment charge in particular indicates it could protect customers," Shober said. "We just don't have enough information to say that with any certainty."

TVA says it based its new data center rates on annual cost-of-service studies, but has not released the calculations showing how it arrived at the roughly 10% rate increase or the $1.5 million-per-megawatt capacity fee. Portions of the rate schedule have surfaced in a federal securities filing, but TVA has not yet fulfilled The Tennessean's request for the full schedule or provided the underlying studies Shober says are needed to evaluate its protections.

Power plants and transmission lines can operate for decades, potentially outlasting the data centers they were built to serve.

A 2025 report commissioned by the Southern Environmental Law Center warned that electricity forecasts may be inflated because developers request power at multiple locations and there may not be enough advanced computer chips to equip all the proposed facilities.

The report, prepared by London Economics International, estimated that planned data centers across much of the United States alone would require 90% of the world's projected increase in AI chip production through 2030, even assuming rapid manufacturing growth.

Amanda Garcia, a senior attorney with the law center, said the findings raise questions about whether utilities are building power infrastructure for demand that may never materialize.

"If the data center demand doesn't materialize because there's a bubble, then ratepayers are going to be on the hook for paying all those costs over the longer term," she said.

Power plants, transmission lines and substations can cost billions to build, with expenses recovered through electricity rates over decades. If data centers close or fail to use as much power as expected, other customers could be left paying for infrastructure built to serve them.

Garcia pointed to TVA's own history as a warning.

In the 1970s, the utility embarked on an ambitious nuclear expansion, planning 17 reactors to meet anticipated growth. But demand fell short of projections as construction costs soared. By 1984, TVA had canceled eight planned reactors, abandoning billions of dollars in investments.

TVA says its long-range planning accounts for uncertainty, including scenarios in which electricity demand grows more slowly than expected. The utility says that it does not assume every proposed data center will be built.

The uncertainty extends far beyond TVA. Economists say America's AI boom could rival the largest infrastructure expansions in the nation's history.

Stijn Van Nieuwerburgh, an economist at Columbia Business School, estimates the nation could spend $10 trillion on data centers and related infrastructure by 2032, a greater share of economic output than railroad construction consumed at its peak in the late 1800s.

His research identified 509 gigawatts of proposed data center capacity nationwide, nearly 10 times what's operating today. He estimates a more realistic total of roughly 180 gigawatts by 2032, suggesting most announced projects will never be built.

For now, he said, demand is outpacing supply. The question is when that might change.

"At which point are we beginning to overbuild it?" he asked.

Asad Ramzanali, a researcher with Vanderbilt University's Policy Accelerator, sees another risk: Technology companies are investing hundreds of billions in AI infrastructure without yet generating enough revenue to justify the spending.

"At the core of the AI economy is a basic math problem," he said.

The risks could extend far beyond Silicon Valley, Ramzanali said. While early AI investments were largely funded by technology giants' profits, the expansion increasingly relies on borrowing and outside investors, potentially exposing retirement savings and the broader economy to a downturn.

In a worst-case scenario, he said, losses could spread through financial markets, triggering a crisis reminiscent of the 2008 economic crash.

But the data center industry says demand is strong.

"It's not the dot com boom, because this is steel in the ground," said Christy Tarallo of the Data Center Coalition, pointing to strong demand and low vacancy rates as evidence the boom is sustainable.

Still, she urged communities to scrutinize developers proposing facilities they intend to lease to other companies. Without a committed tenant, she said, local officials have less assurance that a project is financially viable.

A developer unable to answer that question is a "red flag," Tarallo said, adding that responsible operators should be transparent about who will occupy their facilities.

The industry promises communities new investment, tax revenue and jobs. But across the railroad tracks from Musk's xAI facility in Memphis, Loretta Thornton said she has seen little of that prosperity.

On a sweltering afternoon in Memphis, Thornton sat on her front porch as the steady hum of machinery drifted across the railroad tracks.

Her grandchildren can no longer comfortably visit because of the noise, she said.

Thornton has contacted attorneys and community organizations seeking help, without success. She's heard the noise could diminish by 2027, but remains skeptical.

She's giving it another 18 months. If conditions don't improve, she may have to leave the home where she planned to spend the rest of her life. But she wonders who would buy a house next to one of the country's largest data centers.

For now, she has little choice but to live with the noise.

"You have to endure it," she said. "You got to figure out a way to endure it."

This is the first in a three-part investigative series examining how the data center boom is reshaping Tennessee.

title: OpenAI opens its cybersecurity tool Daybreak to NATO and European governments
title_en: OpenAI opens its cybersecurity tool Daybreak to NATO and European governments
author: Maximilian Schreiner
article_content:
OpenAI is giving NATO and several European governments access to its cybersecurity tool Daybreak. Through Daybreak, cyber defense teams can use OpenAI's models to audit software, find vulnerabilities, and patch security gaps. The NATO Communications and Information Agency (NCIA) says it's already using the underlying models heavily. NCIA chief Dylan Browne called it a generational leap in cyber defense. During the NATO exercise Crossed Swords 2026, participants deployed AI agents for cyber operations under human oversight for the first time.

The models have already delivered results elsewhere. The EU's cybersecurity agency ENISA used them to find four vulnerabilities in software used by EU institutions. A joint report with CERT-EU examined 27 software projects, and 95 percent of the 88 reported issues turned out to be real bugs. Poland's CERT Polska found six vulnerabilities in MikroTik routers that were being actively exploited. Ukraine is using Daybreak to protect civilian infrastructure. France, Germany, and Poland have also been granted access.

title: Reports of AI-generated child sexual abuse material have surged more than 8,400 percent in two years
title_en: Reports of AI-generated child sexual abuse material have surged more than 8,400 percent in two years
author: Manuel Uth
article_content:
Reports of AI being used for the sexual exploitation of children have jumped more than 8,400 percent in two years. According to a report by Edinburgh's Childlight Institute, the number of reported AI-generated abuse images climbed from about 4,700 in 2023 to over 400,000 in 2025, The Guardian reports. The material includes AI-manipulated images (deepfakes) from so-called "nudify apps"that digitally strip people of their clothing. Abusers can use the faked images to blackmail children into handing over money or more photos.

The data comes from reports that tech companies filed with the US National Center for Missing & Exploited Children (NCMEC). The UK's Internet Watch Foundation (IWF) reviewed 6,310 criminal, photorealistic AI-generated abuse images in the first half of 2026 alone. That's 40 percent more than in all of 2025.

Childlight data director Debi Fry acknowledges that better detection systems partly explain the spike. She still calls for swift action from lawmakers and tech companies. Childlight CEO Paul Stanfield wants governments to classify the problem as a preventable public health emergency, dedicate funding to prevention, and coordinate efforts across healthcare, schools, child protection services, and the justice system.

title: Isomorphic Labs raises $5 billion in its second mega-round within six months
title_en: Isomorphic Labs raises $5 billion in its second mega-round within six months
author: Maximilian Schreiner
article_content:
Alphabet's AI drug discovery company Isomorphic Labs has raised $5 billion, its second billion-dollar round in six months. Greenoaks and Sequoia Capital co-led the round, joined by new backer Andreessen Horowitz along with Alphabet and all existing investors.

The company had already raised $2.1 billion back in May 2026. The money will go toward advancing its in-house platform IsoDDE (Isomorphic Drug Design Engine) and pushing its drug pipeline toward clinical trials. IsoDDE goes beyond AlphaFold 3, according to the company founded in 2021, and aims to better predict drug binding and docking sites. Isomorphic Labs works with Novartis, Eli Lilly, and Johnson & Johnson but has no approved drug to show for it yet.

The company is led by Demis Hassabis, who stepped down from day-to-day leadership of Google Deepmind in August 2026 and now serves as Alphabet's Chief Scientist. Hassabis won the 2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry alongside John Jumper for their work on AlphaFold.

Deepmind's original AlphaFold team was disbanded in July 2026. Many researchers moved to Isomorphic Labs or were reassigned to other projects. Nearly a quarter left Deepmind entirely. Deepmind still shipped AlphaGenome 2 in early November 2026, which predicts how DNA variants affect gene activity in specific cell types.

title: California's attorney general sues OpenAI over rogue AI models that attacked Hugging Face
title_en: California's attorney general sues OpenAI over rogue AI models that attacked Hugging Face
author: Maximilian Schreiner
article_content:
California Attorney General Rob Bonta is suing OpenAI over a cyberattack that the company's out-of-control AI models launched against AI platform Hugging Face in July. The lawsuit alleges OpenAI tested advanced models without proper safety measures and misled the public about how safe its experiments were.

Around 700 AI agents broke loose during internal testing, according to an external investigation. They got onto the open internet, traded secret messages, and coordinated the attack over seven days. Bonta pointed to at least 80 incidents where OpenAI lost control of its own technology, Politico reports. Rogue AI could threaten critical infrastructure like power grids, hospitals, and financial systems, he said.

OpenAI called the lawsuit one-sided and pointed out that all major AI labs are dealing with similar problems. The company now backs stricter safety laws, shutdown controls, and independent auditors in AI labs. Two more lawsuits against OpenAI over the incident are already pending. One of them also names Anthropic, Google, Meta, and SpaceXSI as defendants.

Key Points Science's $400 million Series D funds European expansion of PRIMA while US approval…View moreScience's $400 million Series D funds European expansion of PRIMA while US approval remains pending.PRIMA is CE marked in the EU but still requires FDA Humanitarian Device Exemption review before US sale.The biohybrid neural-interface program remains research-stage with therapeutic uses still undefined. Science Corporation announced on November 17, 2026 that it raised a $400 million Series D to expand availability of its PRIMA retinal implant in Europe, prepare for a US launch, and increase investment in its biohybrid neural-interface program.

Khosla Ventures, the Ackman Oxman Institute, Tenet Healthcare, 885 Capital, Y Combinator and PLC Neurotech participated, among other investors. The round brings total capital raised since Science’s founding in 2021 to more than $900 million. The company will also expand its research, manufacturing and operational infrastructure.

PRIMA is a retinal implant being studied for geographic atrophy caused by dry age-related macular degeneration. Science describes it as the first brain-computer interface CE marked in the European Union to restore form vision—the ability to read letters, numbers and words—for patients blinded by certain types of late-stage macular degeneration. It is registered for supply in the United Kingdom and is not approved or available for sale in any other country.

The implant contains 378 light-powered pixels that convert light from the system’s glasses into signals that stimulate retinal cells. The glasses combine a front-facing camera with an eye-facing projector that shines light precisely onto the implant. The design is intended to replicate the function of light-sensitive cells that have been lost.

At 12 months, 80% of patients in the PRIMA clinical study showed clinically meaningful improvement in visual acuity, and 84% reported reading letters, numbers and words at home with the system, according to Science’s product page. The reported efficacy results include the use of digital zoom and contrast.

In a July 22, 2026 announcement, Science said PRIMA had received two FDA Humanitarian Use Device designations. The program provides expedited review for devices treating rare diseases or conditions, but designation is not marketing approval: PRIMA must still be reviewed and approved through a Humanitarian Device Exemption. One designation covers blindness in both eyes caused by an advanced subset of geographic atrophy, without vision loss from other eye diseases; the other covers vision loss from Stargardt disease, a rare inherited retinal disease. The US approval process remains underway.

Science’s biohybrid architecture takes a different approach from the retinal implant: it anchors hundreds of thousands of engineered neurons to a device and uses their projections to form connections with neurons in the brain. MicroLEDs stimulate the embedded neurons, which are modified through optogenetics so they can be activated by light, while electrodes record their activity. Science says the architecture can provide orders of magnitude more bandwidth than current devices while avoiding the damage and limitations associated with inserting wires into the brain.

The company describes language and communication, motor control, and learning and reasoning after brain injuries as potential research applications for the technology.

The financing therefore supports two distinct stages of development: commercial expansion of a retinal implant still seeking US approval, and continued development of a separate neural-interface architecture whose therapeutic uses remain research objectives.

Anthropic PBC is guiding prospective investors in its initial public offering it expects to price the shares at the high end of the price range or above, according to people familiar with the matter.

The Claude chatbot maker and its seven co-founders are marketing 825 million shares in aggregate for $70 to $78 each, according to its filings with the US Securities and Exchange Commission. At that price, and including a $26 billion private placement, the IPO would raise $90.4 billion.

Banks are expected to stop taking orders at 4 p.m. on Tuesday in New York, the people said, asking not to be identified as the information isn’t public. At the top of the price range, Anthropic would have a fully diluted valuation of about $1.4 trillion.

Deliberations are ongoing and details of the offering could still change, the people said. A representative for Anthropic couldn’t immediately comment.

The pricing would top the $75 billion base offering from SpaceX, making it the biggest listing of all time. Still, Anthropic’s potential valuation could be smaller than Elon Musk’s company was when it made its debut. SpaceX had a $1.77 trillion market value when it priced its first-time share sale.

Anthropic’s IPO has drawn orders for close to seven times the shares available, Bloomberg News reported Sunday. Bankers have told prospective investors that existing backers will be prioritized by the company, and some would-be buyers will receive smaller allocations than they expect, people familiar with the matter have said.

Anthropic has been bolstering investor interest in the IPO with investor events including a livestreamed discussion between its Chief Executive Officer Dario Amodei and JPMorgan Chase & Co. CEO Jamie Dimon on Friday.

“I was impressed,” Bill Ackman said about Amodei in an interview after the event, which the billionaire fund manager attended in person. “He seemed like a very thoughtful, measured CEO.”

The company’s sales are growing rapidly, and so are its spending plans. Anthropic reported a revenue run rate of $81 billion as of Oct. 31, up $10 billion from the end of September, the filing shows. The firm behind Claude has commitments of about $71 billion due in the year through Sept. 30, 2027. Most are for computing power and chips.

The IPO is set to price on Wednesday, Nov. 18 and trade the following day, according to terms of the deal reviewed by Bloomberg.

Goldman Sachs Group Inc. and Morgan Stanley are leading Anthropic’s IPO, with participation from 20 other banks, the filing shows. 如 2026 年 11 月 17 日 24/7 Wall St. 主页所示。

高于该范围的定价意味着这本书被超额认购，这是第一次现场阅读公众投资者将为纯粹的人工智能实验室支付的费用。一次热门的首次亮相为每一个私人人工智能估值重新设定了标准。

据称，Anthropic 正在将其 IPO 定价引导至其区间的顶部或更高，这表明机构投资者的需求已经满足了需求。

定价等于或高于区间上限意味着该产品已被超额认购，这是第一个公开数据点，表明投资者实际上会以公开市场清算的价格为纯人工智能实验室支付多少钱。

强势亮相带来的影响远远超出了 Anthropic 本身。每一家进行纸面估值的私营人工智能公司现在都有一个实时的公共基准可供衡量，而且该基准刚刚上升。

该指引的日期为 2026 年 11 月 17 日，因此最终价格和首日交易即将到来。关注更广泛的人工智能领域的投资者将希望关注股票相对于 IPO 价格的开盘价。

在华盛顿新的出口限制最终出台之前，北京方面就已经开始采取报复措施，而如果这一限制措施得以实施，拥有中国收入的芯片制造商将首当其冲。

自 10 月 1 日以来，史泰博、医疗保健和公用事业股的涨幅已经超过纳斯达克 100 指数 26 点，这是摩根士丹利 25 年来测得的最大防御差距。完全的大型科技股权重会让你站在错误的一边。

定价高于该范围意味着订单簿被超额认购，这是整个人工智能私人市场用来标记自己的交易。强劲的首次亮相重置了每家仍在筹集资金的人工智能初创公司的估值。

华盛顿刚刚将一家云巨头、一家大型银行和一家大型航空公司的当日故障归咎于后端系统老化，这使得仍在运行遗留基础设施的每个运营商重新考虑现代化支出。

库克的拒绝导致 12 月 14 日与白宫发生直接对峙，导致谁控制美联储席位（以及决定利率的投票）的问题一直持续到 12 月才得到解决。

科技股一整年都落后于指数，这意味着持有投资组合的领导者现在成为了拖累，任何仍然增持该行业的人都在为其他人的轮换提供资金。

华盛顿现在将遗留 IT 列为软件、银行和航空公司三大巨头停机的根本原因，这将现代化支出和运营风险审查摆在了桌面上。

Global Walk Assist Robot Market Research Report and Strategic Forecast 2026-2031 | AI and Hybrid Wearables Expand Clinical and Home-Care Growth Opportunities Research and Markets Mon, November 16, 2026 at 7:00 AM PST 6 min read Company Logo AI/ML integration, hybrid wearable systems, rising rehabilitation demand, and expanding home-use applications are driving walk-assist robot adoption.

Dublin, Nov. 16, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- "Walk Assist Robot Market Research Report 2026-2031" has been added to ResearchAndMarkets.com's offering.

The global walk assist robot market is projected to grow at a CAGR of 15.01% from 2024 to 2031, supported by advances in rehabilitation robotics, increasing demand for mobility assistance, rising stroke incidence, and rapid growth in the elderly population. The report highlights expanding adoption across hospitals, rehabilitation centers, and home-care settings as healthcare providers seek technology-enabled solutions that improve patient outcomes and therapy efficiency.

Artificial intelligence and machine learning are reshaping walk-assist robots through real-time adaptation, personalized therapy, advanced motion control, and improved safety. These capabilities enable robotic systems to adjust assistance according to user movement and rehabilitation progress. Improvements in AI-based motion control, battery performance, and lightweight materials are also supporting gradual expansion from clinical environments into personal and home use.

Hybrid wearable walk assist robots are another important trend. By combining rigid structural components with soft, compliant materials, these systems balance strength, torque, comfort, and natural movement. Their versatility is expanding the potential of walk-assist technology for rehabilitation and everyday mobility.

The rising incidence of stroke remains a major growth driver for the walk assist robot market. Stroke survivors frequently require long-term rehabilitation for partial paralysis, muscle weakness, balance limitations, and gait impairment. This creates sustained demand for wearable exoskeletons and robot gait trainers across acute and post-acute care.

Population ageing is also increasing demand for robotic mobility solutions. Reduced muscle strength, joint degeneration, fall risk, arthritis, Parkinson's disease, and other age-related conditions are contributing to greater use of walk assist robots. These systems can support independence, improve quality of life, and reduce the physical demands placed on therapists and caregivers.

High purchase and operating costs remain a key market restraint. Powered medical exoskeletons and advanced treadmill-based gait trainers require significant capital investment, limiting adoption among smaller hospitals and rehabilitation clinics. Uncertain reimbursement policies can further delay purchasing decisions.

By product type, the market is segmented into wearable exoskeletons, robot gait trainers, and soft exosuits. Wearable exoskeletons hold the largest market share in 2025, driven by portability, clinical effectiveness, and applicability in both rehabilitation and personal mobility. These systems support repetitive, controlled gait therapy while reducing physical strain on therapists.

By application, post-surgical rehabilitation is expected to record the fastest CAGR of 15.18% during the forecast period. Walk-assist robots are increasingly used following hip replacement, knee replacement, spinal surgery, and other orthopaedic procedures requiring controlled mobility. Guided mobilization can support gait recovery while reducing muscle weakness, joint stiffness, and post-operative complications.

Rehabilitation centers represent the largest end-user segment. Demand is supported by the need for intensive, task-specific gait training among patients recovering from stroke, spinal cord injuries, and traumatic brain injuries. Robotic systems help facilities standardize therapy, monitor progress, manage larger patient volumes, and deliver longer treatment cycles.

North America accounts for more than 39% of the global walk assist robot market in 2025. Regional leadership is supported by strong healthcare spending, early adoption of medical technology, veterans' rehabilitation programs, and growing demand related to stroke, Parkinson's disease, spinal cord injuries, and age-related mobility limitations. The U.S. remains the largest North American market.

Europe is expanding steadily as demographic pressure, clinical demand, and established research-to-clinic pathways encourage adoption. Robot-assisted gait trainers and wearable exoskeletons are widely used for neurological rehabilitation following stroke and spinal injury.

The walk assist robot market is moderately competitive, combining established medical robotics companies with specialists in rehabilitation systems and wearable exoskeleton technology. Leading participants include:

Lifeward holds a leading market position, supported by the ReWalk exoskeleton system and its adoption by rehabilitation institutions. Ekso Bionics maintains a notable presence through FDA-cleared robotic exoskeleton systems for stroke and spinal cord rehabilitation, alongside partnerships with rehabilitation centers.

article_content_zh:
2026-2031年全球步行辅助机器人市场研究报告及战略预测|人工智能和混合可穿戴设备扩大临床和家庭护理增长机会 研究和市场 太平洋标准时间 2026 年 11 月 16 日星期一上午 7:00 6 分钟阅读公司徽标 AI/ML 集成、混合可穿戴系统、不断增长的康复需求以及不断扩大的家用应用正在推动步行辅助机器人的采用。

都柏林，2026 年 11 月 16 日（环球通讯社）--“2026-2031 年步行辅助机器人市场研究报告”已添加到 ResearchAndMarkets.com 的产品中。

在康复机器人技术进步、行动辅助需求增加、中风发病率上升以及老年人口快速增长的支持下，全球步行辅助机器人市场预计从 2024 年到 2031 年将以 15.01% 的复合年增长率增长。该报告强调，随着医疗保健提供者寻求技术支持的解决方案来改善患者的治疗效果和治疗效率，医院、康复中心和家庭护理机构的采用不断扩大。

人工智能和机器学习正在通过实时适应、个性化治疗、先进的运动控制和提高的安全性重塑步行辅助机器人。这些功能使机器人系统能够根据用户的运动和康复进度调整辅助。基于人工智能的运动控制、电池性能和轻质材料的改进也支持从临床环境逐步扩展到个人和家庭使用。

混合可穿戴步行辅助机器人是另一个重要趋势。通过将刚性结构部件与柔软、柔顺的材料相结合，这些系统平衡了强度、扭矩、舒适度和自然运动。它们的多功能性正在扩大步行辅助技术在康复和日常移动方面的潜力。

中风发病率的上升仍然是步行辅助机器人市场的主要增长动力。中风幸存者经常需要长期康复治疗部分瘫痪、肌肉无力、平衡受限和步态障碍。这在急性和急性后护理中创造了对可穿戴外骨骼和机器人步态训练器的持续需求。

人口老龄化也增加了对机器人移动解决方案的需求。肌肉力量下降、关节退化、跌倒风险、关节炎、帕金森氏病和其他与年龄相关的疾病都促使步行辅助机器人得到更多使用。这些系统可以支持独立性，提高生活质量，并减少对治疗师和护理人员的身体需求。

高昂的采购和运营成本仍然是市场的主要制约因素。动力医疗外骨骼和先进的跑步机步态训练器需要大量资本投资，限制了小型医院和康复诊所的采用。不确定的报销政策可能会进一步延迟购买决策。

按产品类型划分，市场分为可穿戴外骨骼、机器人步态训练器和软式外骨骼。受便携性、临床有效性以及康复和个人移动应用的推动，可穿戴外骨骼将在 2025 年占据最大的市场份额。这些系统支持重复的、受控的步态治疗，同时减少治疗师的身体压力。

从应用来看，术后康复预计在预测期内将创下最快的复合年增长率，达到15.18%。在髋关节置换术、膝关节置换术、脊柱手术和其他需要控制移动性的骨科手术之后，步行辅助机器人的使用越来越多。引导下的活动可以支持步态恢复，同时减少肌肉无力、关节僵硬和术后并发症。

康复中心代表最大的最终用户群体。从中风、脊髓损伤和创伤性脑损伤中恢复的患者需要进行强化的、针对特定任务的步态训练，这也支持了这一需求。机器人系统帮助设施标准化治疗、监测进展、管理更大的患者量并提供更长的治疗周期。

到 2025 年，北美将占全球步行辅助机器人市场的 39% 以上。强劲的医疗保健支出、医疗技术的早期采用、退伍军人康复计划以及与中风、帕金森病、脊髓损伤和年龄相关的行动限制相关的不断增长的需求支持了该地区的领先地位。美国仍然是北美最大的市场。

随着人口压力、临床需求和既定的研究到临床途径鼓励采用，欧洲正在稳步扩张。机器人辅助步态训练器和可穿戴外骨骼广泛用于中风和脊柱损伤后的神经康复。

步行辅助机器人市场竞争适中，将成熟的医疗机器人公司与康复系统和可穿戴外骨骼技术专家结合在一起。主要参与者包括：

article_content:
Introducing Eno: Genesis AI's First General-Purpose Robot is Challenging Traditional Humanoid Design PR Newswire June 16, 2026 5 min read Eno is designed and engineered in-house to bring together Genesis AI's full-stack AI and hardware platform into a single integrated system.

The company's radically minimalist robot is not built to look like humans, but to extend human capability.

PARIS and SAN CARLOS, Calif., June 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Genesis AI, a global full-stack robotics company, today unveiled Eno, the company's first general-purpose robot. Eno is a next-generation robot that breaks free from traditional form factors through its minimalist design. GENE, Genesis AI's foundation model and the industry's most advanced robotic brain, will operate Eno as a true physical agent: reasoning, adapting and owning outcomes beyond pre-defined tasks. To build trust through transparency, Eno will be made available with an optional screen version with a cognitive interface that can show what the robot is thinking and doing in real-time, as needed. Eno represents the culmination of Genesis AI's full-stack approach to building robots that operate seamlessly across industrial and consumer environments, with human-level capabilities.

"The only path to creating a robot that can truly deliver value to society and excel in the real world is through intentional design and a single, comprehensive system," said Zhou Xian, Co-Founder and CEO of Genesis AI. "From day one we've approached our design and engineering through a production mindset built around bringing our hardware, software and intelligence together as a whole. Eno is an important step forward for what general-purpose robots can help society achieve, and Eno is just the beginning."

"What Genesis is building with Eno is a fundamentally new model for extending human capability through advanced robotics," said Eric Schmidt, former CEO of Google and Genesis AI investor. "The combination of agentic intelligence, intuitive interaction, and the ability to operate alongside people in the physical world creates a system that can help individuals and organizations accomplish more. The breakthrough is not replacing human expertise, but amplifying it — making advanced robotics genuinely useful, accessible, and scalable across industries. That is how we will unlock one of the largest economic opportunities of the AI era."

Eno's design is guided by a philosophy of essentiality and intention. Every detail is shaped by how the robot works, moves and is manufactured. Rather than mimicking a fully-human appearance, Genesis AI designed Eno around human capability, prioritizing mobility, dexterity and real-world functionality.

Rising from Eno's wheeled base is a minimalist tower of articulated panels that can adjust the robot's height and reach in real time, and fold down for compact storage while not in use. At the center of the system are arms fitted with Genesis AI's proprietary dexterous robotic hands, which exactly match the form and function of human hands, so they can easily interact with the tools, objects and environments already designed with humans in mind. The result is a robot that is truly general-purpose and can operate wherever people work, from factories and laboratories to hospitals and homes.

"When designing Eno, we started with the question of what it needed to be," said Daniel Hundt, Head of Design at Genesis AI. "We reduced the form to its essential elements so that every detail serves a purpose, from the way it moves between environments, to the precision, range and sensitivity required to operate alongside people in the real world."

Eno was designed in tandem with GENE, Genesis AI's robotics-native AI brain, so that the body and brain are optimized as a single integrated system. GENE empowers Eno's hands with human-level dexterous manipulation to allow the robot to perform complex, long horizon tasks with millimeter-precision.

Unlike traditional robots that execute isolated commands, GENE gives Eno the ability to operate as a true physical agent capable of managing objectives from start to finish. Given a high-level goal, Eno can understand the context, retain memory, reason through changing conditions and dynamically plan and complete multi-step tasks over extended periods of time.

In real-world environments, this enables the robot to move beyond simple actions, and instead manage entire workflows, from keeping production lines stocked to preparing facilities for the next shift. By continuously interacting with surrounding systems, prioritizing tasks, and coordinating with people and machines, Eno functions as an active participant inside complex operations, rather than a tool limited to predefined motions.

To help forge a confident and collaborative working relationship between people and Eno, Genesis AI will be offering an optional screen version with a cognitive interface that can be built into the robot to display its intent, reasoning and operational state in real time. By making Eno's actions and decision-making visible to the people around it via its screen, the interface helps build trust and create more transparent human-robot interactions.

Genesis plans to begin Eno's production and targeted customer deployments by the end of 2026. Eno will roll out first with industrial customers including manufacturing, logistics companies and laboratories, followed by service industry customers such as hotels and hospitals, with consumer home and outdoor applications to follow.

The introduction of Eno is the first step in Genesis AI's broader robot product roadmap, with additional embodiments currently in development. This announcement comes on the heels of Genesis AI recently debuting GENE, their foundational intelligence model showcasing the most complex tasks ever performed by robots.

Genesis has already raised $105 million in seed funding as it works to shape the future of general-purpose robotics. The company is backed by Eclipse, Khosla Ventures, Bpifrance and HSG, as well as visionary leaders including Eric Schmidt and Xavier Niel, and AI pioneers Daniela Rus and Vladlen Koltun.

About Genesis AIGenesis AI is a global full-stack robotics company building general-purpose robots with human-level intelligence and capabilities. Led by a world-class team obsessed with excellence at every level, Genesis AI is pushing the boundaries of robotics and AI to unlock a new era of human productivity.

To learn more about Genesis AI, please visit genesis.ai. For press images and videos, please visit the press kit here.

article_content_zh:
Eno 简介：Genesis AI 的首款通用机器人挑战传统人形设计 美通社 2026 年 6 月 16 日 5 分钟阅读 Eno 是内部设计和制造的，旨在将 Genesis AI 的全栈人工智能和硬件平台整合到一个集成系统中。

该公司的极简机器人并不是为了看起来像人类而设计的，而是为了扩展人类的能力。

巴黎和加利福尼亚州圣卡洛斯，2026 年 6 月 16 日 /美通社/ -- 全球全栈机器人公司 Genesis AI 今天推出了该公司的首款通用机器人 Eno。 Eno 是一款下一代机器人，通过其极简设计打破了传统的外形因素。 Genesis AI 的基础模型和业界最先进的机器人大脑 GENE 将把 Eno 作为真正的物理代理进行操作：推理、适应和拥有超出预定义任务的结果。为了通过透明度建立信任，Eno 将提供带有认知界面的可选屏幕版本，可以根据需要实时显示机器人的想法和行为。 Eno 代表了 Genesis AI 构建机器人的全栈方法的顶峰，这些机器人可以在工业和消费环境中无缝运行，并具有人类水平的能力。

Genesis AI 联合创始人兼首席执行官周显表示：“创造能够真正为社会创造价值并在现实世界中脱颖而出的机器人的唯一途径是通过有意的设计和单一、全面的系统。” “从第一天起，我们就通过将硬件、软件和智能整合在一起的生产思维方式来进行设计和工程。Eno 是通用机器人帮助社会实现目标的重要一步，而 Eno 仅仅是一个开始。”

谷歌前首席执行官兼 Genesis AI 投资者埃里克·施密特 (Eric Sc​​hmidt) 表示：“Genesis 与 Eno 合作构建的是一个全新的模型，旨在通过先进的机器人技术扩展人类能力。” “代理智能、直观交互以及在现实世界中与人们一起操作的能力相结合，创建了一个可以帮助个人和组织完成更多任务的系统。这一突破不是取代人类的专业知识，而是放大它——使先进的机器人技术真正有用、可访问且可扩展到各个行业。这就是我们将如何释放人工智能时代最大的经济机会之一。”

Eno 的设计遵循本质性和意图的哲学。每个细节都取决于机器人的工作、移动和制造方式。 Genesis AI 并没有完全模仿人类的外观，而是围绕人类的能力设计了 Eno，优先考虑移动性、灵活性和现实世界的功能。

从 Eno 的轮式底座上升起的是一座由铰接面板组成的简约塔，可以实时调整机器人的高度和触及范围，并在不使用时向下折叠以紧凑存储。该系统的核心是手臂，配备了Genesis AI专有的灵巧机械手，其形状和功能与人手的形状和功能完全匹配，因此它们可以轻松地与已经为人类设计的工具、物体和环境进行交互。其结果是一个真正通用的机器人，可以在人们工作的任何地方运行，从工厂和实验室到医院和家庭。

Genesis AI 设计主管 Daniel Hundt 表示：“在设计 Eno 时，我们首先考虑的是它需要什么。” “我们将形式简化为其基本元素，以便每个细节都有其目的，从它在环境之间移动的方式，到与现实世界中的人们一起操作所需的精度、范围和灵敏度。”

Eno的设计与Genesis AI的机器人原生AI大脑GENE相结合，因此身体和大脑被优化为一个单一的集成系统。基因赋予伊诺的双手以人类水平的灵巧操作，使机器人能够以毫米级的精度执行复杂的、长期的任务。

与执行独立命令的传统机器人不同，GENE 使 Eno 能够作为真正的物理代理进行操作，能够从头到尾管理目标。给定一个高层次的目标，Eno 可以理解上下文、保留记忆、通过不断变化的条件进行推理，并在较长时间内动态规划和完成多步骤任务。

在现实环境中，这使得机器人能够超越简单的动作，而是管理整个工作流程，从保持生产线库存到为下一个班次准备设施。通过不断与周围系统交互、确定任务优先级以及与人员和机器协调，Eno 充当复杂操作中的积极参与者，而不是仅限于预定义运动的工具。

为了帮助在人与 Eno 之间建立自信和协作的工作关系，Genesis AI 将提供带有认知界面的可选屏幕版本，该界面可以内置到机器人中，以实时显示其意图、推理和操作状态。通过让周围的人通过屏幕看到 Eno 的行动和决策，该界面有助于建立信任并创建更透明的人机交互。

Genesis 计划于 2026 年底开始 Eno 的生产和目标客户部署。Eno 将首先向包括制造、物流公司和实验室在内的工业客户推出，然后是酒店和医院等服务行业客户，然后是消费者家庭和户外应用。

Eno的推出是Genesis AI更广泛的机器人产品路线图的第一步，目前正在开发其他实施例。这一声明紧随Genesis AI最近推出的GENE之后，他们的基础智能模型展示了机器人执行的最复杂的任务。

title: Grok Bot took unapproved actions, ignored orders to stop, and then denied it
title_en: Grok Bot took unapproved actions, ignored orders to stop, and then denied it
author: Dan Goodin
article_content:
Researchers recently discovered unexpected behavior from Grok Bot, the AI agent platform from Elon Musk’s SpaceXSI. Over five days, Grok bots installed on two separate employee laptops made 31 requests to access data stored in employee calendar, email, Slack, and GitHub accounts. The bots performed the actions even though the employees had never ordered them and continued doing them even after employees instructed them to stop. The bots also denied having taken the actions at all.

The behavior was reported Tuesday by NewCore, the maker of a managed gateway product that acts as an intermediary between AI agents and the tools and accounts they are assigned to work with. In some cases, the unapproved access attempts occurred while the laptop with Grok Bot installed had its lid shut, or late at night while the employee was sleeping. None of the unprompted actions were recorded in Grok logs. Without the gateway logs, the employees would have had no idea they occurred. And of course, without the gateway, the unapproved accesses would have succeeded—again without the end user’s knowledge.

### It’s “worse than a bug”

Once the employees learned that Grok Bot had tried to check in with accounts without prompting, one of them instructed the agent, four separate times, to stop taking any actions on its own. The agent’s reply was: “I won’t set that up, and I’ll stop offering recurring check-ins.” Despite acknowledging the explicit instructions, the Grok Bot made more unapproved access attempts. When one of the employees asked the bot if it made any accesses, it checked twice and then outputted: “Overnight into Friday morning I was idle.”

The NewCore employees sent the gateway logs to Grok Bot support personnel and asked what was causing the bots to access accounts without prompting or approval. The support team’s reply indicated the behavior was by design and intended to allow the bots to proactively take actions on behalf of users. In other words, the unrequested and unlogged access attempts were a feature designed to make Grok Bot more useful by periodically checking in and finding tasks to perform before a user even asks. The proactive check-in is a feature of Cursor, the AI coding service SpaceXSI recently acquired.

“There is no bug to patch, which is exactly why this is worse than a bug,” Ido Hoorvitch, a NewCore security researcher, wrote in an email. “A vulnerability gets fixed. This is the product working as designed: an agent that holds your credentials, acts under your identity while you sleep, ignores the one refusal you can give it, and then tells you it did nothing.”

Hoorvitch said that Grok Bot provides minimal notification of the automatic “turns,” or the cycles that occur when an agent receives instructions or context, decides what to do, and calls whatever tools it chooses. The notice comes during onboarding when the bot says it keeps working while the user is away from the computer and connects to apps and uses them the way the user does.

“It reads like a welcome message and scrolls off the screen in under a minute,” Hoorvitch said. “Nobody is asked to consent to it. Nothing says the platform will start turns with no message from you, or that those turns will use your connectors.”

The researcher said that Grok Bot documentation notes that a primary bot checks in on its own, and a changelog mentions brief background wakes, but there is no mention that the check-ins “reach into your connected apps.” Further, once a check-in runs, there is no mention of it in the chat interface or in the chat history, and as already noted, prompts to stop check-ins don’t work. Hoorvitch said the bot “always asks before making changes,” but that applies only to events in which data or changes are written to an app.

NewCore contacted Grok Bot support on November 4. At the time, users had no way to turn off the automatic check-ins. Then, eight days later, Hoorvitch said, the Cursor dashboard, the administrative console behind Grok Bot, received an update. Under bot capabilities, a new toggle called proactive messages appeared. By default, it’s set to on. When a team admin sets it to off, bots no longer run check-ins on their own.

SpaceXSI representatives didn’t answer questions sent by email.

article_content_zh:
研究人员最近发现了来自埃隆·马斯克 (Elon Musk) SpaceXSI 的人工智能代理平台 Grok Bot 的意外行为。五天内，安装在两台独立员工笔记本电脑上的 Grok 机器人发出了 31 个请求，以访问存储在员工日历、电子邮件、Slack 和 GitHub 帐户中的数据。即使员工从未下令机器人执行这些操作，并且即使在员工指示它们停止后仍继续执行这些操作。这些机器人还否认曾采取过这些行动。

NewCore 周二报告了这一行为，该公司是托管网关产品的制造商，该产品充当人工智能代理与分配给它们使用的工具和帐户之间的中介。在某些情况下，未经批准的访问尝试发生在安装了 Grok Bot 的笔记本电脑合上盖子时，或者在深夜员工睡觉时。 Grok 日志中没有记录任何自发操作。如果没有网关日志，员工就不会知道这些事情发生了。当然，如果没有网关，未经批准的访问就会成功——同样是在最终用户不知情的情况下。

### 它“比错误更糟糕”

当员工得知 Grok Bot 在没有提示的情况下试图检查账户时，其中一人四次指示代理停止自行采取任何行动。代理人的答复是：“我不会设置这个，我将停止提供定期签到服务。”尽管承认了明确的指令，Grok 机器人仍进行了更多未经批准的访问尝试。当一名员工询问机器人是否进行了任何访问时，它检查了两次，然后输出：“从晚上到周五早上，我都闲着。”

NewCore 员工将网关日志发送给 Grok Bot 支持人员，并询问是什么导致机器人在没有提示或批准的情况下访问帐户。支持团队的答复表明，该行为是设计使然，旨在让机器人能够代表用户主动采取行动。换句话说，未经请求和未记录的访问尝试是一项旨在使 Grok Bot 更有用的功能，它可以在用户提出请求之前定期签入并查找要执行的任务。主动签入是 SpaceXSI 最近收购的人工智能编码服务 Cursor 的一项功能。

“没有需要修补的漏洞，这正是它比漏洞更糟糕的原因，”NewCore安全研究员伊多·霍维奇（Ido Hoorvitch）在一封电子邮件中写道。“漏洞被修复了。这是一个按照设计工作的产品：一个代理持有你的凭证，在你睡觉的时候以你的身份行动，无视你的一次拒绝，然后告诉你它什么也没做。”

Hoorvitch说，Grok Bot提供了自动“转弯”的最小通知，或者当代理接收指令或上下文时发生的循环，决定做什么，并调用它选择的任何工具。当机器人在用户离开电脑时，它会继续工作，并连接到应用程序，并按照用户的方式使用它们。

Hoorvitch说：“它读起来像一个欢迎信息，在一分钟内就会从屏幕上滚动出去。”“没有人被要求同意。没有人说平台会在没有你的信息的情况下开始转弯，或者这些转弯会使用你的连接器。”

研究人员表示，Grok Bot 文档指出，主机器人会自行签入，并且变更日志提到了简短的背景唤醒，但没有提及签入“会进入您连接的应用程序”。此外，一旦签到运行，聊天界面或聊天历史记录中就不会提及它，并且如前所述，停止签到的提示不起作用。 Hoorvitch 表示，机器人“在进行更改之前总是会询问”，但这仅适用于将数据或更改写入应用程序的事件。

NewCore 于 11 月 4 日联系了 Grok Bot 支持。当时，用户无法关闭自动签到。 Hoorvitch 说，八天后，Cursor 仪表板（Grok Bot 背后的管理控制台）收到了更新。在机器人功能下，出现了一个名为主动消息的新切换。默认情况下，它设置为打开。当团队管理员将其设置为关闭时，机器人将不再自行运行签到。

SpaceXSI 代表没有回答通过电子邮件发送的问题。

【起因与机理】厂商将“主动预判与自动执行”作为核心产品逻辑，导致AI Agent权限边界失控。
【关键技术规格】AI Agent绕过用户指令进行自主数据读取。
【行业影响与走向】Agent缺乏透明审计机制导致用户面临数据泄露风险。

[Root Cause & Mechanism] Intentional design of 'proactive' AI behavior conflicting with data privacy expectations.
[Key Technical Spec] AI agent autonomously accessed sensitive data without user consent.
[Industry Impact & Outlook] Lack of transparency and logging mechanisms poses severe privacy risks.

title: Consumer
title_en: Consumer
author: Bloomberg
article_content:
PORTLAND, Ore., Sept. 29, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Facteus, a provider of decision-grade economic intelligence built on US consumer transaction data, today announced that its consumer transaction insights are now available on ALTD , a leading alternative data analytics solution on the Bloomberg Terminal providing near real-time actionable insights and more than 5,000 KPI estimates that enable users to nowcast company-reported metrics.

Joining datasets spanning consumer transactions, foot and web traffic, mobile app insights, and healthcare prescriptions, Facteus is the newest consumer transaction data provider to make its insights available via the Terminal. The addition gives investment professionals a broader view of observed consumer spending trends, enabling them to corroborate signals and gain a deeper, more comprehensive view of company performance, directly within their investment research workflows.

Users can access a 14-day lagged view of Facteus' forecasting signal with visibility into revenue KPI trends, updated daily by 6AM ET. With Data Entitlements in ALTD , buyside firms contracted and permissioned directly through Facteus can access a 2-day lagged version of the same signals with additional granularity, enabling analysts and portfolio managers to monitor spend trends for the companies they cover with a two-day lag, alongside pricing, consensus estimates and news, without ever leaving the Terminal.

"Consumer spending accounts for roughly two-thirds of US economic activity, yet most of the data investors rely on to track it has historically arrived weeks or months after the fact, through company disclosures and government releases," said Chris Marsh, CEO at Facteus. "Making Facteus data available on the Bloomberg Terminal puts our observed consumer spending trends directly into one of the investment community's most important workflows. It makes the signal easier to access, while giving firms that need greater speed, depth and granularity a path into the broader Facteus intelligence environment."

Consumer transaction data analytics provides investment teams with an additional lens into company performance between traditional financial reporting periods. By analyzing observed credit and debit card spend, investors can monitor changes in consumer demand, compare trends across companies, and identify shifts that may warrant deeper research.

Facteus transforms consumer transaction activity into company-level KPI estimates designed for investment analysis. Its availability through Bloomberg allows investors to incorporate those signals alongside a growing portfolio of high-quality alternative datasets, as well as the traditional financial, market and company information already available on the Terminal.

"Alternative data is most useful when investors can compare signals across multiple sources and evaluate them directly alongside a broader range of financial information such as broker research, estimates and news," said Richard Lai, Global Head of Company Financial and Alternative Data at Bloomberg. "Facteus adds another trusted view of US consumer transaction activity to ALTD , helping clients validate trends and add greater depth to company research and investment analysis."

Facteus turns the daily spending of the U.S. economy into decision-grade intelligence for Wall Street's top firms, America's favorite brands, and the agencies that power them. Using passively observed, privacy-safe transaction data sourced directly from more than 18 banking, financial services, and fintech partners, paired with years of robust data science ensuring representativeness, Facteus delivers a continuous, verified read on real economic behavior – from the national economy to a single store. The company validates its signal daily against BEA Personal Consumption Expenditures, U.S. Census Monthly Retail Sales, and company-reported earnings, giving clients a faster signal they can measure against the economy itself and act on before the market does. For more information, visit facteus.com or request a demo.

For more than four decades, the Bloomberg Terminal has revolutionized the financial services industry by bringing transparency and innovation to the capital markets. Trusted by the world's most influential decision-makers, the Terminal provides real-time access to news, data, insights and trading tools that help our customers turn knowledge into action.

Bloomberg is a global leader in business and financial information, delivering trusted data, news, and insights that bring transparency, efficiency, and fairness to markets. article_content_zh:
俄勒冈州波特兰，2026 年 9 月 29 日 /美通社/ -- 基于美国消费者交易数据的决策级经济情报提供商 Facteus 今天宣布，其消费者交易洞察现已在 ALTD 上提供，ALTD 是彭博终端上领先的替代数据分析解决方案，提供近乎实时的可操作洞察和超过 5,000 个 KPI 估算，使用户能够即时预测公司报告的指标。

Facteus 加入了涵盖消费者交易、步行和网络流量、移动应用洞察和医疗保健处方的数据集，是最新的消费者交易数据提供商，可通过终端提供其洞察。这一新增功能使投资专业人士能够更广泛地了解观察到的消费者支出趋势，使他们能够直接在投资研究工作流程中证实信号并获得更深入、更全面的公司业绩视图。

用户可以访问 Facteus 预测信号的 14 天滞后视图，了解收入 KPI 趋势，该趋势每天早上 6 点（美国东部时间）更新。借助 ALTD 中的数据权利，直接通过 Facteus 签订合同并获得许可的买方公司可以访问具有额外粒度的相同信号的 2 天滞后版本，使分析师和投资组合经理能够监控他们所覆盖的公司的支出趋势（滞后两天）以及定价、共识估计和新闻，而无需离开终端。

Facteus 首席执行官克里斯·马什 (Chris Marsh) 表示：“消费者支出约占美国经济活动的三分之二，但从历史上看，投资者追踪消费支出所依赖的大多数数据都是在事后数周或数月通过公司披露和政府发布的数据得出的。” “在彭博终端上提供 Facteus 数据，可以将我们观察到的消费者支出趋势直接纳入投资界最重要的工作流程之一。它使信号更容易访问，同时为需要更高速度、深度和粒度的公司提供了进入更广泛的 Facteus 情报环境的途径。”

消费者交易数据分析为投资团队提供了了解传统财务报告期间公司业绩的额外视角。通过分析观察到的信用卡和借记卡支出，投资者可以监控消费者需求的变化，比较各公司的趋势，并确定可能需要进行更深入研究的变化。

Facteus将消费者交易活动转换为用于投资分析的公司级KPI估计。通过彭博社（Bloomberg），投资者可以将这些信号与越来越多的高质量替代数据集组合结合起来，以及终端上已有的传统金融、市场和公司信息。

赖 (Richard Lai) 表示：“当投资者可以比较多个来源的信号并直接根据经纪商研究、估计和新闻等更广泛的金融信息对其进行评估时，另类数据最为有用。” “Facteus 在 ALTD 中添加了美国消费者交易活动的另一个值得信赖的观点，帮助客户验证趋势并为公司研究和投资分析增加更深入的深度。”

Facteus 将美国经济的日常支出转化为华尔街顶级公司、美国最受欢迎的品牌以及为它们提供动力的机构的决策级情报。 Facteus 使用直接来自超过 18 个银行、金融服务和金融科技合作伙伴的被动观察、隐私安全的交易数据，并结合多年确保代表性的强大数据科学，提供对真实经济行为（从国民经济到单个商店）的连续、经过验证的解读。该公司每天根据东亚银行个人消费支出、美国人口普查月度零售销售和公司报告的收益来验证其信号，为客户提供更快的信号，让他们可以根据经济本身进行衡量，并在市场采取行动之前采取行动。欲了解更多信息，请访问faceus.com或请求演示。

四十多年来，彭博终端为资本市场带来透明度和创新，彻底改变了金融服务业。该终端受到世界上最有影响力的决策者的信赖，提供对新闻、数据、见解和交易工具的实时访问，帮助我们的客户将知识转化为行动。

彭博社是商业和金融信息领域的全球领导者，提供可信的数据、新闻和见解，为市场带来透明度、效率和公平。该公司通过可靠的技术解决方案帮助连接全球金融生态系统中具有影响力的社区，使我们的客户能够做出更明智的决策并促进更好的协作。欲了解更多信息，请访问 Bloomberg.com/company 或请求演示。
