article_content:
Introducing computer-use agents, improved clinical answers, and new healthcare plugins that work across healthcare software to get real work done.

Healthcare teams need to piece together information from the EHR, hospital policies, scheduling systems, and payer portals to deliver care and manage operations. With ChatGPT for Healthcare, we’re bringing the tools teams already use and the medical evidence they need into one platform to help them spend less time navigating systems and more time caring for patients.

Today, we’re sharing advances in computer-use agents, which lets AI agents carry out multi-step work across existing healthcare software. We’re also improving trusted clinical search, which finds, evaluates, and cites medical evidence, and introducing more than 20 new plugins to the healthcare plugin ecosystem.

Together, these capabilities help healthcare teams find the information they need, make decisions grounded in medical evidence, and carry out next steps across the systems they already use.

### Carry work forward across healthcare systems with computer-use agents

Organizations often need to move information between disconnected systems to prepare documentation, coordinate care, and complete administrative tasks. Computer-use agents can help with these steps by navigating the software that teams already use: reading screens, clicking, typing, and moving between applications.

Today, we’re sharing advances in computer-use agents for healthcare, including more capable, safe, and affordable models for clinical and administrative workflows, and access controls and audit logs for secure deployments. We’re also sharing our work with healthcare organizations that are deploying agents, including Abridge, Ambience, Cigna Healthcare, and CVS Health, to process referrals, move documents between systems, and bring together the information care teams need. In the demo below, a clinician uses Voice in the ChatGPT app to ask for help following up on an MRI request. The agent reviews the chart and drafts an order and patient reply for review.

Healthcare organizations can start with a workflow that spans existing applications, set which applications agents can access, and establish clear controls for which steps require human review. To support HIPAA-compliant workflows involving protected health information, organizations must use eligible services covered by their BAA with OpenAI, apply required security and retention settings, and extend protections to connected systems. Content shared with ChatGPT for Healthcare is not used to train models.

Read more about our computer use research, customer stories, and demonstrations in Advancing computer-use agents for healthcare teams.

### Stronger clinical answers, everywhere teams work

We’re improving trusted clinical search in ChatGPT for Healthcare and ChatGPT for Clinicians, including how ChatGPT finds, evaluates, and cites medical evidence. These updates help clinicians connect relevant evidence to clinical questions and translate it into practical next steps, with citations they can inspect.

To measure the impact of these updates, in a blind evaluation, physicians reviewed responses to real-world clinical questions across multiple specialties, including multi-turn conversations. In over 1300 reviews, physicians rated the updated experience more highly across all eight dimensions evaluated, including factual correctness, safety, actionability, and source authoritativeness.

### Bring healthcare tools into one conversation

We’re expanding our healthcare plugin ecosystem with more than 20 new healthcare plugins from leading companies across clinical care, care coordination, and business operations. All of these are available today in ChatGPT for Healthcare, including through ChartGPT, which brings ChatGPT into the EHR workflow.

These plugins let teams bring more of their work into the same conversation: reviewing patient records and hospital protocols, preparing prescriptions for clinician review, coordinating patient outreach, checking insurance eligibility, and analyzing healthcare costs and operational performance.

See how healthcare teams can use these plugins together in ChatGPT.

### Care coordinator | Resolve barriers before the visit

Use Luma Health to find tomorrow’s appointments that still need confirmation, then check those patients’ insurance eligibility with TriZetto. Build a call list showing what I need to confirm or resolve with each patient before their visit.

### Primary care physician | Follow up after a hospital stay

My patient was hospitalized elsewhere for heart failure - find the discharge summary using Metriport. Which medications changed? What follow-up monitoring does UpToDate recommend for those changes? Link me to both sources.

### Inpatient nurse | Navigate complex care

I’m admitting a patient who uses their own insulin pump, and the admitting team has requested endocrinology input. Pull up our hospital’s inpatient pump policy in AIVA, including required nursing checks and documentation, and use Amion to find the covering endocrinologist and how to reach them.

### Care navigator | Compare two sites for an MRI

My patient can get a knee MRI without contrast at either of these two hospitals. Use IMO Health to identify the matching procedure code, check their insurance eligibility and benefits in Stedi, then show me their plan’s negotiated rate for that code at each hospital using Turquoise Health. Also identify any additional information needed to estimate what the patient would owe.

### Referral manager | Review referrals and scheduling follow-ups

For our weekly referral review, use Assort Health to summarize referral volume, conversion trends, and our main referring practices. Use Ferry Health to show appointment tasks by status and link to those awaiting follow-up. Put the referral trends and outstanding scheduling work into a brief my team can use to prioritize patient follow-up.

The new plugins join ChatGPT’s broader ecosystem of plugins supporting work across industries, from healthcare data and research to documents, presentations, and software development.

With our plugin partners, we’re making it easier for care teams to bring clinical evidence, patient information, and their everyday tools into ChatGPT. We’re continuing to invest in this ecosystem and inviting more healthcare companies to build with us.

### Availability and next steps

ChatGPT for Healthcare supports clinical, research, and administrative teams in a governed workspace. ChatGPT for Clinicians is free for eligible, verified clinicians in the U.S. to review medical evidence and prepare clinical documentation. Both products offer customers a Business Associate Agreement (BAA) with OpenAI to support HIPAA-compliant workflows.

ChatGPT for Healthcare customers: Computer-use agents in ChatGPT Work and Codex and improved trusted clinical search are available today, subject to workspace settings. Ask your workspace administrator to enable new healthcare plugins.

Developers exploring computer use: Computer-use agent capability is available in the OpenAI API, ChatGPT Work, and Codex. Contact our sales team to discuss using these capabilities in your clinical and administrative workflows.

To purchase ChatGPT for Healthcare directly or through an AWS Marketplace private offer, contact our sales team.

医疗保健团队需要将来自电子病历、医院政策、调度系统和付款人门户的信息整合在一起，以提供护理和管理运营。通过 ChatGPT for Healthcare，我们将团队已经使用的工具和他们所需的医学证据整合到一个平台中，以帮助他们花更少的时间浏览系统，而将更多的时间花在照顾患者上。

### 通过计算机使用代理在整个医疗保健系统中推进工作

组织通常需要在断开连接的系统之间移动信息，以准备文档、协调护理和完成管理任务。计算机使用代理可以通过导航团队已使用的软件来帮助完成这些步骤：阅读屏幕、单击、键入以及在应用程序之间移动。

今天，我们将分享医疗保健计算机使用代理的进展，包括用于临床和管理工作流程的更强大、更安全和更实惠的模型，以及用于安全部署的访问控制和审核日志。我们还与正在部署代理的医疗机构（包括 Abridge、Ambience、Cigna Healthcare 和 CVS Health）分享我们的工作，以处理转诊、在系统之间移动文档以及汇集护理团队所需的信息。在下面的演示中，临床医生使用 ChatGPT 应用程序中的语音来请求帮助以跟进 MRI 请求。代理人审查图表并起草订单和患者答复以供审查。

医疗保健组织可以从跨越现有应用程序的工作流程开始，设置代理可以访问哪些应用程序，并为哪些步骤需要人工审核建立明确的控制。为了支持涉及受保护健康信息的符合 HIPAA 的工作流程，组织必须将其 BAA 涵盖的合格服务与 OpenAI 结合使用，应用所需的安全和保留设置，并将保护扩展到连接的系统。与 ChatGPT for Healthcare 共享的内容不用于训练模型。

详细了解我们的计算机使用研究、客户案例和演示，请参阅为医疗团队推进计算机使用代理。

### 在团队工作的任何地方提供更强大的临床答案

我们正在改进 ChatGPT for Healthcare 和 ChatGPT for Clinicians 中的可信临床搜索，包括 ChatGPT 如何查找、评估和引用医学证据。这些更新可帮助临床医生将相关证据与临床问题联系起来，并将其转化为实际的后续步骤，并附上可供检查的引文。

为了衡量这些更新的影响，在盲目评估中，医生审查了多个专业对现实临床问题的回答，包括多轮对话。在 1300 多条评论中，医生在评估的所有八个维度（包括事实正确性、安全性、可操作性和来源权威性）上对更新后的体验给予了更高的评价。

### 将医疗保健工具融入一次对话中

我们正在通过来自临床护理、护理协调和业务运营领域领先公司的 20 多个新医疗保健插件来扩展我们的医疗保健插件生态系统。所有这些现在都可以在 ChatGPT for Healthcare 中使用，包括通过 ChartGPT，它将 ChatGPT 引入 EHR 工作流程。

这些插件使团队可以将更多工作纳入同一对话中：审查患者记录和医院协议、准备处方以供临床医生审查、协调患者外展、检查保险资格以及分析医疗保健成本和运营绩效。

了解医疗保健团队如何在 ChatGPT 中一起使用这些插件。

### 护理协调员|参观前解决障碍

使用 Luma Health 查找明天仍需要确认的预约，然后使用 TriZetto 检查这些患者的保险资格。建立一个通话清单，显示我在每位患者就诊之前需要确认或解决的问题。

### 初级保健医生 |住院后随访

我的患者因心力衰竭在其他地方住院 - 使用 Metriport 查找出院摘要。哪些药物发生了变化？ UpToDate 建议对这些更改进行哪些后续监控？将我链接到两个来源。

### 住院护士|导航复杂的护理

我正在收治一名使用自己的胰岛素泵的患者，收治团队已要求内分泌科提供意见。在 AIVA 中调出我们医院的住院泵政策，包括所需的护理检查和文件，并使用 Amion 找到负责的内分泌科医生以及如何联系他们。

### 护理导航|比较两个部位的 MRI

我的病人可以在这两家医院中的任何一家接受无造影剂的膝盖 MRI 检查。使用 IMO Health 识别匹配的程序代码，在 Stedi 中检查他们的保险资格和福利，然后使用 Turquoise Health 向我显示他们的计划在每家医院对该代码的协商费率。还要确定估计患者欠款所需的任何其他信息。

### 推荐经理 |审查转介并安排后续行动

对于我们的每周推荐审核，请使用 Assort Health 来总结推荐量、转化趋势和我们的主要推荐实践。使用 Ferry Health 按状态显示预约任务，并链接到等待跟进的任务。将转诊趋势和未完成的安排工作放入一份简报中，我的团队可以使用它来确定患者随访的优先顺序。

新插件加入了 ChatGPT 更广泛的插件生态系统，支持跨行业的工作，从医疗保健数据和研究到文档、演示文稿和软件开发。

通过我们的插件合作伙伴，我们使护理团队能够更轻松地将临床证据、患者信息及其日常工具引入 ChatGPT。我们将继续投资这个生态系统，并邀请更多医疗保健公司与我们一起建设。

### 可用性和后续步骤

ChatGPT for Healthcare 在受监管的工作空间中为临床、研究和管理团队提供支持。 ChatGPT for Clinicians 可免费供美国符合资格且经过验证的临床医生审查医学证据并准备临床文件。这两款产品都为客户提供了与 OpenAI 的业务合作协议 (BAA)，以支持符合 HIPAA 的工作流程。

title: Alibaba says it filtered Qwen4-Max's training data to remove offensive cyber capabilities and mitigate chemical, biological, radiological, and nuclear risks (Ann Cao/South China Morning Post)
title_en: Alibaba says it filtered Qwen4-Max's training data to remove offensive cyber capabilities and mitigate chemical, biological, radiological, and nuclear risks (Ann Cao/South China Morning Post)

inline_images.caption: Alibaba’s Max series of models had always been closed-source until Qwen 3.8, which was made available as open source in August. Photo: Shutterstock
inline_images.alt: Alibaba’s Max series of models had always been closed-source until Qwen 3.8, which was made availabl

author: South China Morning Post
article_content:
Alibaba Group Holding has launched its most advanced artificial intelligence model to date, Qwen4-Max, with strict cybersecurity guardrails, as the tech giant balances safety with a continued commitment to open sourcing amid growing global concerns over AI-enabled cyberattacks.

The release highlights a growing focus on safety in China’s AI industry as Alibaba said it intentionally filtered the model’s training data to remove offensive cyberattack capabilities while retaining capabilities useful for cyber defence such as vulnerability detection.

The Hangzhou-based company also introduced dedicated data sets and post-training enhancements to mitigate chemical, biological, radiological and nuclear (CBRN) risks, it said on Monday.

Alibaba also highlighted the model’s improvements in scientific research, including the completion of a continuous 48-hour run to discover an experimentally validated coolant molecule for next-generation semiconductor chips, as well as autonomous research on Alzheimer’s disease.

There is heated debate about whether open-weight models, which are favoured by Chinese companies, could heighten CBRN risks more than the closed-source models championed by their US rivals such as OpenAI and Anthropic.

Some experts have warned that AI systems could eventually be powerful enough to enable malicious actors or states to develop CBRN weapons.

While Qwen4-Max is a closed model, Alibaba reaffirmed its open-source strategy by noting that smaller-scale, open-weight versions of the Qwen4 series would be released to global developers soon.

Qwen4-Max boasts 2.4 trillion parameters, the same size as its previous Qwen3.8-Max, though it activates only 71 billion parameters per token – 25 per cent less than its predecessor.

That allows it to deliver superior reasoning capabilities while bringing down inference costs, cutting the average cost per task by 60 per cent, according to Alibaba, citing an internal benchmark called Work360, which evaluates model performance on various work tasks.

The model is currently available via QwenCloud, with input pricing set at 7.5 US cents per 1 million tokens.

Alibaba’s AI efforts have focused heavily on capturing the enterprise AI market and cultivating an open-source community to outpace local rivals like DeepSeek and Z.ai, as well as US competitors.

Liu Dayiheng, head of Alibaba’s Qwen large language model team, presented a road map outlining plans for the Qwen 4, Qwen 4.5 and Qwen 5 series in September, while stressing the team’s commitment to the open-source community earlier this month at the World Internet Conference in Wuzhen.

The company has said that its next-generation model, Qwen 5, would be scaled up to between 5 trillion and 10 trillion parameters.

Alibaba owns the South China Morning Post.

article_content_zh:
阿里巴巴集团控股有限公司推出了迄今为止最先进的人工智能模型Qwen4-Max，该模型具有严格的网络安全护栏，在全球对人工智能网络攻击日益担忧的情况下，这家科技巨头在安全与持续致力于开源之间取得了平衡。

此次发布突显了中国人工智能行业对安全性的日益关注，阿里巴巴表示，它有意过滤模型的训练数据，以消除进攻性网络攻击能力，同时保留对网络防御有用的功能，例如漏洞检测。

这家总部位于杭州的公司周一表示，还推出了专用数据集和培训后增强功能，以减轻化学、生物、放射性和核（CBRN）风险。

阿里巴巴还强调了该模型在科学研究方面的进步，包括完成了连续 48 小时运行，发现了经过实验验证的用于下一代半导体芯片的冷却剂分子，以及针对阿尔茨海默病的自主研究。

关于中国公司青睐的开放权重模型是否会比 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 等美国竞争对手所倡导的闭源模型更大地增加 CBRN 风险，存在着激烈的争论。

一些专家警告说，人工智能系统最终可能强大到足以使恶意行为者或国家能够开发核生化武器。

虽然Qwen4-Max是一个封闭模型，但阿里巴巴重申了其开源战略，指出Qwen4系列的较小规模、开放重量版本将很快向全球开发者发布。

阿里巴巴的Max系列机型一直是闭源的，直到8月份Qwen 3.8成为开源版本。Max系列也是该公司参数尺寸最大的机型。然而，该公司强调了其最新型号在为用户提供服务时更具成本效益的成就。

Qwen4-Max 拥有 2.4 万亿个参数，与之前的 Qwen3.8-Max 大小相同，但每个代币仅激活 710 亿个参数，比其前身少了 25%。

阿里巴巴称，这使其能够提供卓越的推理能力，同时降低推理成本，将每个任务的平均成本降低 60%，并引用了一个名为 Work360 的内部基准，该基准评估模型在各种工作任务上的性能。

该模型目前可通过 QwenCloud 获得，输入价格设定为每 100 万个代币 7.5 美分。

阿里巴巴的人工智能工作主要集中在占领企业人工智能市场和培育开源社区，以超越 DeepSeek 和 Z.ai 等本土竞争对手以及美国竞争对手。

阿里巴巴Qwen大语言模型团队负责人刘大一恒在9月份的乌镇世界互联网大会上发布了Qwen 4、Qwen 4.5和Qwen 5系列的路线图，概述了Qwen 4、Qwen 4.5和Qwen 5系列的计划，同时强调了团队对开源社区的承诺。

该公司表示，其下一代模型 Qwen 5 将扩展到 5 万亿至 10 万亿个参数。

title: Qwen4-Max scores 43 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, beating Qwen3.8 Max at ~67% lower cost per task but trailing Kimi K3.1 Pro at ~11% lower cost (Artificial Analysis)
title_en: Qwen4-Max scores 43 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, beating Qwen3.8 Max at ~67% lower cost per task but trailing Kimi K3.1 Pro at ~11% lower cost (Artificial Analysis)
author: Artificial Analysis
article_content:
Qwen4 Max is above average in intelligence and reasonably priced when comparing to other models of similar price. The model supports text and image input, outputs text, and has a 984k tokens context window.

Qwen4 Max scores 43 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, placing it above average among comparable models (median: 41). When evaluating the Intelligence Index, it generated 127M tokens, which is very verbose in comparison to the median of 78.6M.

Pricing for Qwen4 Max is $1.50 per 1M input tokens (moderately priced, median: $2.00) and $4.50 per 1M output tokens (moderately priced, median: $10.00). On average, it costs $3.27 per task to evaluate Qwen4 Max on the Intelligence Index.

Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5.0.1 includes: AA-Briefcase v1.1, AutomationBench-AA, Terminal-Bench 4.0, FrontierCode-AA 2.0, AA-Omniscience v1.1, GDP.pdf, HLE-Diamond, CritPt v2 (Hard Subset), Terminal-Bench-Science 0.1. See Intelligence Index methodology for further details, including a breakdown of each evaluation and how we run them.

Weighted average cost per Intelligence Index task. Each evaluation’s cost is calculated from input, cache hit, cache write, reasoning, and answer token prices, divided by task count, and weighted by its Intelligence Index weight.

title: Trump Administration to Name Nvidia Among AI ‘National Champions’
title_en: Trump Administration to Name Nvidia Among AI ‘National Champions’

author: Yoko Kubota and Amrith Ramkumar
article_content:
Nvidia will be one of more than two dozen companies designated artificial intelligence “national champions” as part of an effort by the Trump administration to help AI firms win business overseas, people familiar with the plans said.

The announcement, which is expected within the next week, indicates the administration is barreling ahead with its tech strategy despite the turmoil surrounding Nvidia. The national champions initiative is part of an effort to get foreign companies and countries to adopt U.S. AI technology over Chinese rivals.

The Trump administration is preparing to designate Nvidia, Microsoft, Amazon, OpenAI and Anthropic, among more than two dozen American companies, as artificial intelligence “national champions”, according to a report by The Wall Street Journal. The proposed initiative is aimed at helping US technology firms expand overseas and compete with Chinese rivals in the global AI market.

A formal announcement is expected within the coming week, with Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick likely to lead it, the report said. The timeline, however, could change.

The programme seeks to encourage foreign governments and businesses to adopt American-developed AI systems instead of Chinese alternatives. It would bring together US-made processors, AI architectures and related products in packages intended to make procurement easier for overseas buyers.

Portraits of Dreamers and Doers under 35

Companies selected under the initiative could receive faster authorisations for export licences, government support for international operations and access to federal funding mechanisms, according to details on the Commerce Department's initiative portal.

First unveiled around a year ago as part of the administration's broader technology strategy, the programme's list of participating companies had not previously been made public.

The initiative reflects Washington's efforts to strengthen the international presence of American AI companies as competition with Beijing intensifies. Chinese firms, including Huawei Technologies, have been expanding their presence in markets across Europe and Latin America.

Nvidia's expected inclusion comes amid continuing debate in Washington over the export of advanced AI chips to China. Its processors power many of the world's most sophisticated AI systems and are central to the development of advanced computing infrastructure.

President Donald Trump has repeatedly praised Nvidia and its chief executive, Jensen Huang, for building a major American technology company at the centre of the AI boom.

But the company's role in the global chip market has also placed it under scrutiny from national security officials and lawmakers concerned that advanced Nvidia components could reach Chinese entities through gaps in export controls.

The Wall Street Journal report said disclosures concerning Huang's alleged links to a Chinese intelligence operative have added to pressure from critics calling for national security considerations to take precedence over commercial interests.

Lutnick has also faced criticism over claims that the Commerce Department has not adequately closed loopholes that could allow Chinese companies to obtain advanced Nvidia chips. The Wall Street Journal has previously reported concerns about his reluctance to alienate Beijing during trade negotiations.

The planned announcement comes as Lutnick prepares to accompany Trump on a diplomatic visit to China this week. The Commerce Department is also expected to advance new regulations to prevent the illicit diversion of high-performance processors to Beijing.

Expanding American AI exports has been a central part of the Trump administration's technology agenda since last summer. Washington views the initiative as a way to secure overseas markets for US-developed systems and reinforce its position in a sector increasingly shaped by strategic competition with China.

The proposed national champions framework would combine technology, export facilitation and diplomatic support in an effort to make American AI products more accessible to foreign buyers.

article_content_zh:
知情人士称，作为特朗普政府帮助人工智能公司赢得海外业务的努力的一部分，英伟达将成为被指定为人工智能“国家冠军”的两打公司之一。

该公告预计将在下周内发布，这表明尽管英伟达面临着动荡，但政府仍在大力推进其科技战略。国家冠军计划是让外国公司和国家采用美国人工智能技术而不是中国竞争对手的努力的一部分。

据《华尔街日报》报道，特朗普政府正准备将英伟达、微软、亚马逊、OpenAI 和 Anthropic 等二十多家美国公司指定为人工智能“国家冠军”。该倡议旨在帮助美国科技公司向海外扩张，并在全球人工智能市场与中国竞争对手竞争。

报道称，预计将在下周内发布正式公告，商务部长霍华德·卢特尼克可能会领导该公告。然而，时间表可能会改变。

该计划旨在鼓励外国政府和企业采用美国开发的人工智能系统，而不是中国的替代方案。它将把美国制造的处理器、人工智能架构和相关产品整合在一起，旨在让海外买家更容易采购。

35岁以下梦想家和实干家的肖像

根据商务部倡议门户网站上的详细信息，根据该倡议选出的公司可以更快地获得出口许可证授权、政府对国际业务的支持以及联邦融资机制的使用。

作为政府更广泛技术战略的一部分，该计划于大约一年前首次公布，参与该计划的公司名单此前并未公开。

该举措反映了随着与北京的竞争加剧，华盛顿为加强美国人工智能公司的国际影响力而做出的努力。包括华为在内的中国企业一直在扩大在欧洲和拉丁美洲市场的影响力。

英伟达预计将被纳入其中之际，华盛顿正在就向中国出口先进人工智能芯片展开持续争论。其处理器为世界上许多最复杂的人工智能系统提供动力，并且是先进计算基础设施开发的核心。

唐纳德·特朗普总统多次赞扬英伟达及其首席执行官黄仁勋在人工智能热潮的中心打造了一家美国大型科技公司。

但该公司在全球芯片市场中的角色也使其受到国家安全官员和立法者的审查，他们担心先进的英伟达组件可能通过出口管制漏洞到达中国实体。

《华尔街日报》的报道称，有关黄涉嫌与中国情报人员有联系的披露加大了批评人士的压力，他们呼吁国家安全考虑优先于商业利益。

卢特尼克还面临批评，称美国商务部没有充分堵住可能允许中国公司获得先进英伟达芯片的漏洞。 《华尔街日报》此前曾报道过对他不愿在贸易谈判期间疏远北京的担忧。

计划宣布这一消息之际，卢特尼克正准备本周陪同特朗普对中国进行外交访问。预计商务部还将推进新法规，以防止高性能处理器非法转移到北京。

title: Trump Administration to Name Nvidia Among AI ‘National Champions’
title_en: Trump Administration to Name Nvidia Among AI ‘National Champions’

author: Yoko Kubota and Amrith Ramkumar
article_content:
Nvidia will be one of more than two dozen companies designated artificial intelligence “national champions” as part of an effort by the Trump administration to help AI firms win business overseas, people familiar with the plans said.

The announcement, which is expected within the next week, indicates the administration is barreling ahead with its tech strategy despite the turmoil surrounding Nvidia. The national champions initiative is part of an effort to get foreign companies and countries to adopt U.S. AI technology over Chinese rivals.

The Trump administration is preparing to designate Nvidia, Microsoft, Amazon, OpenAI and Anthropic, among more than two dozen American companies, as artificial intelligence “national champions”, according to a report by The Wall Street Journal. The proposed initiative is aimed at helping US technology firms expand overseas and compete with Chinese rivals in the global AI market.

A formal announcement is expected within the coming week, with Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick likely to lead it, the report said. The timeline, however, could change.

The programme seeks to encourage foreign governments and businesses to adopt American-developed AI systems instead of Chinese alternatives. It would bring together US-made processors, AI architectures and related products in packages intended to make procurement easier for overseas buyers.

Portraits of Dreamers and Doers under 35

Companies selected under the initiative could receive faster authorisations for export licences, government support for international operations and access to federal funding mechanisms, according to details on the Commerce Department's initiative portal.

First unveiled around a year ago as part of the administration's broader technology strategy, the programme's list of participating companies had not previously been made public.

The initiative reflects Washington's efforts to strengthen the international presence of American AI companies as competition with Beijing intensifies. Chinese firms, including Huawei Technologies, have been expanding their presence in markets across Europe and Latin America.

Nvidia's expected inclusion comes amid continuing debate in Washington over the export of advanced AI chips to China. Its processors power many of the world's most sophisticated AI systems and are central to the development of advanced computing infrastructure.

President Donald Trump has repeatedly praised Nvidia and its chief executive, Jensen Huang, for building a major American technology company at the centre of the AI boom.

But the company's role in the global chip market has also placed it under scrutiny from national security officials and lawmakers concerned that advanced Nvidia components could reach Chinese entities through gaps in export controls.

The Wall Street Journal report said disclosures concerning Huang's alleged links to a Chinese intelligence operative have added to pressure from critics calling for national security considerations to take precedence over commercial interests.

Lutnick has also faced criticism over claims that the Commerce Department has not adequately closed loopholes that could allow Chinese companies to obtain advanced Nvidia chips. The Wall Street Journal has previously reported concerns about his reluctance to alienate Beijing during trade negotiations.

The planned announcement comes as Lutnick prepares to accompany Trump on a diplomatic visit to China this week. The Commerce Department is also expected to advance new regulations to prevent the illicit diversion of high-performance processors to Beijing.

Expanding American AI exports has been a central part of the Trump administration's technology agenda since last summer. Washington views the initiative as a way to secure overseas markets for US-developed systems and reinforce its position in a sector increasingly shaped by strategic competition with China.

The proposed national champions framework would combine technology, export facilitation and diplomatic support in an effort to make American AI products more accessible to foreign buyers.

title_zh: 特朗普政府将英伟达列为人工智能“国家冠军”
summary_zh: 特朗普政府拟将英伟达、亚马逊、微软、OpenAI及Anthropic等超24家企业列为人工智能“国家冠军”，以提升美国AI技术在全球市场的竞争力
article_content_zh:
知情人士称，作为特朗普政府帮助人工智能公司赢得海外业务的努力的一部分，英伟达将成为被指定为人工智能“国家冠军”的两打公司之一。

该公告预计将在下周内发布，这表明尽管英伟达面临着动荡，但政府仍在大力推进其科技战略。国家冠军计划是让外国公司和国家采用美国人工智能技术而不是中国竞争对手的努力的一部分。

据《华尔街日报》报道，特朗普政府正准备将英伟达、微软、亚马逊、OpenAI 和 Anthropic 等二十多家美国公司指定为人工智能“国家冠军”。该倡议旨在帮助美国科技公司向海外扩张，并在全球人工智能市场与中国竞争对手竞争。

报道称，预计将在下周内发布正式公告，商务部长霍华德·卢特尼克可能会领导该公告。然而，时间表可能会改变。

该计划旨在鼓励外国政府和企业采用美国开发的人工智能系统，而不是中国的替代方案。它将把美国制造的处理器、人工智能架构和相关产品整合在一起，旨在让海外买家更容易采购。

35岁以下梦想家和实干家的肖像

根据商务部倡议门户网站上的详细信息，根据该倡议选出的公司可以更快地获得出口许可证授权、政府对国际业务的支持以及联邦融资机制的使用。

作为政府更广泛技术战略的一部分，该计划于大约一年前首次公布，参与该计划的公司名单此前并未公开。

该举措反映了随着与北京的竞争加剧，华盛顿为加强美国人工智能公司的国际影响力而做出的努力。包括华为在内的中国企业一直在扩大在欧洲和拉丁美洲市场的影响力。

英伟达预计将被纳入其中之际，华盛顿正在就向中国出口先进人工智能芯片展开持续争论。其处理器为世界上许多最复杂的人工智能系统提供动力，并且是先进计算基础设施开发的核心。

唐纳德·特朗普总统多次赞扬英伟达及其首席执行官黄仁勋在人工智能热潮的中心打造了一家美国大型科技公司。

但该公司在全球芯片市场中的角色也使其受到国家安全官员和立法者的审查，他们担心先进的英伟达组件可能通过出口管制漏洞到达中国实体。

《华尔街日报》的报道称，有关黄涉嫌与中国情报人员有联系的披露加大了批评人士的压力，他们呼吁国家安全考虑优先于商业利益。

卢特尼克还面临批评，称美国商务部没有充分堵住可能允许中国公司获得先进英伟达芯片的漏洞。 《华尔街日报》此前曾报道过对他不愿在贸易谈判期间疏远北京的担忧。

计划宣布这一消息之际，卢特尼克正准备本周陪同特朗普对中国进行外交访问。预计商务部还将推进新法规，以防止高性能处理器非法转移到北京。

自去年夏天以来，扩大美国人工智能出口一直是特朗普政府技术议程的核心部分。华盛顿将这一举措视为确保美国开发系统的海外市场并巩固其在日益受到与中国战略竞争影响的行业中的地位的一种方式。

拟议的国家冠军框架将结合技术、出口便利化和外交支持，以使外国买家更容易获得美国人工智能产品。

title: Kindo raises $30M after 800% revenue growth: Can one control centre tame enterprise AI agents?
title_en: Kindo raises $30M after 800% revenue growth: Can one control centre tame enterprise AI agents?
author: Abhinaya Prabhu
article_content:
As businesses deploy AI agents across more departments, controlling what these systems can access, change and spend is becoming a growing challenge.

Kindo, an AI agent management platform, has raised $30 million in a funding round co-led by Crosspoint Capital and Forgepoint Capital, bringing its total funding to $57.6 million. The company did not name the round.

Kindo reported approximately 800% year-on-year revenue growth in 2026. It plans to use the capital to expand its go-to-market organisation and accelerate development of its enterprise AI Control Center and Deep Hat models and add-ons.

“Agent builders from the AI labs, hyperscalers, and thousands of startups make it easy to deploy powerful agents across the business. What’s missing is the tooling that lets an organization centrally control how those agents are built, what data they can reach, where that data can go, and what they cost, while also allowing support teams to reach in and fix an agent at any hour,” said Ron Williams, founder and CEO of Kindo.

### Founded by an enterprise technology veteran

Kindo was founded in 2022 by Williams, who serves as its CEO. He began his career as a programmer in the US Air Force before moving into IT and security leadership. According to Kindo’s website, he served as chief information officer and chief information security officer at Riot Games, Clover Health and Bird.

Kindo’s founding team also includes Bryan Vann, its co-founder and CTO. Vann was one of the original architects of Google Drive and left Google as a senior director managing most of the Drive engineering team, according to a 2024 Pulse 2.0 interview.

### A central control centre for enterprise agents

Kindo helps businesses discover AI agents already operating across their environments, including tools deployed without formal IT approval. It then provides a unified view of agent activity, data access, costs and outcomes.

Its gateways govern and audit calls made by agents to connected data sources, tools and approved AI models. Identity controls extend existing organisational permissions to both employees and agents, while allowing administrators to tighten access centrally.

For mission-critical applications, Kindo offers a purpose-built agent harness that provides continuous monitoring and support. Teams can directly intervene or take over an agent when something goes wrong.

The platform can connect to agents and models already in use, rather than requiring businesses to rebuild their AI infrastructure. It can run on-premises, in a customer’s cloud, through Kindo’s cloud or in air-gapped environments.

Kindo says it runs in production at large and mid-market enterprises in financial services, professional services, healthcare, and aviation and transportation. Aireon, a global aviation in-flight data provider, reported in May 2026 that using Kindo for threat hunting and Tier 1 and Tier 2 security operations centre work helped it save more than $2 million a year, according to the company.

### Cutting AI costs as enterprise adoption grows

Beyond security and compliance, the cost of running AI agents is becoming a major concern for businesses. Kindo’s AI Control Center gives finance teams visibility into token consumption, agent runs and their outcomes, including unsuccessful tasks.

Costs can be tracked by employee, agent, department and project. Businesses can also set budgets, trigger spending alerts and enforce hard limits. This helps identify agents that repeatedly fail, consume excessive resources or use expensive models for relatively simple tasks.

Kindo’s Deep Hat add-ons are designed to reduce these expenses further. Deep Hat Sift filters repetitive events from alert and ticket queues after human approval, while logging the activity and sending samples through to measure potential misses.

Deep Hat Tune adapts smaller, less expensive models to specific tasks, reducing reliance on larger models. Deep Hat Shrink converts repeatable workflow steps into code, eliminating model costs for those operations while routing exceptions back to an AI model. Deep Hat Attack provides private, lower-cost offensive security testing.

### AI agent security and governance attracts competitors

Kindo is entering a competitive market where startups and established technology companies are developing tools to secure, monitor and govern autonomous AI systems.

London-based Geordie AI raised $30 million in Series A funding led by Balderton Capital in May 2026 to build a security layer for AI agents. Barcelona-based NeuralTrust raised $20 million in seed funding led by Alstin Capital in June 2026 to govern enterprise agents.

Israel’s Zenity raised $125 million in a Series C led by Norwest in August 2026 to secure AI agents. GitGuardian raised $50 million in Series C funding in February 2026, led by Insight Partners, and is extending its non-human identity security to credentials used by AI agents. FriskAI raised $3.6 million in pre-seed funding led by MaC Venture Capital in August 2026 to record and review what agents do.

### Investor backing

Alongside Crosspoint Capital and Forgepoint Capital, TFX Capital and CircleRock Capital joined the financing. Existing investors Drive Capital, Riot Ventures, RRE Ventures, Eniac Ventures, Marlinspike Partners, New Era Ventures and Sunset Venture also participated.

Andre Fuetsch, managing director at Crosspoint Capital, and Ernie Bio, managing director at Forgepoint Capital, will join Kindo’s board.

“2026 has been the year of the agent. Companies are putting AI agents into real business processes, but most still lack a reliable way to see what those agents are doing or control which systems they can reach. Kindo differentiates itself by giving the teams who need deep control the ability to see and take action while allowing AI transformation to move forward across the enterprise,” said Fuetsch.

“A company may start with one agent triaging security tickets. As more employees and teams put agents to work, the CIO needs a single place to manage what they can access, support what they do, and control the cost. We backed Kindo because it gives enterprises a way to rein in the tokenmaxxing madness with centrally managed, data-informed control policies,” added Bio.

With cost now as pressing as security, the question for Kindo is whether enterprises will buy one control layer for both, or keep separate tools for each.

article_content_zh:
随着企业在更多部门部署人工智能代理，控制这些系统可以访问、更改和支出的内容正成为越来越大的挑战。

人工智能代理管理平台 Kindo 在 Crosspoint Capital 和 Forgepoint Capital 共同领投的一轮融资中筹集了 3000 万美元，使其总融资达到 5760 万美元。该公司没有透露该轮融资的具体名称。

Kindo 报告称，2026 年收入同比增长约 800%。该公司计划利用这笔资金扩大其上市组织，并加速其企业 AI 控制中心和 Deep Hat 模型及附加组件的开发。

Kindo 创始人兼首席执行官 Ron Williams 表示：“来自人工智能实验室、超大规模企业和数千家初创公司的代理构建者可以轻松地在整个企业中部署强大的代理。现在缺少的是一种工具，可以让组织集中控制这些代理的构建方式、它们可以访问哪些数据、这些数据可以去往何处以及它们的成本，同时还允许支持团队随时介入并修复代理。”

### 由企业技术资深人士创立

Kindo 由 Williams 于 2022 年创立，并担任首席执行官。他的职业生涯始于美国空军的一名程序员，之后进入 IT 和安全领导岗位。据 Kindo 网站称，他曾在 Riot Games、Clover Health 和 Bird 担任首席信息官和首席信息安全官。

Kindo 的创始团队还包括联合创始人兼首席技术官 Bryan Vann。根据 2024 年 Pulse 2.0 的采访，范恩是 Google Drive 的最初架构师之一，离开 Google 后担任高级总监，管理大部分 Drive 工程团队。

### 企业代理的中央控制中心

Kindo 帮助企业发现已经在其环境中运行的人工智能代理，包括未经正式 IT 批准而部署的工具。然后，它提供代理活动、数据访问、成本和结果的统一视图。

其网关管理和审核代理对连接的数据源、工具和批准的人工智能模型发出的调用。身份控制将现有的组织权限扩展到员工和代理，同时允许管理员集中加强访问。

对于关键任务应用程序，Kindo 提供了专门构建的代理工具，可提供持续监控和支持。当出现问题时，团队可以直接干预或接管代理。

该平台可以连接到已经在使用的代理和模型，而不需要企业重建其人工智能基础设施。它可以在本地、客户的云中、通过 Kindo 的云或气隙环境中运行。

Kindo 表示，它在金融服务、专业服务、医疗保健、航空和运输领域的大中型市场企业中运行生产。全球航空飞行数据提供商 Aireon 于 2026 年 5 月报告称，使用 Kindo 进行威胁搜寻以及一级和二级安全运营中心工作帮助其每年节省了超过 200 万美元。

### 随着企业采用率的提高降低人工智能成本

除了安全性和合规性之外，运行人工智能代理的成本也正成为企业关注的主要问题。 Kindo 的人工智能控制中心使财务团队能够了解代币消耗、代理运行及其结果，包括不成功的任务。

可以按员工、代理、部门和项目跟踪成本。企业还可以设置预算、触发支出警报并实施硬性限制。这有助于识别反复失败、消耗过多资源或使用昂贵模型来完成相对简单任务的代理。

Kindo 的 Deep Hat 附加组件旨在进一步减少这些费用。 Deep Hat Sift 在人工批准后过滤警报和票证队列中的重复事件，同时记录活动并发送样本以测量潜在的遗漏。

Deep Hat Tune 使更小、更便宜的模型适应特定任务，减少对更大模型的依赖。 Deep Hat Shrink 将可重复的工作流程步骤转换为代码，消除了这些操作的模型成本，同时将异常情况路由回 AI 模型。 Deep Hat Attack 提供私密、低成本的进攻性安全测试。

### AI代理安全和治理吸引竞争对手

Kindo 正在进入一个竞争激烈的市场，初创公司和成熟的科技公司正在开发用于保护、监控和管理自主人工智能系统的工具。

总部位于伦敦的 Geordie AI 于 2026 年 5 月在 Balderton Capital 领投的 A 轮融资中筹集了 3000 万美元，用于为 AI 代理构建安全层。总部位于巴塞罗那的 NeuralTrust 于 2026 年 6 月筹集了由 Alstin Capital 领投的 2000 万美元种子资金，用于管理企业代理。

以色列的 Zenity 于 2026 年 8 月在由 Norwest 领投的 C 轮融资中筹集了 1.25 亿美元，以确保人工智能代理的安全。 GitGuardian 于 2026 年 2 月筹集了 5000 万美元的 C 轮融资，由 Insight Partners 领投，并将其非人类身份安全性扩展到人工智能代理使用的凭证。 FriskAI 于 2026 年 8 月筹集了由 MaC Venture Capital 领投的 360 万美元种子前资金，用于记录和审查代理商的工作。

除了 Crosspoint Capital 和 Forgepoint Capital 之外，TFX Capital 和 CircleRock Capital 也加入了融资。现有投资者 Drive Capital、Riot Ventures、RRE Ventures、Eniac Ventures、Marlinspike Partners、New Era Ventures 和 Sunset Ventures 也参与其中。

Crosspoint Capital 董事总经理 Andre Fuetsch 和 Forgepoint Capital 董事总经理 Ernie Bio 将加入 Ki​​ndo 董事会。

Fuetsch 表示：“2026 年是代理年。公司正在将 AI 代理引入实际业务流程，但大多数公司仍然缺乏可靠的方法来查看这些代理正在做什么或控制它们可以访问哪些系统。Kindo 的与众不同之处在于，它为需要深度控制的团队提供了查看并采取行动的能力，同时允许 AI 转型在整个企业中向前推进。”

“一家公司可能会从一个代理对安全票据进行分类开始。随着越来越多的员工和团队让代理工作，首席信息官需要一个单一的地方来管理他们可以访问的内容、支持他们所做的事情并控制成本。我们支持 Kindo，因为它为企业提供了一种通过集中管理、数据通知的控制策略来控制代币最大化疯狂的方法，”Bio 补充道。

由于成本现在和安全性一样紧迫，Kindo 面临的问题是企业是否会为两者购买一个控制层，还是为两者保留单独的工具。

title: Apple launches new app to study how people use AI for health
title_en: Apple launches new app to study how people use AI for health
author: Ivan Mehta
article_content:
Big AI labs like OpenAI and Anthropic have made their bets on offering chatbots that can answer health-related queries with specialized features. Apple is debuting a new study to understand how people use AI for health. But it isn’t quite following other AI startups just yet; it wants to study how clinically grounded answers can help people.

The iPhone maker is partnering with healthcare-focused AI company OpenEvidence to launch a new study app. Apple is inviting users in the U.S. over 21, using iPhone 15 or later, and running iOS 26 or later, with Apple Intelligence enabled. The company is aiming to run this study with up to 200,000 participants for more than 12 months.

The new app will allow users to ask health-related questions, as they do with ChatGPT or Claude, with answers grounded in clinical data, from sources including The New England Journal of Medicine, Journal of the American Medical Association, and Nature. Apple said that the app will try to give simplified answers to everyday medical questions. Users can rate those answers and provide feedback about the responses; they’ll also be asked to participate in monthly surveys.

Participants can share data from HealthKit such as resting heart rate, activity, sleep, or lab results to get more personalized and pointed suggestions from the app. The company said the app can also help prepare participants better for a doctor’s visit, and it will guide users to specific providers for answers related to concerning medical issues.

Apple specified that the data will be anonymized before sending it to a secure third-party cloud provider, and it won’t be used to train any kind of AI models. The company said that OpenEvidence deletes the query and response data after 24 hours.

“At Apple, we believe responsible innovation starts with scientific rigor and clinical grounding. Health is deeply personal, and conducting a dedicated research study is the most thoughtful way to understand how people engage with, comprehend, and evaluate health AI in everyday life,” Sumbul Desai, MD, Apple’s vice president of Health and Fitness, said in a statement, adding, “Insights from this study will help advance the broader scientific conversation and ensure that as technology evolves, we continue building trusted tools that genuinely support people wherever they are on their health journey.”

The app is available to download starting today for U.S. users. It’s not clear if Apple wants to release AI-powered answering to its Health app or Siri yet. The potential is huge — earlier this year, OpenAI said users were asking over 300 million health-related queries each week.

title_zh: 苹果推出新应用程序来研究人们如何利用人工智能促进健康
summary_zh: 苹果联合OpenEvidence推出健康AI研究应用，邀请20万美国用户参与，探索临床数据驱动的AI问答模式
article_content_zh:
OpenAI 和 Anthropic 等大型人工智能实验室已经押注于提供能够通过专门功能回答与健康相关的查询的聊天机器人。苹果公司推出了一项新研究，旨在了解人们如何利用人工智能来促进健康。但它还没有完全追随其他人工智能初创公司的脚步。它想要研究基于临床的答案如何帮助人们。

这家 iPhone 制造商正在与专注于医疗保健的人工智能公司 OpenEvidence 合作推出一款新的研究应用程序。 Apple 正在邀请年满 21 岁、使用 iPhone 15 或更高版本、运行 iOS 26 或更高版本并启用 Apple Intelligence 的美国用户。该公司的目标是对多达 20 万名参与者进行这项为期 12 个月以上的研究。

新应用程序将允许用户提出与健康相关的问题，就像使用 ChatGPT 或 Claude 一样，答案基于临床数据，来源包括《新英格兰医学杂志》、《美国医学会杂志》和《自然》等。苹果表示，该应用程序将尝试为日常医疗问题提供简化的答案。用户可以对这些答案进行评分并提供有关答复的反馈；他们还将被要求参加每月调查。

参与者可以共享 HealthKit 中的数据，例如静息心率、活动、睡眠或实验室结果，以便从应用程序中获得更加个性化和针对性的建议。该公司表示，该应用程序还可以帮助参与者更好地准备去看医生，并将引导用户向特定的提供商寻求与医疗问题相关的答案。

苹果明确表示，这些数据在发送给安全的第三方云提供商之前将进行匿名处理，并且不会用于训练任何类型的人工智能模型。该公司表示，OpenEvidence 会在 24 小时后删除查询和响应数据。

苹果健康与健身副总裁 Sumbul Desai 医学博士在一份声明中表示：“在苹果，我们相信负责任的创新始于科学严谨性和临床基础。健康是非常个性化的，进行专门的研究是了解人们如何在日常生活中参与、理解和评估健康人工智能的最深思熟虑的方式。”正在踏上健康之旅。”

该应用程序从今天开始可供美国用户下载。目前尚不清楚苹果是否想要为其健康应用程序或 Siri 发布人工智能驱动的应答功能。潜力巨大——今年早些时候，OpenAI 表示用户每周提出超过 3 亿个与健康相关的问题。

Ivan 在 TechCrunch 上报道全球消费技术发展。他居住在印度，此前曾在《赫芬顿邮报》和《The Next Web》等出版物工作。

The e-commerce giant-turned-AI player said its Qwen4-Max model scored near the top of coding benchmarks, outperforming Anthropic's Claude Fable 5.1 as well as homegrown rival Moonshot's Kimi K3.1 Pro. Alibaba did not make the model open weight, which would allow users to download and customize it, but said it would make smaller versions of the series available soon.

Chinese firms including Alibaba, Moonshot and DeepSeek are challenging US dominance in artificial intelligence, unveiling a succession of new models with rapid improvements in coding and reasoning. Monday's release adds to a flurry of recent Chinese launches, including Tencent's Hunyuan 4 and Moonshot's Kimi K3.1 Pro.

Alibaba's Qwen series is so far the most downloaded open-weight model family in the world following an ambitious push into the technology spearheaded by Chief Executive Officer Eddie Wu. The company is building a full AI ecosystem, from models to AI chips.

The CEO said in September that Alibaba's T-Head chipmaking unit, which recently filed for an IPO in Hong Kong, would roll out China's most powerful AI chips domestically.

The Hangzhou, China-headquartered firm has made attaining artificial general intelligence, or AGI, its primary goal. It is also rapidly expanding its computing power, with Wu setting a target of building 20 gigawatts of data center capacity globally by 2032.

The firm introduced upgraded security measures in its latest model, following a series of alarming incidents that have raised concerns over the cybersecurity risks of open-weight models. That follows similar moves from Tencent and Moonshot.

阿里巴巴、Moonshot 和 DeepSeek 等中国公司正在挑战美国在人工智能领域的主导地位，推出了一系列在编码和推理方面快速改进的新模型。周一的发布是中国最近推出的一系列产品的又一补充，其中包括腾讯的混元 4 和 Moonshot 的 Kimi K3.1 Pro。

在一系列令人震惊的事件引发人们对开放重量模型的网络安全风险的担忧之后，该公司在其最新模型中引入了升级的安全措施。腾讯和 Moonshot 也采取了类似的举措。

title: Nvidia’s Days as an Open Checkbook for the AI Economy Are Numbered
title_en: Nvidia’s Days as an Open Checkbook for the AI Economy Are Numbered

inline_images.caption: Nvidia’s Days as an Open Checkbook for the AI Economy Are Numbered (Source: Wall Street Journal)
inline_images.caption_en: Nvidia’s Days as an Open Checkbook for the AI Economy Are Numbered (Source: Wall Street Journal)

author: Robbie Whelan and Anissa Gardizy and Kate Clark
article_content:
In his final months as chief executive of Nvidia, Jensen Huang was laying the groundwork to pull back the company’s approach to backstopping the AI economy.

Now, with a finance chief at the helm who was already wary of some deals the ousted chief forged, the startups who had been counting on Nvidia’s support expect an even greater pullback.

Just last month, the CEOs of emerging cloud companies that buy Nvidia chips and rent out computing power gathered in Berlin

Huang told his partners that if their companies wanted allocations of Nvidia’s prized GPUs, they would need to secure upfront payments from customers, people in attendance said. That would make their projects easier to finance and ensure that Nvidia wasn’t alone in being a source of financial support.

“You’re not charging what you should be charging,” he said, telling them that Elon Musk was renting Nvidia chips to customers at better rates than they were. “I don’t even need you guys. I could just give all this capacity to Elon! Elon wants it!” he said, according to two executives who heard the remarks and one who was briefed on them shortly after.

Weeks later, Huang resigned after revelations that he had engaged in at least two affairs, including one with a woman U.S. officials believe is a Chinese intelligence asset and another with one of his direct reports. His interim successor, finance chief Colette Kress, has at times pushed back against some of the company’s big deals and sought to rein in Nvidia.

Many companies that had relied on Nvidia are now worried.

UBS analyst Tim Arcuri estimated in a recent note that an Nvidia financing pullback could take $50 billion or more out of the market, starving companies of support as interest rates rise.

The chip giant spent much of the past year on a dealmaking spree to provide financial backstops to emerging companies, lend its balance sheet to support debt financings of data-center projects, and even act as a customer of last resort for its own chips. The firm agreed to rent its chips from some customers to signal to lenders that those companies had solid contracts in-hand.

Earlier this year, Nvidia signaled it was preparing to roll out new financial incentives and do more deals than ever.

Rivals, such as Alphabet’s Google and Advanced Micro Devices, were offering these companies similar incentives, and Huang didn’t want to lose market share. Among the executives leading the charge was Nico Caprez, an Nvidia vice president who is also Huang’s son-in-law.

Nvidia announced its financing program in July, but by August, Huang and Kress questioned the return on investment from some deals.

When Nvidia used its creditworthy balance sheet to help OpenAI sign a massive data center lease in Piketon, Ohio, with SoftBank’s SB Energy, it cut the scale of its commitment in August during negotiations. Kress had become skeptical of the scale of the deal.

Huang told his finance team in August that the company was under pressure, The Wall Street Journal previously reported. Major cloud providers were making plans to use alternative chips and lessen their reliance on the firm, and Nvidia was staring at a glut of chip wafers and memory it had committed to buying, he told them.

The then-CEO pressed staff to develop a way to decide whether guarantees were worthwhile. Later that month, it paused some deals in that initiative, the Journal reported.

U.K.-based neocloud Nscale is still negotiating with Nvidia and other investors to provide financial backing for a $45-billion data center for Anthropic in West Virginia, the Journal reported.

In addition to its extensive backstopping, the chip maker also made a string of equity investments in AI startups. In total, Nvidia has participated in a record 129 venture-capital deals this year, as of Nov. 10, accounting for 27% of global VC deal value, according to PitchBook, up from a total of 49 such deals in 2023.

CEOs of startups that had closed deals with Nvidia breathed a sigh of relief that their deals made it through before Huang’s ouster.

Perplexity Chief Executive Aravind Srinivas shared that Nvidia closed a $3 billion investment in the company with his employees during a weekly all-hands at the startup’s San Francisco headquarters on Oct. 30, a person familiar with the meeting said. It was one day after news broke that the Nvidia CEO was seen as a target of a Chinese spy plot.

The AI search company is now raising additional capital at a higher valuation of $38 billion before the new investment, according to people familiar with the matter.

Nvidia recently made an offer to Reflection AI, an open-source model developer valued at $25 billion, to license its technology and hire away some of its talent, according to people familiar with the matter. Huang had publicly praised the company. An agreement hadn’t been reached before he left, the people said.

Nvidia has also been finalizing a massive investment in Thinking Machines Lab, another provider of open-source models, valuing the company at $40 billion, according to people familiar with the matter. Thinking Machines is confident the deal will be completed, according to a person familiar with the matter.

Some details of Nvidia’s recent investments were earlier reported by the Financial Times and The Information.

Reflection and Thinking Machines are burning huge amounts of capital each month to pay for the computing power to develop their AI models, but haven’t yet developed a way to generate substantial revenue.

Some founders and venture-capital backers of companies with little to no sales said that if Nvidia did pull back from future equity investments, they could struggle to find capital to keep their cash-hungry businesses going, let alone secure a lucrative exit.

ai_analysis.takeaway_en: Nvidia faces not only a leadership vacuum but also acute scrutiny of its secondary sales channels in Southeast Asia, which may trigger tighter U.S. export compliance enforcement. The new leadership must urgently recalibrate aggressive sales strategies to restore market confidence in supply chain integrity.

article_content_zh:
在担任 Nvidia 首席执行官的最后几个月里，黄仁勋正在为撤回该公司支持人工智能经济的做法奠定基础。

现在，由于财务主管已经对被罢黜的主管伪造的一些交易持谨慎态度，一直指望英伟达支持的初创公司预计会出现更大的回调。

就在上个月，购买英伟达芯片并出租算力的新兴云公司的首席执行官齐聚柏林

与会人士表示，黄告诉他的合作伙伴，如果他们的公司想要分配 Nvidia 珍贵的 GPU，他们需要从客户那里获得预付款。这将使他们的项目更容易融资，并确保英伟达不是唯一一个提供财务支持的来源。

他说：“你没有收取应有的费用。”他告诉他们，埃隆·马斯克以比他们更好的价格向客户出租 Nvidia 芯片。 “我什至不需要你们。我可以把所有这些能力都给埃隆！埃隆想要它！”据两位听到这番言论的高管以及一位不久后听取简报的高管透露，他是这样说道的。

几周后，黄在被曝至少有过两起婚外情后辞职，其中一桩是与美国官员认为是中国情报人员的一名女性发生的，另一桩是与他的一名直接下属发生的。他的临时继任者、首席财务官科莱特·克雷斯(Colette Kress)有时会反对该公司的一些重大交易，并试图控制英伟达。

许多曾经依赖英伟达的公司现在都感到担忧了。

瑞银 (UBS) 分析师蒂姆·阿库里 (Tim Arcuri) 在最近的一份报告中估计，英伟达 (Nvidia) 融资撤回可能会导致市场损失 500 亿美元或更多美元，随着利率上升，企业将缺乏支持。

这家芯片巨头去年大部分时间都在大肆进行交易，为新兴公司提供财务支持，借出资产负债表来支持数据中心项目的债务融资，甚至充当自己芯片的最后客户。该公司同意从一些客户那里租用芯片，以向贷方表明这些公司手头有可靠的合同。

今年早些时候，英伟达表示正准备推出新的财务激励措施，并进行比以往更多的交易。

Alphabet 旗下的谷歌和 Advanced Micro Devices 等竞争对手正在向这些公司提供类似的激励措施，而黄仁勋不想失去市场份额。牵头的高管包括英伟达副总裁尼科·卡普雷斯 (Nico Caprez)，他也是黄仁勋的女婿。

英伟达在 7 月份宣布了融资计划，但到了 8 月份，黄仁勋和克雷斯对一些交易的投资回报提出了质疑。

当英伟达利用其信誉良好的资产负债表帮助 OpenAI 与软银旗下的 SB Energy 签署俄亥俄州皮克顿的大规模数据中心租赁协议时，英伟达在 8 月份的谈判中削减了承诺规模。克雷斯对这笔交易的规模产生了怀疑。

据《华尔街日报》此前报道，黄在 8 月份告诉他的财务团队，公司面临压力。他告诉他们，主要的云提供商正在计划使用替代芯片并减少对公司的依赖，而英伟达正面临着其承诺购买的芯片晶圆和内存过剩的问题。

时任首席执行官敦促员工制定一种方法来决定担保是否值得。据《华尔街日报》报道，当月晚些时候，该公司暂停了该计划中的一些交易。

据《华尔街日报》报道，英国 Neocloud Nscale 仍在与 Nvidia 和其他投资者进行谈判，为 Anthropic 位于西弗吉尼亚州的价值 450 亿美元的数据中心提供财务支持。

除了广泛的支持外，这家芯片制造商还对人工智能初创公司进行了一系列股权投资。根据 PitchBook 的数据，截至 11 月 10 日，英伟达今年总共参与了创纪录的 129 笔风险投资交易，占全球风险投资交易价值的 27%，高于 2023 年的 49 笔此类交易。

那些已经与英伟达达成交易的初创公司的首席执行官们松了一口气，因为他们的交易在黄仁勋下台之前就已经完成了。

据一位知情人士透露，Perplexity 首席执行官 Aravind Srinivas 表示，10 月 30 日，英伟达在该初创公司旧金山总部举行的每周全体会议上，与员工一起完成了对该公司 30 亿美元的投资。一天前，有消息传出，英伟达首席执行官被视为中国间谍阴谋的目标。

据知情人士透露，这家人工智能搜索公司目前正在筹集额外资金，在新投资之前，估值将达到 380 亿美元。

据知情人士透露，英伟达最近向估值 250 亿美元的开源模型开发商 Reflection AI 提出要约，以许可其技术并挖走其部分人才。黄曾公开赞扬该公司。知情人士称，在他离开之前尚未达成协议。

据知情人士透露，英伟达还敲定了对另一家开源模型提供商 Thinking Machines Lab 的巨额投资，该公司估值为 400 亿美元。据一位知情人士透露，Thinking Machines 有信心完成这笔交易。

英国《金融时报》和《信息报》早些时候报道了英伟达近期投资的一些细节。

Reflection and Thinking Machines 每个月都会燃烧大量资金来支付开发人工智能模型的计算能力，但尚未开发出一种产生大量收入的方法。

一些销售额很少甚至没有销售额的公司的创始人和风险资本支持者表示，如果英伟达确实从未来的股权投资中撤出，他们可能很难找到资金来维持急需现金的业务，更不用说确保利润丰厚的退出了。

title: Nvidia’s Days as an Open Checkbook for the AI Economy Are Numbered
title_en: Nvidia’s Days as an Open Checkbook for the AI Economy Are Numbered

inline_images.caption_en: Nvidia’s Days as an Open Checkbook for the AI Economy Are Numbered (Source: Wall Street Journal)

author: Robbie Whelan and Anissa Gardizy and Kate Clark
article_content:
In his final months as chief executive of Nvidia, Jensen Huang was laying the groundwork to pull back the company’s approach to backstopping the AI economy.

Now, with a finance chief at the helm who was already wary of some deals the ousted chief forged, the startups who had been counting on Nvidia’s support expect an even greater pullback.

Just last month, the CEOs of emerging cloud companies that buy Nvidia chips and rent out computing power gathered in Berlin

Huang told his partners that if their companies wanted allocations of Nvidia’s prized GPUs, they would need to secure upfront payments from customers, people in attendance said. That would make their projects easier to finance and ensure that Nvidia wasn’t alone in being a source of financial support.

“You’re not charging what you should be charging,” he said, telling them that Elon Musk was renting Nvidia chips to customers at better rates than they were. “I don’t even need you guys. I could just give all this capacity to Elon! Elon wants it!” he said, according to two executives who heard the remarks and one who was briefed on them shortly after.

Weeks later, Huang resigned after revelations that he had engaged in at least two affairs, including one with a woman U.S. officials believe is a Chinese intelligence asset and another with one of his direct reports. His interim successor, finance chief Colette Kress, has at times pushed back against some of the company’s big deals and sought to rein in Nvidia.

Many companies that had relied on Nvidia are now worried.

UBS analyst Tim Arcuri estimated in a recent note that an Nvidia financing pullback could take $50 billion or more out of the market, starving companies of support as interest rates rise.

The chip giant spent much of the past year on a dealmaking spree to provide financial backstops to emerging companies, lend its balance sheet to support debt financings of data-center projects, and even act as a customer of last resort for its own chips. The firm agreed to rent its chips from some customers to signal to lenders that those companies had solid contracts in-hand.

Earlier this year, Nvidia signaled it was preparing to roll out new financial incentives and do more deals than ever.

Rivals, such as Alphabet’s Google and Advanced Micro Devices, were offering these companies similar incentives, and Huang didn’t want to lose market share. Among the executives leading the charge was Nico Caprez, an Nvidia vice president who is also Huang’s son-in-law.

Nvidia announced its financing program in July, but by August, Huang and Kress questioned the return on investment from some deals.

When Nvidia used its creditworthy balance sheet to help OpenAI sign a massive data center lease in Piketon, Ohio, with SoftBank’s SB Energy, it cut the scale of its commitment in August during negotiations. Kress had become skeptical of the scale of the deal.

Huang told his finance team in August that the company was under pressure, The Wall Street Journal previously reported. Major cloud providers were making plans to use alternative chips and lessen their reliance on the firm, and Nvidia was staring at a glut of chip wafers and memory it had committed to buying, he told them.

The then-CEO pressed staff to develop a way to decide whether guarantees were worthwhile. Later that month, it paused some deals in that initiative, the Journal reported.

U.K.-based neocloud Nscale is still negotiating with Nvidia and other investors to provide financial backing for a $45-billion data center for Anthropic in West Virginia, the Journal reported.

In addition to its extensive backstopping, the chip maker also made a string of equity investments in AI startups. In total, Nvidia has participated in a record 129 venture-capital deals this year, as of Nov. 10, accounting for 27% of global VC deal value, according to PitchBook, up from a total of 49 such deals in 2023.

CEOs of startups that had closed deals with Nvidia breathed a sigh of relief that their deals made it through before Huang’s ouster.

Perplexity Chief Executive Aravind Srinivas shared that Nvidia closed a $3 billion investment in the company with his employees during a weekly all-hands at the startup’s San Francisco headquarters on Oct. 30, a person familiar with the meeting said. It was one day after news broke that the Nvidia CEO was seen as a target of a Chinese spy plot.

The AI search company is now raising additional capital at a higher valuation of $38 billion before the new investment, according to people familiar with the matter.

Nvidia recently made an offer to Reflection AI, an open-source model developer valued at $25 billion, to license its technology and hire away some of its talent, according to people familiar with the matter. Huang had publicly praised the company. An agreement hadn’t been reached before he left, the people said.

Nvidia has also been finalizing a massive investment in Thinking Machines Lab, another provider of open-source models, valuing the company at $40 billion, according to people familiar with the matter. Thinking Machines is confident the deal will be completed, according to a person familiar with the matter.

Some details of Nvidia’s recent investments were earlier reported by the Financial Times and The Information.

Reflection and Thinking Machines are burning huge amounts of capital each month to pay for the computing power to develop their AI models, but haven’t yet developed a way to generate substantial revenue.

Some founders and venture-capital backers of companies with little to no sales said that if Nvidia did pull back from future equity investments, they could struggle to find capital to keep their cash-hungry businesses going, let alone secure a lucrative exit.

content_snippet: Interim CEO Colette Kress is expected to rein in deals after a stretch in which Nvidia aggressively financed computing deals and startup investments
summary_en: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned amid espionage and misconduct scandals, with CFO Colette Kress appointed as interim CEO, triggering a reassessment of Nvidia's aggressive AI infrastructure financing. Nvidia has provided approximately $36 billion in off-balance-sheet credit support to 'neocloud' providers like CoreWeave and Nebius, and the new management is expected to pivot toward requiring upfront customer payments to mitigate credit risks.

ai_analysis.insight_zh: 英伟达过去通过资本链深度绑定云厂商的扩张策略本质上是“高杠杆加成下的硬件销售”，黄仁勋离职后的融资收缩将直接刺破AI基建领域的流动性泡沫。此举标志着AI产业从单纯的算力堆砌阶段转向财务自平衡考核，依赖英伟达直接信贷背书的二线算力集群将面临严峻的再融资压力与信用降级风险。
ai_analysis.insight_en: Nvidia’s strategy of binding cloud providers through capital support functioned as hardware sales supercharged by high leverage; Huang’s departure and the subsequent financing contraction will likely expose the liquidity bubble in AI infrastructure. This pivot signals a shift from raw compute expansion to financial sustainability, placing severe refinancing pressure and credit risk on second-tier providers reliant on Nvidia’s balance sheet.
ai_analysis.digest_zh: 英伟达创始人兼CEO黄仁勋因间谍与不当关系丑闻辞职，CFO柯蕾特·克雷斯出任代理CEO，引发市场对该公司深度参与AI基础设施信贷支持模式的深度重构。此前英伟达通过直接融资与背书，为CoreWeave、Nebius等“新云”厂商提供了约360亿美元的表外信贷背书，新管理层或将强制要求客户采取预付款模式以降低财务风险。
ai_analysis.digest_en: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned amid espionage and misconduct scandals, with CFO Colette Kress appointed as interim CEO, triggering a reassessment of Nvidia's aggressive AI infrastructure financing. Nvidia has provided approximately $36 billion in off-balance-sheet credit support to 'neocloud' providers like CoreWeave and Nebius, and the new management is expected to pivot toward requiring upfront customer payments to mitigate credit risks.

title: Mount Thor raises $45 million to build Mac data centers for AI agents
title_en: Mount Thor raises $45 million to build Mac data centers for AI agents
author: Bradley C
article_content:
Mount Thor, a Bay Area startup building cloud infrastructure on Apple silicon, announced today that it has raised $45 million across Seed and Series A rounds. The pitch to its investors was simple: AI agents are incredible on Apple silicon, and nobody is renting them at data-center scale.

CRV and Conviction co-led the Series A. Chad Byers and Offline Ventures co-led the Seed. CSC Leasing, Enea Capital, Long Journey Ventures, and Upper90 participated, along with angel investors from OpenAI, Meta, Cognition, Together AI, and Vercel. The company also raised separate non-dilutive financing for new hardware as well.

Mount Thor runs macOS on Apple silicon as elastic compute instances, just as a cloud provider rents Linux VMs. Customers get on-demand fleets of Macs for work that only happens on macOS: training computer-use models in reinforcement learning environments, running secure macOS sandboxes for agents, long-running instances that let an agent work across a user’s devices under one Apple ID, and build and test farms for Apple software.

There are two ways to use its solution. With managed compute, customers pick a machine class and image, and get either a full bare-metal Mac or an isolated macOS VM with administrator access, provisioned through a web portal, a command-line tool, Kubernetes, or the API, and billed per Mac on a 24-hour basis. With customer-managed compute, an organization runs its own Macs at a Mount Thor site using its own MDM, while Mount Thor operates the facility and provides inventory by serial number, problem reporting, and event notifications.

The argument is that agents are becoming macOS users, and the demand for Apple’s platform now scales with the number of agents rather than the number of people.

“Making Apple’s operating system and silicon available at datacenter-scale is a massive untapped opportunity in AI infrastructure,” said Peter Voell, Founder and CEO of Mount Thor. “Decades of investment in accessibility and human-computer interaction make macOS the best place for agents to work and for humans to hold them accountable. And with chips like the M5 Ultra, Apple silicon is becoming a high performance, more power- and cost- efficient platform for production inference.”

The other half of its pitch is inference. The M5 Ultra Mac Studio shipped in August with up to 512GB of unified memory, which puts large open-weight models within reach of a single machine at a fraction of the power draw of a traditional GPU-based server. Mount Thor says a focus of the new funding is building what it calls the best inference lab for open-source models on Apple silicon.

“Mount Thor sits at the intersection of two important shifts: the rapidly expanding capabilities of autonomous agents and the increasing demand for compute that can support both local and cloud workloads,” said Brittany Walker, General Partner at CRV. “We’re thrilled to back Peter and the team as they make it easier to use Apple’s platforms at scale for agentic AI.”

The team comes from Cerebras, CoreWeave, Fluidstack, Nebius, OpenAI, and xAI. The company was founded this year and deployed its first data center in under six months.

### Wrap up

Macs in the cloud are not new as AWS has rented Mac instances for a few years, and MacStadium has been doing so longer than AWS. Mount Thor’s pitch is that the larger customer is an AI agent that needs a Mac to do its job, and that demand grows with the number of agents rather than the number of developers.

The company says the funding will go toward expanding its compute footprint and building out the team, and that it plans to add capacity quickly to keep up with customer demand.

article_content_zh:
Mount Thor 是一家在 Apple 芯片上构建云基础设施的湾区初创公司，今天宣布已通过种子轮和 A 轮融资筹集 4500 万美元。向投资者推销的内容很简单：苹果芯片上的人工智能代理令人难以置信，而且没有人在数据中心规模上租用它们。

CRV 和 Conviction 共同领投了 A 轮融资。Chad Byers 和 Offline Ventures 共同领投了种子轮融资。 CSC Leasing、Enea Capital、Long Journey Ventures 和 Upper90 参与其中，还有来自 OpenAI、Meta、Cognition、Together AI 和 Vercel 的天使投资者。该公司还为新硬件筹集了单独的非稀释性融资。

Mount Thor 在 Apple 芯片上运行 macOS 作为弹性计算实例，就像云提供商租用 Linux 虚拟机一样。客户可以按需获得一组 Mac 来完成仅在 macOS 上进行的工作：在强化学习环境中训练计算机使用模型、为代理运行安全的 macOS 沙箱、让代理在一个 Apple ID 下跨用户设备工作的长期运行实例，以及为 Apple 软件构建和测试场。

有两种方法可以使用其解决方案。通过托管计算，客户可以选择机器类别和映像，并获得完整的裸机 Mac 或具有管理员访问权限的独立 macOS 虚拟机，通过 Web 门户、命令行工具、Kubernetes 或 API 进行配置，并按 24 小时按 Mac 计费。通过客户管理的计算，组织可以使用自己的 MDM 在 Mount Thor 站点运行自己的 Mac，而 Mount Thor 则运营该设施并按序列号提供库存、问题报告和事件通知。

争论的焦点是，客服人员正在成为 macOS 用户，而对苹果平台的需求现在随着客服人员的数量而不是人数的增加而增加。

Mount Thor 创始人兼首席执行官 Peter Voell 表示：“在数据中心规模上提供苹果操作系统和芯片是人工智能基础设施领域一个尚未开发的巨大机遇。” “数十年在可访问性和人机交互方面的投资使 macOS 成为智能体工作和人类追究其责任的最佳场所。借助 M5 Ultra 等芯片，Apple 芯片正在成为一个高性能、更省电且更具成本效益的生产推理平台。”

它的另一半内容是推理。 M5 Ultra Mac Studio 于 8 月份发货，配备高达 512GB 的统一内存，这使得大型开放式重量模型可以在单台机器上运行，而功耗只是传统的基于 GPU 的服务器的一小部分。 Mount Thor 表示，新资金的重点是在苹果芯片上建立所谓的最佳开源模型推理实验室。

CRV 普通合伙人 Brittany Walker 表示：“Mount Thor 处于两个重要转变的交汇点：自主代理功能的快速扩展以及对支持本地和云工作负载的计算需求的不断增长。” “我们很高兴能够支持 Peter 和他的团队，因为他们让大规模使用 Apple 平台实现代理 AI 变得更加容易。”

该团队来自 Cerebras、CoreWeave、Fluidstack、Nebius、OpenAI 和 xAI。该公司成立于今年，并在不到六个月的时间内部署了第一个数据中心。

云中的 Mac 并不新鲜，因为 AWS 租用 Mac 实例已经有几年了，而且 MacStadium 这样做的时间比 AWS 还要长。 Mount Thor 的主张是，更大的客户是需要 Mac 来完成工作的 AI 代理，并且这种需求随着代理数量而不是开发人员数量的增长而增长。

该公司表示，这笔资金将用于扩大其计算范围和建设团队，并计划快速增加容量以满足客户需求。
